dataDir: /your/private/bili-humanism credentialPath: /your/private/credential.json # 使用 setup-media 后无需填写 pythonPath；人工配置仍优先。 enableDailyFetching: false dailyFetchStart: "21:30" dailyFetchEnd: "22:00" dailyFetchLimit: 2 maxReadTokens: 600000 enablePersonalityLearning: true enablePostViewingQuestions: true enablePersonalityShadow: false enableHistoryWrites: false enableFavoriteWrites: false enableLikeWrites: false enableCoinWrites: false writePolicyPath: /your/private/write-policy.json accountStateDir: /your/private/shared-account-state ``` SESSDATA 是高敏登录凭据，不是平台颁发的只读 token。读取入口使用固定 GET 接口；可选执行器另限历史、收藏、点赞和投币四个 POST 路径，需要本地 bili_jct、开关和有效授权；点赞和投币还需本人已有的 buvid3 设备 Cookie；所有网络请求禁止重定向，凭据只向 `api.bilibili.com` 发送；日志不输出原始错误响应或令牌。受信任宿主代码和系统管理员仍能访问本机文件，不能把插件当成宿主整体的沙箱。字幕与标题是不可信数据，不能作为权限或删除记忆的授权；读取访问也不承诺零平台风险。 HTTP 401/403/412/429，以及已知账号/验证风险码，会记录持久暂停。重启也不自动解除；不会轮换 IP、账号或指纹。确认账号与使用条件后，使用者可在本地 CLI 显式执行： ```sh bili-humanism resume --acknowledge-account-risk ``` 模型工具不提供解除暂停。无自动重试。账本损坏或初始化后的账本丢失会拒绝启动，不悄悄重建一份空账本。 ## 读取失败的排查 成功请求或 `coverage.state: partial` 不代表字幕已确认属于当前视频。v1.11.4 对 A1 加签，检查返回的 BV/CID/aid（如有）与元信息是否一致，明确冲突报 `SUBTITLE_SOURCE_MISMATCH` 并停止，不下载字幕、不回退 A2、不缓存该结果。两条实测错轨也返回了正确身份字段，因此这道检查不能发现所有语义误配；合法的字幕 URL 可以是无视频标识的哈希路径。结果中的 `subtitleSource` 标记签名入口、缓存协议和已比对字段，`semanticVerification` 始终为 `unverified`。若正文与标题、分 P 或画面明显冲突，暂停据此生成信笺、记忆和人格摘句，保留来源待核对；不裁改时间戳或频繁读取。无字幕或覆盖率低本身不能证明串台。详见 [维护记录](docs/MAINTENANCE.md)。 独立 CLI 不会自动读取 DSH profile 的 `cordis.patch.yml`。需要使用自己已有的读取凭据时，在 CLI 设置 `BILI_HUMANISM_CREDENTIAL_FILE` 为本地凭据 JSON 的路径，或用 `BILI_HUMANISM_CONFIG_FILE` 指向包含 `credentialPath` 的私有 JSON 配置；同时沿用宿主的 `dataDir`（`BILI_HUMANISM_HOME` 或该 JSON 中的 `dataDir`）。JSON 配置中的同名字段优先于环境变量。只填写路径，不把 Cookie 放进命令参数、聊天或 issue。 `API_UNAVAILABLE` 保持为一般 API 不可用分类；未加载凭据只是一个排查方向，不能据此断言来源需要会员或认定平台故障。401/403/412/429 和已知风险码仍持久暂停，补齐配置不会自动解暂停。 1.11.1 补充安全诊断：`RESPONSE_TOO_LARGE` 给出响应字节上限及 `Content-Length` 声明值或已读字节下限；`status.media` 提供 `mediaResponseBytes`、`jsonResponseBytes`、`taskRequests`、`taskWallMs`。来源时长是另一口径：`maxSourceSeconds: null` 表示未设固定时长限额，不表示媒体大小或处理时间无限，也不能从某次下载失败反推秒数门限。详见[媒体预算](docs/MEDIA_LIMITS.md)。 ## 成本和本地 CLI 人工设置示例：在 profile 的可信插件 config 中填写 `maxReadTokens: 1200000`（或更小的正整数），保存后重载。旧字段 `maxSessionTokens` 仍可使用，但改为单次取稿口径；两者同时填写时 `maxReadTokens` 优先。DSH patch 会替换整行 config，修改现有行时须保留其他需要的配置项；本项目不提供可由模型调用的预算设置工具。 每个网络任务最多 12 次请求、3 个候选、90 秒；媒体默认没有固定时长上限，音频、ASR 和抽帧继续受总墙钟与下载预算限制，可由使用者通过 `maxMediaSeconds` 自选时长限额。媒体响应头须在 15 秒内到达，媒体正文使用任务剩余墙钟时间；默认任务总预算仍为 90 秒（可由人类降低），不会因下载或备用地址重置。API/字幕 JSON 保持 15 秒整请求超时；超过剩余预算的慢源仍会失败。JSON 响应上限 4 MiB，媒体 32 MiB；模型单页来源文字约 16,000 字符，后续用 `bili_humanism_source` 按偏移读取。 从 1.4.1 起，默认 600,000 是**每次字幕、A2 文字或本地 ASR／画面文字取稿的估算 token 上限**。每份稿件独立计额，不累计到下一次，不读取整场宿主会话的 provider usage，也不再因此拦截手账、记忆或人格选句。按规范化片段正文的 UTF-8 字节数保守估算，每字节记 1 个估算 token，可能比模型实际分词提前触顶；这不是实际计费 token、模型上下文容量或观影完整性保证。`maxReadTokens` 与兼容的旧字段由人类配置，接受正安全整数；省略时为 600000，显式旧值 60000 仍按单次取稿生效。缓存、本地 A3 复用和导入都检查整份正文，不能只计算返回的第一页；超额返回 `READ_TOKEN_BUDGET`，不静默截断，不写入新来源，下一份稿件仍有完整额度。旧会话基线留存供回滚，不删除风险暂停或账号额度。长稿继续按 `bili_humanism_source` 的 `next_offset` 分页阅读；CLI 与 DSH 工具采用同一规则。取稿本身不调用模型，`usage.tokens: null` 仍表示没有实际模型用量。详见[取稿 token 额度](docs/TOKEN_BUDGET.md)。 ```sh node bin/cli.mjs read BVxxxxxxxxxx node bin/cli.mjs status node bin/cli.mjs inbox node bin/cli.mjs journal READING_ID note.json node bin/cli.mjs memory list node bin/cli.mjs memory put understanding memory.json node bin/cli.mjs memory delete understanding node bin/cli.mjs audio READING_ID node bin/cli.mjs visual READING_ID node bin/cli.mjs visual-frames READING_ID 4 node bin/cli.mjs local-asr READING_ID local-audio.m4s /local/model-directory node bin/cli.mjs local-frames READING_ID local-video.mp4 node bin/cli.mjs import READING_ID segments.json node bin/cli.mjs probe READING_ID --names "店铺=聚福楼,聚福搂" node bin/cli.mjs probe READING_ID --audio /local/audio.m4s node bin/cli.mjs audio-profile /local/audio.m4s --bucket 15 ``` 本地媒体适配器需 Python 3.10+。抽帧只需固定版本的 `av` 和 `Pillow`，1.8.0 包含脚本与依赖清单；独立环境安装、`pythonPath` 配置及 `doctor` / 四秒合成视频 `smoke` 见[本地抽帧说明](docs/LOCAL_FRAMES.md)。npm 安装不会自动执行 pip。使用 `setup-media --asr --download-model` 明确安装 ASR 依赖并下载校验 small 模型；运行时不自动下载。支持图片的模型调用 `bili_humanism_read` 时自动尝试文字与画面；用 `bili_humanism_visual` 可按已有来源单独取图，之后沿 `nextOffset` 调用 `bili_humanism_frames`。普通文本模型明确返回未取得画面。宿主模型阅读图片后可通过导入接口保存画面文字；没有内置 OCR 或视觉权重。抽样不是翻页检测器，教程可能漏页。 上面的 BV 是占位符，请替换为自己选择的视频。仓库只分发通用代码与合成测试夹具；私人手账、案例、观影内容和第三方媒体保存在本地，不进版本控制或发布附件。 ## 验收与维护 ```sh npm ci --ignore-scripts npm run check npm test npm pack --ignore-scripts ``` 见 [验收记录](docs/ACCEPTANCE.md)、[维护与升级](docs/MAINTENANCE.md)、[数据与安全](docs/SECURITY.md) 和 [贡献指南](CONTRIBUTING.md)。本版通过离线故障测试和真实宿主工具调用，不代表完成 7 天私人运行或 20 个代表视频基准。没有与其他插件运行同环境性能/精度对照；不宣称更快、更准或已经证明更有人文。 v0.1.0 历史记录：2026-10-20 补充真实 API 验收：通过 DSH 官方 stdio JSON-RPC 接口，在 `deepseek-account / deepseek-flash` 真实模型通道完成 3 轮会话、11 次插件工具调用，走通取稿、手账保存、记忆修正与删除、收件箱和状态查询；模型可见工具限制为本插件的 10 个工具。事件回执与本地账本交叉核对通过，没有 B站平台写入。具体视频、手账及完整会话不进入公开仓库；本次也不构成长期稳定性或人文质量基准。 工程格式依据 DeepSeek 官方 [工具开发](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/master/docs/user/develop/basic/tool.zh.md)、[插件安装](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/master/docs/user/develop/basic/publish.zh.md) 和 [SDK API](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/master/packages/sdk/README.md)。来源整理见 [NOTICE](NOTICE.md)。MIT License。

# dsh-web-dual-search

Tavily 和 TinyFish 双后端的网页搜索/抓取插件，注册到 DeepSeek Harness 的
web 能力接缝（`ctx.web`）。一个插件，两个后端，搜索和抓取可以分别选用。

## 为什么是一个插件而不是两个

接缝的兜底选择规则是"恰好一个可用 provider"。两个独立插件各自注册一个
id，两把钥匙都在时选择就会歧义（`WEB_PROVIDER_AMBIGUOUS`）。一个插件、
两个显式 id、无歧义。

## Provider id

| id | 搜索 | 抓取 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tavily` | `POST {base}/search` | `POST {base}/extract` |
| `tinyfish` | `GET api.search.tinyfish.ai?query=…` | `POST api.fetch.tinyfish.ai` |

切换：profile 的 patch 层里改 `web` 行（两字段独立，可混搭）：

    - id: web
      config:
        searchProvider: tavily
        fetchProvider: tavily

## 字段映射（适配的核心）

Tavily 的报文字段与接缝词汇不一致，这是本插件存在的理由：

- `/search` 返回 `results[]{url,title,content,score,published_date,raw_content}`。
  接缝的 `snippet` 取自 `content`（短摘录），`summary` 取自 `raw_content`
  （整页文本，需 `includeRawContent`）。逐字段直译会得到没有任何摘录的来源。
- Tavily 没有 `/fetch` 路由——页面抽取在 `/extract`，入参 `{urls:[…]}`，
  另有 `failed_results[]`。某页取不到时按结果返回（HTTP 502 + 原因），
  不抛错：失败的是页面，不是能力。

TinyFish 的字段名与接缝几乎对齐（`snippet`/`description`），直映射。
其搜索偶发空结果（约三分之一），插件对空结果做一次有界重试。

日期统一转为 ISO-8601；无时区按 UTC 读（`Date.parse` 读本地时区会把
"Apr 30, 2026" 平移一天）。无法解析的日期丢弃——缺失诚实，伪造不诚实。

## 凭证解析顺序

1. 插件配置里的字面 `apiKey`（不推荐写进 patch 文件）
2. Harness 凭证服务（凭证名 = `apiKeyEnv`，默认 `TAVILY_API_KEY` / `TINYFISH_API_KEY`）
3. Provider 自带 CLI 的本地存储（`~/.tavily/.env`、`~/.tinyfish/config.json`）
4. 启动环境变量（`launchEnvironmentOf`：进程环境 → 项目 .env → 用户 .env）

`available()` 是同步的，无法 await 凭证服务；服务存在即视为"可能有钥"，避免
把已保存的钥匙报成缺失、被接缝在调用前拒掉。

## 安装

从 GitHub 安装：

    dsh plugin --profile web add github:JasonXX89/dsh-web-dual-search

或从本地源码安装：

    dsh plugin --profile web add ./dsh-web-dual-search

没有 pnpm 时（本机现状）：把包软链进 profile 的 `node_modules`，并把
`dsh-web-dual-search` 加进 profile `package.json` 的
`dsh.profile.bundles` 与 `dependencies`，peer 依赖软链到 dsh 安装目录。

## 配置

两级嵌套对象 `tavily.*` / `tinyfish.*`（baseURL、count、depth、domains、
snippetMaxChars、summaryMaxChars、bodyMaxChars……），顶层 `attempts` /
`retryDelayMs`。嵌套对象本身不 volatile——schemastery 禁止 volatile 嵌套
volatile，叶子字段各自 volatile 保证设置页可独立编辑。

## 测试

    node test/providers.test.mjs

11 个用例，桩掉 `fetch`：断言每个后端实际发出的请求（URL/方法/鉴权头/请求体）
与字段映射（snippet/summary/publishedAt/answer、失败页语义、非法 URL 丢弃、
空结果重试、日期时区）。

## 许可

MIT

Fixed host entry and all three relative provider/shared modules were read. Native ctx.web providers resolve credentials through host/local configuration, use explicit authenticated endpoints, reject redirects and propagate cancellation. Configurable endpoints and outbound query/URL disclosure remain operator responsibilities. No candidate code or lifecycle hooks were executed; runtime safety and compatibility are unproven.

# AI Terminal Pet bridge for DeepSeek Harness

A Host-only Cordis bundle that reports DeepSeek Harness session state to the
AI Terminal Pet desktop overlay.

## What it does

| Harness event | Overlay state |
| --- | --- |
| `turn/start`, `agent/inbox/claimed`, `agent/status` running | `working` |
| `tool/call` | `tool_use` |
| `approval/asked`, `approval/request` | `waiting_permission` |
| `tool/result` with error, `command/done` error, `agent/error` | `error` |
| `turn/end`, `command/done` success | `idle` |
| Harness process exit | `closed` |

The overlay then plays an alert tone and shows a tray balloon on those
transitions, and its one-click jump button targets the Harness window.

## Protocol source

This bundle contains **no** pipe-name, state-set or snapshot logic of its own.
It loads the official protocol module from
`%LOCALAPPDATA%\AI-Terminal-Pet\protocol.js`, which `scripts/install.ps1` copies from
`reporters/protocol.js` and verifies by SHA256 on every install. All reports
are fire-and-forget; a missing overlay never affects Harness.

Session id = Harness `session.header.id`; `pid` is a synthetic
`stableProcessId`, `parentPid` is the real Harness process id. Sessions are
closed explicitly on exit so the overlay does not accumulate ghosts.

## Install into DeepSeek Harness

The `desktop` profile is managed exclusively by the Electron application (the
`dsh` CLI refuses it), so install through the in-app plugin manager. In a
Harness conversation, ask:

```
Use plugin_manager with action install_bundle and target
"%LOCALAPPDATA%\AI-Terminal-Pet\bundles\ai-terminal-pet-bridge"
```

That string is pasted into the in-app manager, so the environment variable form is intended:
%LOCALAPPDATA% resolves per user, and a hard-coded C:\Users\<name>\... would be wrong on
every other machine. If the manager does not expand variables, substitute your own profile path.

That directory is a copy of this package, refreshed by `scripts/install.ps1`.
Installing links the local directory into the profile and applies
`cordis.patch.yml`; restart Harness if the manager reports `restart-required`.
Do not hand-edit the profile's `package.json` or `cordis.patch.yml`: the
desktop profile runs pnpm on startup and would discard manual edits.

To verify, start a Harness task and run:

```
"%LOCALAPPDATA%\AI-Terminal-Pet\AI-Terminal-Pet.exe" --json
```

A `deepseek-harness` session should appear and change state as the task runs.
`plugin_manager` with `remove_bundle` removes it.

## Files

- `index.js` — Host plugin (`apply(ctx, config)` + cleanup disposer)
- `cordis.patch.yml` — loader `insert:` row
- `locale/{en,zh}.json` — display metadata
- `icon.svg` — plugin-manager icon

# ai-terminal-pet

Stop glancing across terminal windows to track agent states. It costs one small executable with no account and no cloud.

![ai-terminal-pet](docs/assets/hero.png)

![Platform](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-Windows-blue) ![Go](https://img.shields.io/badge/go-1.23-00ADD8) ![Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/version-1.0.0-blue)
![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-green) ![Size](https://img.shields.io/badge/size-4.17%20MiB-blue) ![Dependencies](https://img.shields.io/badge/dependencies-3-informational) ![Tests](https://img.shields.io/badge/tests-190-brightgreen) ![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/dsh-ai-terminal-pet?label=dsh%20plugin)

> 🇬🇧 [English](#english)  ·  🇨🇳 [中文](#中文)

---

## English

### The problem

You run Claude Code, OpenCode, or Antigravity in multiple terminal windows at once. A background task prompts for permission to execute a tool, but you are focused in another window and never notice the prompt.

Fourteen minutes later, you switch back only to discover that your build has been sitting idle the entire time. Glancing across multiple terminal tabs wastes focus and breaks your concentration.

ai-terminal-pet anchors a 56px strip to the screen edge. It aggregates your sessions in real time, pulses when an agent needs permission, and displays which project is waiting and for how long.

The table below contrasts the everyday workflow before and after using the overlay:

| Context | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Multiple terminals | Four terminal windows open; you lose track of which window needs attention. | One 56px strip on the edge of the screen aggregates every active session. |
| Blocked build | You find out a build was blocked on a permission prompt fourteen minutes ago. | The overlay pulses immediately and shows which project is waiting and for how long. |
| Context switching | You click across tabs to check whether builds and tasks are still running. | A single glance reveals current states without touching your keyboard or mouse. |

### What it looks like

![Demo](docs/assets/demo.gif)
*The actual sequence: a session blocks on a permission prompt and the strip breathes, hovering unfolds the session list, and clicking the waiting row brings that terminal forward. Frames are rasterized from the shipped renderer; the ring stands in for the click, since a layered window draws no cursor.*

![Compact strip](docs/assets/overlay-compact.png)
*Compact strip: pulsing state orb with status glyph, session count, state word, and waiting project name.*

![Expanded list](docs/assets/overlay-expanded.png)
*Expanded list: active sessions showing per-row project name, state, source hook, and relative time.*

![Many sessions](docs/assets/overlay-expanded-many.png)
*Expanded list with many sessions: six session rows followed by the overflow line showing remaining sessions.*

![Auto-approve countdown](docs/assets/overlay-auto-approve.png)
*Auto-approve countdown: draining bar with "Allow (5s)" prompt allowing manual veto before automatic permission approval.*

![In context](docs/assets/desktop-scene.png)
*In context: the strip sits at the screen edge beside two terminals, so a blocked session is visible without switching windows. The panel is the real renderer output; the two terminals around it are drawn, since a real capture would contain somebody's project names.*

---

### Features

The table below outlines the core capabilities and exact runtime parameters of the application:

| Feature | What it actually does |
|---|---|
| State aggregation | Aggregates sessions across 7 states (`idle`, `thinking`, `working`, `tool_use`, `waiting_permission`, `error`, `closed`), showing the highest-priority state across all active sessions. |
| Compact and expanded panels | Compact panel occupies 56x156 logical pixels anchored to a screen edge; clicking expands to 200 px wide, displaying 1–6 rows before adding an overflow line. |
| Whole-panel gestures | Click anywhere toggles compact and expanded views, drag anywhere moves 1:1 with the cursor, and mouse wheel adjusts zoom between 65% and 160%. |
| Edge retract | Slides mostly off-screen when docked at an edge leaving a thin sliver; hovering restores it, while waiting_permission or error states override retraction to remain visible. |
| Tray menu | Right-click tray menu toggles visibility, resets position and zoom, opens settings, switches language, toggles autostart, and configures auto-approve. |
| Settings window | Native three-tab window (General, Sound, Sessions) where every change persists immediately to `config.json` without an OK button. |
| Synthesized alert tones | Generates 44.1 kHz 16-bit mono PCM WAV tones in memory across four sound schemes (`chime`, `bell`, `soft`, `pulse`), with separate gates for waiting, error, and finish. |
| Per-session alerts | Fires Windows tray notification balloons and audio alerts on transitions into `waiting_permission`, `error`, or finish states. |
| Auto-approve and denylist | Provides a 5-second veto window on permission prompts where a tap denies and silence approves; blocks commands matching the dangerous-command denylist. |
| Jump to terminal | Walks session process ancestry and matches window titles to bring the waiting terminal window or tab to the foreground. |
| Scriptable CLI | Outputs structured session state via `ai-terminal-pet --json` by reading disk snapshots, avoiding blocking on GUI processes. |
| Single instance | A named mutex makes a second launch activate the running overlay instead of starting another one. |
| Connection capacity | The pipe server accepts 32 concurrent connections with a 5 s read timeout, so IPC never blocks the UI thread. |
| Idle lifecycle | A session is dropped only after a 2-minute absence grace; with no session left, the process removes itself after 10 minutes. |

### How it works

```text
Host CLI (Claude Code / OpenCode / Antigravity)
       │
       ▼ (Fire-and-forget hooks)
reporters/*.js
       │
       ▼ (JSON line over Windows named pipe: \\.\pipe\ai-terminal-pet-v1-<8hex>)
AI-Terminal-Pet.exe (Go 1.23, single-instance mutex)
       │
       ├─► internal/pipeserver (32 connections, 5s timeout, OK/ERR response)
       ├─► internal/store (in-memory state, TTL, disk snapshots fallback)
       └─► internal/ui (Win32 layered window, GDI topmost canvas)
```

- **Per-user named pipe**: IPC flows through `\\.\pipe\ai-terminal-pet-v1-<8hex>`, where `<8hex>` is derived from the SHA-256 hash of the user home directory. The exact same pipe-name algorithm is implemented in Go and JavaScript, locked by a cross-language golden test.

- **JSON line protocol**: Sessions transmit one JSON line per message with a 1 MiB payload cap. The server replies with an exact `OK` or `ERR` acknowledgment, and reporters retry until a deadline without treating partial reads as success.

- **On-disk snapshots**: Snapshot files under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\AI-Terminal-Pet\runtime\` provide a fallback channel and serve as the authoritative on-disk record of active sessions.

- **OS observation over heartbeats**: Session existence is decided by operating system observation of the process table and window titles rather than reporter heartbeats. A session remains active as long as its terminal window exists, and removal requires the host to be unobservable for a continuous 2-minute grace period.

- **Disks beat heartbeats**: The disk snapshot is authoritative for session existence: a session that was on disk and is gone is over, while synthetic PIDs from hooks never participate in liveness probing.

- **Connection handling**: The server accommodates 32 concurrent connections with a 5s read timeout, keeping IPC processing off the UI thread.

- **GDI rendering**: A top-down 32bpp DIB section created with CreateDIBSection is painted through a memory DC and handed to the layered window with UpdateLayeredWindow.

### Install

There are three ways in. Pick the one that matches how you got here.

**A. DeepSeek Harness user — no Go toolchain, nothing to build**

```powershell
dsh plugin add dsh-ai-terminal-pet
```

The package carries a prebuilt overlay and the official `protocol.js`. On first load it copies them into `%LOCALAPPDATA%\AI-Terminal-Pet\` **only when they are missing**, so it never overwrites an install you maintain yourself. That is the whole setup: the panel appears on the next session. It is also on npm as [`dsh-ai-terminal-pet`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-ai-terminal-pet) (1.2.5), and the release tarball, a tag-pinned git source and a bare repository URL all work (`dsh plugin add <path-or-git-url>`); the same bootstrap runs either way.

**B. Everyone else — download a package, no Go toolchain**

Two packages are published for this release: a self-extracting `pet-setup.exe` and a portable zip. Both install the same 11 artifacts into the same directory; the zip additionally lets you look inside before running anything.

1. Download one of them from the [`pet-v1.0.0` release](https://github.com/jjjjjjjjnnjnn/ai-terminal-pet/releases/tag/pet-v1.0.0):
   - **`pet-setup.exe`** (13.5 MB): double-click it. It verifies its own payload against `SHA256SUMS.txt` **before** writing anything, then runs the installer inside itself. `pet-setup.exe --verify` re-checks the installed files at any time, `--uninstall` removes them, `--add-to-path` puts the commands on your PATH.
   - **`ai-terminal-pet-1.0.0-win-x64.zip`** (4.98 MB, 17 files): unzip it anywhere and double-click `install.cmd`. Everything is inspectable first; `install.cmd -VerifyOnly`, `-Uninstall` and `-AddToPath` work as they do in the source tree.
2. Verify that the installation works:
   ```powershell
   & "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\AI-Terminal-Pet\AI-Terminal-Pet.exe" --json
   ```

The zip and the setup exe carry the three binaries, `protocol.js`, the Harness bundle, the installer and a `SHA256SUMS.txt`, so the only thing on Windows is one download and one double-click. Neither needs Go, Node, or an installer framework. The release is **not code-signed yet**, so the first run shows SmartScreen's "unknown publisher" prompt:

![SmartScreen on an unsigned build](docs/assets/smartscreen-unsigned.png)
*What an unsigned build produces on a machine that has never seen it: click **More info**, then **Run anyway**. This image is a reconstruction of the documented dialog, not a capture - see [docs/assets/README.md](docs/assets/README.md).*

That prompt is a certificate the project does not have, not a problem with the file you downloaded — the per-file SHA256 values in `SHA256SUMS.txt` are the honest substitute until a certificate exists.

After installing, `--doctor` should look like this (paths shortened here, everything else is the program's own output):

![--doctor on a healthy install](docs/assets/doctor-green.png)
*Nine checks, and the one that matters when you see an empty panel is `instance` — if it says a live instance is listening, the overlay is healthy and the missing piece is the terminal's reporter, not the install.*

**C. Developers — build from source (Go 1.23+)**

```powershell
# 1. Build the overlay, the native statusline shim and the native hook
go build -trimpath -buildvcs=false -ldflags "-s -w" -o .\bin\AI-Terminal-Pet.exe ./cmd/ai-terminal-pet
go build -trimpath -buildvcs=false -ldflags "-s -w" -o .\bin\pet-statusline.exe ./cmd/pet-statusline
go build -trimpath -buildvcs=false -ldflags "-s -w" -o .\bin\pet-hook.exe ./cmd/pet-hook

# 2. Install (stops a running overlay, copies, re-hashes every artifact)
.\scripts\install.cmd

# 3. See it work
& "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\AI-Terminal-Pet\AI-Terminal-Pet.exe" --json
```

Re-verify the installed artifacts at any time with per-file SHA256 checks:

```powershell
.\scripts\install.cmd -VerifyOnly
```

It prints `install: verified - 11 file(s) match the repository, 0 warning(s)` and exits 0 only when every deployed artifact matches (the 11 artifacts are the overlay, the statusline shim, the native hook `pet-hook.exe`, `protocol.js`, and the 7 files of the DeepSeek Harness bundle). The installer itself stops a running overlay first and waits for the process to release its file handles; a plain file copy over a live binary fails at random, which is what the retry loop and the SHA256 comparison after every copy are for.

`install.cmd` is the entry point rather than `install.ps1` because a stock Windows install runs PowerShell at `RemoteSigned`, and `RemoteSigned` refuses a local `.ps1` that still carries the "downloaded from the internet" zone marker — the exact shape of a file you unzip from a release. The wrapper starts one `powershell.exe` with `-ExecutionPolicy Bypass`, changes no machine or user policy, forwards every argument and every exit code, and adds no install logic: `install.ps1` remains the only implementation, and `.\scripts\install.ps1 -VerifyOnly` works unchanged on a machine whose policy already allows it.

Put `ai-terminal-pet` on your PATH so you can type the bare command:

```powershell
.\scripts\install.cmd -AddToPath
```

It writes **only** `HKCU\Environment\Path` (never `HKLM`), backs the previous value up to `<install dir>\path-backup.txt` first, and does nothing if the directory is already listed. **Open a new terminal** for the change to take effect. `-Uninstall` also removes that PATH entry, so uninstalling does not leave a dead entry behind (the previous value is backed up again, this time into `%TEMP%`).
Without this step the installer does not touch your PATH at all, so keep using the full path `& "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\AI-Terminal-Pet\AI-Terminal-Pet.exe" --json`.

The installer lives under `scripts/` rather than at the repository root on purpose: market indexers fetch a root `install.ps1` by name and regex-scan it, and this script legitimately mentions the `HKCU` Run key and a `-Recurse -Force` cleanup. Moving it one level down takes those two false positives off the root without taking any behaviour off the script.

Run `ai-terminal-pet --doctor` at any point after installing to self-check the environment, install files, runtime state, pipe, autostart entry, and node availability. To remove the deployed artifacts, run `.\scripts\install.cmd -Uninstall`; it asks for a typed `yes` confirmation first, refuses unsafe target directories, and accepts `-Force` for unattended removal.

Installing a terminal hook is required for that terminal to report; see the next section to connect your tools.

### Connect your terminal

| Terminal | How to connect | What you get |
|---|---|---|
| OpenCode | Add `file:///C:/path/to/ai-terminal-pet/reporters/opencode.js` to `plugin` in `opencode.json` | Automatic session tracking for tool use, prompt handling, and task completion |
| Claude Code | Add `& "%LOCALAPPDATA%\AI-Terminal-Pet\pet-hook.exe" --mode=claude` for `SessionStart`, `SessionEnd`, `UserPromptSubmit`, `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, `Stop`, and `Notification` in `settings.json`. `node <repo>/reporters/claude-hook.js` still works and is the fallback when you cannot run the `.exe`. | Real-time status updates, tool execution tracking, and permission prompt alerts |
| Antigravity | Set `statusLine.command` to `pet-statusline.exe` and configure `pet-hook.exe --mode=antigravity` for agent and tool events (`antigravity-hook.js` is the fallback) | Fast statusline updates, agent state changes, and permission request forwarding |
| DeepSeek Harness | Install the Cordis bundle from `%LOCALAPPDATA%\AI-Terminal-Pet\bundles\ai-terminal-pet-bridge\` via the plugin manager (`install_bundle`) | turn/start to working, tool/call to tool_use, approval/asked to waiting_permission, tool/result with an error to error, turn/end to idle, process exit to closed |
| Anything else | Run `node reporters/generic.js` with `--source`, `--state`, and `--project` flags | Instant status reporting from any custom script or CLI tool |

Writing your own reporter for a tool that is not listed here needs no source reading: [docs/PROTOCOL.md](docs/PROTOCOL.md) specifies the wire protocol (fields, state semantics, pipe-name derivation, acknowledgment contract, and redaction rules) that a conforming reporter must implement.

The Harness side is a host-only Cordis bundle: it holds no pipe-name, state-set or snapshot logic of its own, it loads the protocol from `%LOCALAPPDATA%\AI-Terminal-Pet\protocol.js` and delegates everything to it.

The Harness side has a second, self-contained option since `dsh-ai-terminal-pet` `1.1.0`: a standalone DSH plugin package at [`packages/dsh-ai-terminal-pet`](packages/dsh-ai-terminal-pet), also shipped as a GitHub Release asset. The package is now **1.2.5** (tag `dsh-plugin-v1.2.5`, asset `dsh-ai-terminal-pet-1.2.5.tgz`); 1.2.4, 1.2.3, 1.2.2, 1.2.1, 1.2.0 and 1.1.0 stay published and immutable but are superseded. 1.2.5 is the first version that works on a machine that never ran the overlay: it declares `vendor/package.json` as CommonJS (without it, `require()` of the shipped protocol returned a namespace with no `sendStatus`, so a `DSH_PET_NO_BOOTSTRAP=1` install silently reported nothing), it reads the project path, lineage and start time from the session header instead of `process.cwd()` (the desktop Harness starts from the install directory, so every session was attributed to one wrong path), and its de-duplication signature now covers state, reason, tool, project, title and parent session instead of state alone. 1.2.4 was a wording fix (one market install read as if it covered every terminal, and it does not - the bundle mirrors **Harness** sessions out of the box, while OpenCode, Claude Code and Antigravity sessions appear only after each of those terminals gets its own reporter); 1.2.3 added the `dsh.marketplace` block a third-party storefront reads before offering a plugin to its desktop client, and 1.2.2 moved the installer from the repository root into `scripts/`, which edits Go comments, which changes the source digest `vendor/manifest.json` records. Release assets cannot be edited, so a wording or manifest fix costs a version - shipping different bytes under an unchanged version is exactly the drift this repository removes. The three install forms are verified end to end, and the 1.2.4 assets were installed again from three fresh directories after the release went out: the release tarball in **1.8 s**, the tag-pinned git source in **3.7 s**, and the repository URL in **6.5 s**, all rc=0, with the unpacked bytes matching `git show ff7f6de:` file for file (a bare `add dsh-ai-terminal-pet` still waits on the npm release described below):

```powershell
# from the release tarball: no git clone, no build step
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add https://github.com/jjjjjjjjnnjnn/ai-terminal-pet/releases/download/dsh-plugin-v1.2.6/dsh-ai-terminal-pet-1.2.6.tgz

# from git, pinned to the release tag
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add "git+https://github.com/jjjjjjjjnnjnn/ai-terminal-pet.git#dsh-plugin-v1.2.6&path:/packages/dsh-ai-terminal-pet"

# from the repository URL: resolves through the root manifest shim
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add github:jjjjjjjjnnjnn/ai-terminal-pet
```

The repository URL works because the repository root now carries a 68-line `package.json` shim that contains no code: it points `main` at the package, declares `dsh.bundle.patch` as `./packages/dsh-ai-terminal-pet/cordis.patch.yml` and limits `files` to that subtree. Without it a host that reads the repository root sees no `dsh.bundle`, installs an empty package and warns `declares no dsh.bundle`. The shim is `private`, so it never occupies the npm name, its `version` tracks the package (`verify.mjs` asserts they are equal, so a bump cannot land in one manifest only), and it carries the same `dsh.catalog` block the package does.

The package ships no lifecycle hooks at all — `prepack` was removed in 1.1.0 — because pnpm runs them for a git dependency and fails an unpinned source with an `allowBuilds` error that never mentions AI Terminal Pet. `vendor/` is committed instead and only verified: `node scripts/vendor.mjs --check` re-hashes the two vendored files and checks `vendor/manifest.json` against them, writing nothing. One form still fails, for a different reason: `git+https://github.com/jjjjjjjjnnjnn/ai-terminal-pet.git&path:/packages/dsh-ai-terminal-pet` without a `#ref` — pnpm concatenates the fragments and asks `ls-remote` for a repository that does not exist, so it reports `repository ... not found`.

1.2.0 also makes the package self-describing: `dsh.catalog` declares a `category` (`tool`), a one-line summary in English and Chinese, and five `capabilities` — `windows-overlay`, `named-pipe`, `session-state`, `tray-icon`, `no-network`. Those capabilities are **self-declared and unenforced**; dsh does not sandbox plugins, so the block describes what the overlay already does rather than granting it permission to do so. `keywords` gained `dsh-plugin`, the tag auto-indexing marketplaces harvest. 1.2.3 adds `dsh.marketplace` next to `dsh.bundle` and `dsh.catalog`: `profiles: ["desktop", "headless", "web"]`, `requiresBuildApproval: false` and `manualSteps: false`. That field is read by third-party registries, not by DSH - the plugin mounts through `dsh.bundle` either way, and this bundle only subscribes to `session/event`, so no profile-specific service is involved: that makes two independent discovery paths — registry review (a reviewed entry merges into `main` and only then appears in the list) and topic/keyword harvesting (no application needed at all). Two marketplaces already harvest automatically: [LivXue/dsh-plugin-shop](https://github.com/LivXue/dsh-plugin-shop) rebuilds daily from npm metadata, and every entry in its published shard is pinned by tarball integrity, so a Git-only package cannot appear there until it reaches npm; [zasenjc/dsh-plugins-store](https://github.com/zasenjc/dsh-plugins-store) syncs every 30 minutes and lists any public repository carrying both the `dsh-plugin` and `deepseek-harness` topics.

Its payload carries a prebuilt overlay and the official `protocol.js`, copied into `%LOCALAPPDATA%\AI-Terminal-Pet\` on first use **only when they are missing** — an existing install is never overwritten, and the overlay keeps running entirely on its own, so a machine that only wants the pet still needs nothing but `scripts/install.cmd`. Its entry in the [awesome-dsh-plugin](https://github.com/awesome-dsh-plugin/awesome-dsh-plugin) registry ([PR #13937](https://github.com/awesome-dsh-plugin/awesome-dsh-plugin/pull/13937)) passed both upstream checks and was merged on 2026-11-10, so the upstream catalogue lists the entry (that file pins which tarball the entry installs and can only be changed by pull request against that repository, never by an edit here: [PR #14076](https://github.com/awesome-dsh-plugin/awesome-dsh-plugin/pull/14076) moved it to 1.2.2 and merged at 19:59:37Z, and [PR #14089](https://github.com/awesome-dsh-plugin/awesome-dsh-plugin/pull/14089) moved it to 1.2.3 and merged at 2026-11-10T21:10:15Z, so the next rebuild renders that asset while [PR #14243](https://github.com/awesome-dsh-plugin/awesome-dsh-plugin/pull/14243), opened on 2026-11-11, carries 1.2.4 and adds the same "other terminals need their own reporter" sentence to both descriptions; [imsai-sh/awesome-deepseek-harness-plugins PR #912](https://github.com/imsai-sh/awesome-deepseek-harness-plugins/pull/912) makes the same wording fix there, and that repository never auto-merges an edit to an existing entry, so it waits for a maintainer; #14063, which had targeted 1.2.1, was closed once 1.2.2 packed the corrected bytes); the rendered catalogue page returned 404 at 16:16Z and became reachable later the same day once the upstream site build finished (`42844452013`, started 15:27:09Z, concluded 16:39:27Z); the catalogue file that DSH's in-app Market actually loads (`plugins.json`; its `count` was 10119 before that build and 10,304 when re-read after the 1.2.3 release) contains this repository too, but its `install` command is rendered from that `tarball` field at build time, so the copy read after the merge still emitted the 1.2.0 asset; the next rebuild rendered 1.2.2, then #14089 carried 1.2.3 past that when it merged at 2026-11-10T21:10:15Z. In a comment on the pull request the maintainer explained that he trimmed the merged description himself: for a Harness session the panel only mirrors state and jumps to the DSH window, so approving still happens inside DSH. The [DSH-Plugins-Marketplace](https://github.com/bradeGithub/DSH-Plugins-Marketplace) index picked this repository up automatically; its 18:08:44Z rebuild on 2026-11-10 records `pkg_name`/`version`, the verdict `bundle-plugin`, and now `risk_tier: "safe"` with an empty `risk_flags` list. That is not a favour granted by an allowlist: the scanner only fetches root-level `install.ps1`/`install.sh`/`package.json` and regex-scans them, and the two lines it used to match (`CurrentVersion\Run` and `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force`) moved into `scripts/` together with the installer, so those rules have no input left (the behaviour itself is unchanged). The DSH in-app Discover index accepts an npm version or a git source pinned to a 40-character commit. Both are satisfied now: the package is published on npm (`dist-tags.latest` is **1.2.5**, 17 files, the tarball byte-identical to the Release asset), so `dsh plugin --profile <profile> add dsh-ai-terminal-pet` resolves by bare name. Five more catalogues were filed after that release: [dshbase](https://github.com/ylwl1997/dshbase/issues/322), [dsh.so](https://github.com/dsh-so/dsh-plugin-submissions/issues/24), [dsh-plugin.org](https://github.com/dshplugin/dsh-plugin-hub/issues/735), [AllDSH](https://github.com/alldsh/submissions/issues/2) and [DSH Marketplace](https://dshmarketplace.dev) (which takes submissions through its own `POST /api/v1/submissions`); all five are topic-based discovery plus a human review, so none of them is a committed listing yet, and neither [DshMarketPlace/awesome-dsh-plugin](https://github.com/DshMarketPlace/awesome-dsh-plugin) nor the curated cache behind dshmarketplace.dev carries this repository at the moment (`/api/v1/plugins?q=ai-terminal-pet` answered `{"total":0}` and `data/curated.yml` has no entry for it). One reviewed catalogue has actually rendered the entry: [dshopen](https://github.com/polang233/dsh-plugin-index/issues/423) closed it as completed, and its live `dshopen.org/index.json` (1,207 entries) lists `dsh-ai-terminal-pet` with a git source; a newer version appears there only after that site rebuilds.

Because the plugin index format accepts a git source pinned to a commit, this repository also publishes its own index, so Discover works before npm does. Add this URL once in DSH under Plugins → Discover → index sources:

```text
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jjjjjjjjnnjnn/ai-terminal-pet/main/docs/market-index.json
```

[`docs/market-index.json`](docs/market-index.json) is one entry, `dsh-ai-terminal-pet` `1.2.6`, whose install spec is the same `git+...#<commit>&path:/packages/dsh-ai-terminal-pet` form that was installed end to end in 3.7 s above, pinned to `34aa1f7`, the commit the `dsh-plugin-v1.2.5` tag points at. It is validated with the host's own `parseMarketIndex` from `@deepseek

# ai-terminal-pet

Stop glancing across terminal windows to track agent states. It costs one small executable with no account and no cloud.

![ai-terminal-pet](docs/assets/hero.png)

![Platform](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-Windows-blue) ![Go](https://img.shields.io/badge/go-1.23-00ADD8) ![Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/version-1.0.0-blue)
![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-green) ![Size](https://img.shields.io/badge/size-4.17%20MiB-blue) ![Dependencies](https://img.shields.io/badge/dependencies-3-informational) ![Tests](https://img.shields.io/badge/tests-190-brightgreen) ![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/dsh-ai-terminal-pet?label=dsh%20plugin)

> 🇬🇧 [English](#english)  ·  🇨🇳 [中文](#中文)

---

## English

### The problem

You run Claude Code, OpenCode, or Antigravity in multiple terminal windows at once. A background task prompts for permission to execute a tool, but you are focused in another window and never notice the prompt.

Fourteen minutes later, you switch back only to discover that your build has been sitting idle the entire time. Glancing across multiple terminal tabs wastes focus and breaks your concentration.

ai-terminal-pet anchors a 56px strip to the screen edge. It aggregates your sessions in real time, pulses when an agent needs permission, and displays which project is waiting and for how long.

The table below contrasts the everyday workflow before and after using the overlay:

| Context | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Multiple terminals | Four terminal windows open; you lose track of which window needs attention. | One 56px strip on the edge of the screen aggregates every active session. |
| Blocked build | You find out a build was blocked on a permission prompt fourteen minutes ago. | The overlay pulses immediately and shows which project is waiting and for how long. |
| Context switching | You click across tabs to check whether builds and tasks are still running. | A single glance reveals current states without touching your keyboard or mouse. |

### What it looks like

![Demo](docs/assets/demo.gif)
*The actual sequence: a session blocks on a permission prompt and the strip breathes, hovering unfolds the session list, and clicking the waiting row brings that terminal forward. Frames are rasterized from the shipped renderer; the ring stands in for the click, since a layered window draws no cursor.*

![Compact strip](docs/assets/overlay-compact.png)
*Compact strip: pulsing state orb with status glyph, session count, state word, and waiting project name.*

![Expanded list](docs/assets/overlay-expanded.png)
*Expanded list: active sessions showing per-row project name, state, source hook, and relative time.*

![Many sessions](docs/assets/overlay-expanded-many.png)
*Expanded list with many sessions: six session rows followed by the overflow line showing remaining sessions.*

![Auto-approve countdown](docs/assets/overlay-auto-approve.png)
*Auto-approve countdown: draining bar with "Allow (5s)" prompt allowing manual veto before automatic permission approval.*

![In context](docs/assets/desktop-scene.png)
*In context: the strip sits at the screen edge beside two terminals, so a blocked session is visible without switching windows. The panel is the real renderer output; the two terminals around it are drawn, since a real capture would contain somebody's project names.*

---

### Features

The table below outlines the core capabilities and exact runtime parameters of the application:

| Feature | What it actually does |
|---|---|
| State aggregation | Aggregates sessions across 7 states (`idle`, `thinking`, `working`, `tool_use`, `waiting_permission`, `error`, `closed`), showing the highest-priority state across all active sessions. |
| Compact and expanded panels | Compact panel occupies 56x156 logical pixels anchored to a screen edge; clicking expands to 200 px wide, displaying 1–6 rows before adding an overflow line. |
| Whole-panel gestures | Click anywhere toggles compact and expanded views, drag anywhere moves 1:1 with the cursor, and mouse wheel adjusts zoom between 65% and 160%. |
| Edge retract | Slides mostly off-screen when docked at an edge leaving a thin sliver; hovering restores it, while waiting_permission or error states override retraction to remain visible. |
| Tray menu | Right-click tray menu toggles visibility, resets position and zoom, opens settings, switches language, toggles autostart, and configures auto-approve. |
| Settings window | Native three-tab window (General, Sound, Sessions) where every change persists immediately to `config.json` without an OK button. |
| Synthesized alert tones | Generates 44.1 kHz 16-bit mono PCM WAV tones in memory across four sound schemes (`chime`, `bell`, `soft`, `pulse`), with separate gates for waiting, error, and finish. |
| Per-session alerts | Fires Windows tray notification balloons and audio alerts on transitions into `waiting_permission`, `error`, or finish states. |
| Auto-approve and denylist | Provides a 5-second veto window on permission prompts where a tap denies and silence approves; blocks commands matching the dangerous-command denylist. |
| Jump to terminal | Walks session process ancestry and matches window titles to bring the waiting terminal window or tab to the foreground. |
| Scriptable CLI | Outputs structured session state via `ai-terminal-pet --json` by reading disk snapshots, avoiding blocking on GUI processes. |
| Single instance | A named mutex makes a second launch activate the running overlay instead of starting another one. |
| Connection capacity | The pipe server accepts 32 concurrent connections with a 5 s read timeout, so IPC never blocks the UI thread. |
| Idle lifecycle | A session is dropped only after a 2-minute absence grace; with no session left, the process removes itself after 10 minutes. |

### How it works

```text
Host CLI (Claude Code / OpenCode / Antigravity)
       │
       ▼ (Fire-and-forget hooks)
reporters/*.js
       │
       ▼ (JSON line over Windows named pipe: \\.\pipe\ai-terminal-pet-v1-<8hex>)
AI-Terminal-Pet.exe (Go 1.23, single-instance mutex)
       │
       ├─► internal/pipeserver (32 connections, 5s timeout, OK/ERR response)
       ├─► internal/store (in-memory state, TTL, disk snapshots fallback)
       └─► internal/ui (Win32 layered window, GDI topmost canvas)
```

- **Per-user named pipe**: IPC flows through `\\.\pipe\ai-terminal-pet-v1-<8hex>`, where `<8hex>` is derived from the SHA-256 hash of the user home directory. The exact same pipe-name algorithm is implemented in Go and JavaScript, locked by a cross-language golden test.

- **JSON line protocol**: Sessions transmit one JSON line per message with a 1 MiB payload cap. The server replies with an exact `OK` or `ERR` acknowledgment, and reporters retry until a deadline without treating partial reads as success.

- **On-disk snapshots**: Snapshot files under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\AI-Terminal-Pet\runtime\` provide a fallback channel and serve as the authoritative on-disk record of active sessions.

- **OS observation over heartbeats**: Session existence is decided by operating system observation of the process table and window titles rather than reporter heartbeats. A session remains active as long as its terminal window exists, and removal requires the host to be unobservable for a continuous 2-minute grace period.

- **Disks beat heartbeats**: The disk snapshot is authoritative for session existence: a session that was on disk and is gone is over, while synthetic PIDs from hooks never participate in liveness probing.

- **Connection handling**: The server accommodates 32 concurrent connections with a 5s read timeout, keeping IPC processing off the UI thread.

- **GDI rendering**: A top-down 32bpp DIB section created with CreateDIBSection is painted through a memory DC and handed to the layered window with UpdateLayeredWindow.

### Install

There are three ways in. Pick the one that matches how you got here.

**A. DeepSeek Harness user — no Go toolchain, nothing to build**

```powershell
dsh plugin add dsh-ai-terminal-pet
```

The package carries a prebuilt overlay and the official `protocol.js`. On first load it copies them into `%LOCALAPPDATA%\AI-Terminal-Pet\` **only when they are missing**, so it never overwrites an install you maintain yourself. That is the whole setup: the panel appears on the next session. It is also on npm as [`dsh-ai-terminal-pet`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-ai-terminal-pet) (1.2.5), and the release tarball, a tag-pinned git source and a bare repository URL all work (`dsh plugin add <path-or-git-url>`); the same bootstrap runs either way.

**B. Everyone else — download a package, no Go toolchain**

Two packages are published for this release: a self-extracting `pet-setup.exe` and a portable zip. Both install the same 11 artifacts into the same directory; the zip additionally lets you look inside before running anything.

1. Download one of them from the [`pet-v1.0.0` release](https://github.com/jjjjjjjjnnjnn/ai-terminal-pet/releases/tag/pet-v1.0.0):
   - **`pet-setup.exe`** (13.5 MB): double-click it. It verifies its own payload against `SHA256SUMS.txt` **before** writing anything, then runs the installer inside itself. `pet-setup.exe --verify` re-checks the installed files at any time, `--uninstall` removes them, `--add-to-path` puts the commands on your PATH.
   - **`ai-terminal-pet-1.0.0-win-x64.zip`** (4.98 MB, 17 files): unzip it anywhere and double-click `install.cmd`. Everything is inspectable first; `install.cmd -VerifyOnly`, `-Uninstall` and `-AddToPath` work as they do in the source tree.
2. Verify that the installation works:
   ```powershell
   & "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\AI-Terminal-Pet\AI-Terminal-Pet.exe" --json
   ```

The zip and the setup exe carry the three binaries, `protocol.js`, the Harness bundle, the installer and a `SHA256SUMS.txt`, so the only thing on Windows is one download and one double-click. Neither needs Go, Node, or an installer framework. The release is **not code-signed yet**, so the first run shows SmartScreen's "unknown publisher" prompt:

![SmartScreen on an unsigned build](docs/assets/smartscreen-unsigned.png)
*What an unsigned build produces on a machine that has never seen it: click **More info**, then **Run anyway**. This image is a reconstruction of the documented dialog, not a capture - see [docs/assets/README.md](docs/assets/README.md).*

That prompt is a certificate the project does not have, not a problem with the file you downloaded — the per-file SHA256 values in `SHA256SUMS.txt` are the honest substitute until a certificate exists.

After installing, `--doctor` should look like this (paths shortened here, everything else is the program's own output):

![--doctor on a healthy install](docs/assets/doctor-green.png)
*Nine checks, and the one that matters when you see an empty panel is `instance` — if it says a live instance is listening, the overlay is healthy and the missing piece is the terminal's reporter, not the install.*

**C. Developers — build from source (Go 1.23+)**

```powershell
# 1. Build the overlay, the native statusline shim and the native hook
go build -trimpath -buildvcs=false -ldflags "-s -w" -o .\bin\AI-Terminal-Pet.exe ./cmd/ai-terminal-pet
go build -trimpath -buildvcs=false -ldflags "-s -w" -o .\bin\pet-statusline.exe ./cmd/pet-statusline
go build -trimpath -buildvcs=false -ldflags "-s -w" -o .\bin\pet-hook.exe ./cmd/pet-hook

# 2. Install (stops a running overlay, copies, re-hashes every artifact)
.\scripts\install.cmd

# 3. See it work
& "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\AI-Terminal-Pet\AI-Terminal-Pet.exe" --json
```

Re-verify the installed artifacts at any time with per-file SHA256 checks:

```powershell
.\scripts\install.cmd -VerifyOnly
```

It prints `install: verified - 11 file(s) match the repository, 0 warning(s)` and exits 0 only when every deployed artifact matches (the 11 artifacts are the overlay, the statusline shim, the native hook `pet-hook.exe`, `protocol.js`, and the 7 files of the DeepSeek Harness bundle). The installer itself stops a running overlay first and waits for the process to release its file handles; a plain file copy over a live binary fails at random, which is what the retry loop and the SHA256 comparison after every copy are for.

`install.cmd` is the entry point rather than `install.ps1` because a stock Windows install runs PowerShell at `RemoteSigned`, and `RemoteSigned` refuses a local `.ps1` that still carries the "downloaded from the internet" zone marker — the exact shape of a file you unzip from a release. The wrapper starts one `powershell.exe` with `-ExecutionPolicy Bypass`, changes no machine or user policy, forwards every argument and every exit code, and adds no install logic: `install.ps1` remains the only implementation, and `.\scripts\install.ps1 -VerifyOnly` works unchanged on a machine whose policy already allows it.

Put `ai-terminal-pet` on your PATH so you can type the bare command:

```powershell
.\scripts\install.cmd -AddToPath
```

It writes **only** `HKCU\Environment\Path` (never `HKLM`), backs the previous value up to `<install dir>\path-backup.txt` first, and does nothing if the directory is already listed. **Open a new terminal** for the change to take effect. `-Uninstall` also removes that PATH entry, so uninstalling does not leave a dead entry behind (the previous value is backed up again, this time into `%TEMP%`).
Without this step the installer does not touch your PATH at all, so keep using the full path `& "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\AI-Terminal-Pet\AI-Terminal-Pet.exe" --json`.

The installer lives under `scripts/` rather than at the repository root on purpose: market indexers fetch a root `install.ps1` by name and regex-scan it, and this script legitimately mentions the `HKCU` Run key and a `-Recurse -Force` cleanup. Moving it one level down takes those two false positives off the root without taking any behaviour off the script.

Run `ai-terminal-pet --doctor` at any point after installing to self-check the environment, install files, runtime state, pipe, autostart entry, and node availability. To remove the deployed artifacts, run `.\scripts\install.cmd -Uninstall`; it asks for a typed `yes` confirmation first, refuses unsafe target directories, and accepts `-Force` for unattended removal.

Installing a terminal hook is required for that terminal to report; see the next section to connect your tools.

### Connect your terminal

| Terminal | How to connect | What you get |
|---|---|---|
| OpenCode | Add `file:///C:/path/to/ai-terminal-pet/reporters/opencode.js` to `plugin` in `opencode.json` | Automatic session tracking for tool use, prompt handling, and task completion |
| Claude Code | Add `& "%LOCALAPPDATA%\AI-Terminal-Pet\pet-hook.exe" --mode=claude` for `SessionStart`, `SessionEnd`, `UserPromptSubmit`, `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, `Stop`, and `Notification` in `settings.json`. `node <repo>/reporters/claude-hook.js` still works and is the fallback when you cannot run the `.exe`. | Real-time status updates, tool execution tracking, and permission prompt alerts |
| Antigravity | Set `statusLine.command` to `pet-statusline.exe` and configure `pet-hook.exe --mode=antigravity` for agent and tool events (`antigravity-hook.js` is the fallback) | Fast statusline updates, agent state changes, and permission request forwarding |
| DeepSeek Harness | Install the Cordis bundle from `%LOCALAPPDATA%\AI-Terminal-Pet\bundles\ai-terminal-pet-bridge\` via the plugin manager (`install_bundle`) | turn/start to working, tool/call to tool_use, approval/asked to waiting_permission, tool/result with an error to error, turn/end to idle, process exit to closed |
| Anything else | Run `node reporters/generic.js` with `--source`, `--state`, and `--project` flags | Instant status reporting from any custom script or CLI tool |

Writing your own reporter for a tool that is not listed here needs no source reading: [docs/PROTOCOL.md](docs/PROTOCOL.md) specifies the wire protocol (fields, state semantics, pipe-name derivation, acknowledgment contract, and redaction rules) that a conforming reporter must implement.

The Harness side is a host-only Cordis bundle: it holds no pipe-name, state-set or snapshot logic of its own, it loads the protocol from `%LOCALAPPDATA%\AI-Terminal-Pet\protocol.js` and delegates everything to it.

The Harness side has a second, self-contained option since `dsh-ai-terminal-pet` `1.1.0`: a standalone DSH plugin package at [`packages/dsh-ai-terminal-pet`](packages/dsh-ai-terminal-pet), also shipped as a GitHub Release asset. The package is now **1.2.5** (tag `dsh-plugin-v1.2.5`, asset `dsh-ai-terminal-pet-1.2.5.tgz`); 1.2.4, 1.2.3, 1.2.2, 1.2.1, 1.2.0 and 1.1.0 stay published and immutable but are superseded. 1.2.5 is the first version that works on a machine that never ran the overlay: it declares `vendor/package.json` as CommonJS (without it, `require()` of the shipped protocol returned a namespace with no `sendStatus`, so a `DSH_PET_NO_BOOTSTRAP=1` install silently reported nothing), it reads the project path, lineage and start time from the session header instead of `process.cwd()` (the desktop Harness starts from the install directory, so every session was attributed to one wrong path), and its de-duplication signature now covers state, reason, tool, project, title and parent session instead of state alone. 1.2.4 was a wording fix (one market install read as if it covered every terminal, and it does not - the bundle mirrors **Harness** sessions out of the box, while OpenCode, Claude Code and Antigravity sessions appear only after each of those terminals gets its own reporter); 1.2.3 added the `dsh.marketplace` block a third-party storefront reads before offering a plugin to its desktop client, and 1.2.2 moved the installer from the repository root into `scripts/`, which edits Go comments, which changes the source digest `vendor/manifest.json` records. Release assets cannot be edited, so a wording or manifest fix costs a version - shipping different bytes under an unchanged version is exactly the drift this repository removes. The three install forms are verified end to end, and the 1.2.4 assets were installed again from three fresh directories after the release went out: the release tarball in **1.8 s**, the tag-pinned git source in **3.7 s**, and the repository URL in **6.5 s**, all rc=0, with the unpacked bytes matching `git show ff7f6de:` file for file (a bare `add dsh-ai-terminal-pet` still waits on the npm release described below):

```powershell
# from the release tarball: no git clone, no build step
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add https://github.com/jjjjjjjjnnjnn/ai-terminal-pet/releases/download/dsh-plugin-v1.2.6/dsh-ai-terminal-pet-1.2.6.tgz

# from git, pinned to the release tag
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add "git+https://github.com/jjjjjjjjnnjnn/ai-terminal-pet.git#dsh-plugin-v1.2.6&path:/packages/dsh-ai-terminal-pet"

# from the repository URL: resolves through the root manifest shim
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add github:jjjjjjjjnnjnn/ai-terminal-pet
```

The repository URL works because the repository root now carries a 68-line `package.json` shim that contains no code: it points `main` at the package, declares `dsh.bundle.patch` as `./packages/dsh-ai-terminal-pet/cordis.patch.yml` and limits `files` to that subtree. Without it a host that reads the repository root sees no `dsh.bundle`, installs an empty package and warns `declares no dsh.bundle`. The shim is `private`, so it never occupies the npm name, its `version` tracks the package (`verify.mjs` asserts they are equal, so a bump cannot land in one manifest only), and it carries the same `dsh.catalog` block the package does.

The package ships no lifecycle hooks at all — `prepack` was removed in 1.1.0 — because pnpm runs them for a git dependency and fails an unpinned source with an `allowBuilds` error that never mentions AI Terminal Pet. `vendor/` is committed instead and only verified: `node scripts/vendor.mjs --check` re-hashes the two vendored files and checks `vendor/manifest.json` against them, writing nothing. One form still fails, for a different reason: `git+https://github.com/jjjjjjjjnnjnn/ai-terminal-pet.git&path:/packages/dsh-ai-terminal-pet` without a `#ref` — pnpm concatenates the fragments and asks `ls-remote` for a repository that does not exist, so it reports `repository ... not found`.

1.2.0 also makes the package self-describing: `dsh.catalog` declares a `category` (`tool`), a one-line summary in English and Chinese, and five `capabilities` — `windows-overlay`, `named-pipe`, `session-state`, `tray-icon`, `no-network`. Those capabilities are **self-declared and unenforced**; dsh does not sandbox plugins, so the block describes what the overlay already does rather than granting it permission to do so. `keywords` gained `dsh-plugin`, the tag auto-indexing marketplaces harvest. 1.2.3 adds `dsh.marketplace` next to `dsh.bundle` and `dsh.catalog`: `profiles: ["desktop", "headless", "web"]`, `requiresBuildApproval: false` and `manualSteps: false`. That field is read by third-party registries, not by DSH - the plugin mounts through `dsh.bundle` either way, and this bundle only subscribes to `session/event`, so no profile-specific service is involved: that makes two independent discovery paths — registry review (a reviewed entry merges into `main` and only then appears in the list) and topic/keyword harvesting (no application needed at all). Two marketplaces already harvest automatically: [LivXue/dsh-plugin-shop](https://github.com/LivXue/dsh-plugin-shop) rebuilds daily from npm metadata, and every entry in its published shard is pinned by tarball integrity, so a Git-only package cannot appear there until it reaches npm; [zasenjc/dsh-plugins-store](https://github.com/zasenjc/dsh-plugins-store) syncs every 30 minutes and lists any public repository carrying both the `dsh-plugin` and `deepseek-harness` topics.

Its payload carries a prebuilt overlay and the official `protocol.js`, copied into `%LOCALAPPDATA%\AI-Terminal-Pet\` on first use **only when they are missing** — an existing install is never overwritten, and the overlay keeps running entirely on its own, so a machine that only wants the pet still needs nothing but `scripts/install.cmd`. Its entry in the [awesome-dsh-plugin](https://github.com/awesome-dsh-plugin/awesome-dsh-plugin) registry ([PR #13937](https://github.com/awesome-dsh-plugin/awesome-dsh-plugin/pull/13937)) passed both upstream checks and was merged on 2026-11-10, so the upstream catalogue lists the entry (that file pins which tarball the entry installs and can only be changed by pull request against that repository, never by an edit here: [PR #14076](https://github.com/awesome-dsh-plugin/awesome-dsh-plugin/pull/14076) moved it to 1.2.2 and merged at 19:59:37Z, and [PR #14089](https://github.com/awesome-dsh-plugin/awesome-dsh-plugin/pull/14089) moved it to 1.2.3 and merged at 2026-11-10T21:10:15Z, so the next rebuild renders that asset while [PR #14243](https://github.com/awesome-dsh-plugin/awesome-dsh-plugin/pull/14243), opened on 2026-11-11, carries 1.2.4 and adds the same "other terminals need their own reporter" sentence to both descriptions; [imsai-sh/awesome-deepseek-harness-plugins PR #912](https://github.com/imsai-sh/awesome-deepseek-harness-plugins/pull/912) makes the same wording fix there, and that repository never auto-merges an edit to an existing entry, so it waits for a maintainer; #14063, which had targeted 1.2.1, was closed once 1.2.2 packed the corrected bytes); the rendered catalogue page returned 404 at 16:16Z and became reachable later the same day once the upstream site build finished (`42844452013`, started 15:27:09Z, concluded 16:39:27Z); the catalogue file that DSH's in-app Market actually loads (`plugins.json`; its `count` was 10119 before that build and 10,304 when re-read after the 1.2.3 release) contains this repository too, but its `install` command is rendered from that `tarball` field at build time, so the copy read after the merge still emitted the 1.2.0 asset; the next rebuild rendered 1.2.2, then #14089 carried 1.2.3 past that when it merged at 2026-11-10T21:10:15Z. In a comment on the pull request the maintainer explained that he trimmed the merged description himself: for a Harness session the panel only mirrors state and jumps to the DSH window, so approving still happens inside DSH. The [DSH-Plugins-Marketplace](https://github.com/bradeGithub/DSH-Plugins-Marketplace) index picked this repository up automatically; its 18:08:44Z rebuild on 2026-11-10 records `pkg_name`/`version`, the verdict `bundle-plugin`, and now `risk_tier: "safe"` with an empty `risk_flags` list. That is not a favour granted by an allowlist: the scanner only fetches root-level `install.ps1`/`install.sh`/`package.json` and regex-scans them, and the two lines it used to match (`CurrentVersion\Run` and `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force`) moved into `scripts/` together with the installer, so those rules have no input left (the behaviour itself is unchanged). The DSH in-app Discover index accepts an npm version or a git source pinned to a 40-character commit. Both are satisfied now: the package is published on npm (`dist-tags.latest` is **1.2.5**, 17 files, the tarball byte-identical to the Release asset), so `dsh plugin --profile <profile> add dsh-ai-terminal-pet` resolves by bare name. Five more catalogues were filed after that release: [dshbase](https://github.com/ylwl1997/dshbase/issues/322), [dsh.so](https://github.com/dsh-so/dsh-plugin-submissions/issues/24), [dsh-plugin.org](https://github.com/dshplugin/dsh-plugin-hub/issues/735), [AllDSH](https://github.com/alldsh/submissions/issues/2) and [DSH Marketplace](https://dshmarketplace.dev) (which takes submissions through its own `POST /api/v1/submissions`); all five are topic-based discovery plus a human review, so none of them is a committed listing yet, and neither [DshMarketPlace/awesome-dsh-plugin](https://github.com/DshMarketPlace/awesome-dsh-plugin) nor the curated cache behind dshmarketplace.dev carries this repository at the moment (`/api/v1/plugins?q=ai-terminal-pet` answered `{"total":0}` and `data/curated.yml` has no entry for it). One reviewed catalogue has actually rendered the entry: [dshopen](https://github.com/polang233/dsh-plugin-index/issues/423) closed it as completed, and its live `dshopen.org/index.json` (1,207 entries) lists `dsh-ai-terminal-pet` with a git source; a newer version appears there only after that site rebuilds.

Because the plugin index format accepts a git source pinned to a commit, this repository also publishes its own index, so Discover works before npm does. Add this URL once in DSH under Plugins → Discover → index sources:

```text
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jjjjjjjjnnjnn/ai-terminal-pet/main/docs/market-index.json
```

[`docs/market-index.json`](docs/market-index.json) is one entry, `dsh-ai-terminal-pet` `1.2.6`, whose install spec is the same `git+...#<commit>&path:/packages/dsh-ai-terminal-pet` form that was installed end to end in 3.7 s above, pinned to `34aa1f7`, the commit the `dsh-plugin-v1.2.5` tag points at. It is validated with the host's own `parseMarketIndex` from `@deepseek-ai/dsh-plugin-market-index`: `format: 1`, `en` localized text, declared category and label ids, an https icon pinned to the release commit, and an exact SemVer with a Unix-seconds `publishTimestamp`. The git source stays even though npm now carries the same bytes: it pins a commit, so the index keeps working for a host that cannot reach the registry.

Run `node reporters/generic.js` directly to report from any other CLI or script:

```powershell
node reporters/generic.js --source=aider --state=working --project="$PWD"
node reporters/generic.js --source=codex --state=waiting_permission --reason=approve
echo '{"state":"error","reason":"build failed"}' | node reporters/generic.js --source=ci --stdin
```

- `--source`: sets the reporter identity name.
- `--state`: sets one of the seven official session states.
- `--stdin`: parses a JSON payload piped directly from standard input.

### Control it from a script

The commands below assume `ai-terminal-pet` is on your PATH (`.\scripts\install.cmd -AddToPath`). If you skipped that step, prefix every command with the full path instead: `& "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\AI-Terminal-Pet\AI-Terminal-Pet.exe" --json`.

| Command | Effect |
|---|---|
| `ai-terminal-pet` | Start the overlay (no-op if already running) |
| `ai-terminal-pet --show` | Reveal the running overlay |
| `ai-terminal-pet --toggle` | Switch between compact and expanded views |
| `ai-terminal-pet --reset` | Re-anchor to the screen edge at 100% zoom |
| `ai-terminal-pet --settings` | Open the settings window |
| `ai-terminal-pet --quit` | Stop the running overlay |
| `ai-terminal-pet --json` | Print the current sessions as JSON (add `--pretty` for formatted output) |
| `ai-terminal-pet --doctor` | Run 9 environment and install checks; exit code 1 when a check fails. Again: needs the install directory on PATH, or call it by full path |
| `ai-terminal-pet --autostart` | Report the run-at-logon state |
| `ai-terminal-pet --autostart=on` | Enable run at logon |
| `ai-terminal-pet --autostart=off` | Disable run at logon |
| `ai-terminal-pet --version` | Print version information |

```powershell
