# dsh-ai-terminal-pet

A DeepSeek Harness (DSH) Cordis bundle that mirrors Harness session state onto
the [AI Terminal Pet](https://github.com/jjjjjjjjnnjnn/ai-terminal-pet) desktop
overlay: a small always-on-top Win32 pet that shows which sessions are working,
which one is waiting for your approval, which failed, and which finished.

The package ships the overlay binary and the official reporter protocol module
inside the tarball, so a single market install is enough to get a pet on screen
that follows **this Harness's** sessions. It does not attach to any other
terminal by itself: sessions from OpenCode, Claude Code and Antigravity appear
only after that terminal's own reporter is installed into it. The repository
README section [Connect your terminal](https://github.com/jjjjjjjjnnjnn/ai-terminal-pet#connect-your-terminal)
has one hook per terminal; the panel, the pipe and the protocol are shared, so
once a terminal reports it shows up next to the Harness sessions.

No npm dependencies, no install scripts, no network calls at runtime (unless the
maintainer pins a release in lib/release-pins.json, see below).

## What it does

| Harness signal | Overlay state |
| --- | --- |
| `turn/start`, `agent/inbox/claimed`, `agent/status` running | working |
| `tool/call` | tool_use |
| `approval/request` (waterfall listener) | waiting_permission |
| `tool/result` with `error`, `agent/error` | error |
| `turn/end`, `agent/status` idle | idle |
| Harness process exit | closed |

Events this table does not list are not part of the Harness session log: there is
no `command/done` or `working-directory/change` in `SessionEventMap`. The project
path, the parent session and the session start time do not come from events at
all - they are read from `session.header` (`cwd`, `parentSession`, `createdAt`),
which is the only place the host states them. That is also why a session shows
the right project even though the desktop Harness itself runs from its install
directory, and why a subagent conversation is nested under the session it was
forked from.

The overlay then plays an alert tone, shows a tray balloon on those transitions
and its one-click jump button targets the Harness window. Plugin reload (HMR)
disposes the listeners but deliberately does not close sessions: only a real
process exit means the conversation is over.

## Where it is listed, and what each market indexes

Three independent paths exist today, and each one reads a different field:

| Market | What it indexes | What this package offers it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| npm registry | package name, version, `dist.integrity` | published as `dsh-ai-terminal-pet`; a market that installs by name gets a verified tarball |
| dshmarket (the market tab most Harness Desktop users run) | `https://awesome-dsh-plugin.com/plugins.json`, which is generated from the [awesome-dsh-plugin](https://github.com/awesome-dsh-plugin/awesome-dsh-plugin) repository | entry merged via PR [#13937](https://github.com/awesome-dsh-plugin/awesome-dsh-plugin/pull/13937); the `install` command it renders comes from that entry's pinned `tarball`, so bumping it is always a pull request *there*, never an edit here |
| GitHub-harvesting markets | repositories carrying the `dsh-plugin` topic plus a root `package.json` declaring `name` and `dsh.bundle` | this repository has the topic and the root shim manifest, which is what makes `dsh plugin add github:owner/repo` resolve instead of mounting a 0.0.0 dependency |

"Listed" and "visible" are different states, and only the second one helps a
user: the awesome entry existed before its `plugins.json` entry did, because the
site builds the catalog on a schedule. Check the market's own public index, not
the merged pull request. The package README cannot promise what another
repository's build will render; it can only promise that the fields those builds
read are present and correct.

The package describes itself to storefronts through `dsh.catalog`: a category, a
one-line summary in both languages, and the capabilities it uses. Capabilities
are self-declared and never checked — DSH does not sandbox plugins — so read them
as a description, not a permission grant.
The bundle is Windows only and declares `dsh.bundle.platforms: ["win32"]`, so
other platforms show it as unsupported instead of installing it.

It also declares `dsh.marketplace` (`profiles: ["desktop", "headless", "web"]`,
`requiresBuildApproval: false`, `manualSteps: false`). DSH itself never reads
that field - the bundle mounts through `dsh.bundle` either way - but storefronts
that sort entries by profile do: without it a registry falls back to a
headless-or-web guess and a desktop client hides the entry.

Manually, from a terminal, into a profile you own — by package name, by release
tarball, or by pinning the release tag. All three are verified end to end:

```sh
# by package name: published on npm, no clone, no Go toolchain
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add dsh-ai-terminal-pet

# release tarball: same bytes as the npm release, straight from the GitHub Release
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add https://github.com/jjjjjjjjnnjnn/ai-terminal-pet/releases/download/dsh-plugin-v1.2.6/dsh-ai-terminal-pet-1.2.6.tgz

# git source, pinned to the release tag
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add "git+https://github.com/jjjjjjjjnnjnn/ai-terminal-pet.git#dsh-plugin-v1.2.6&path:/packages/dsh-ai-terminal-pet"
```

Those three differ only in transport. The npm path is the shortest and the one a
market uses when it installs by name; the tarball path works when a market pins a
release asset instead of a registry entry; the git path is the fallback for a
machine that cannot reach npm at all. Every one of them lands the same
prebuilt overlay in `vendor/`.

Do not hand pnpm a bare repository URL. pnpm resolves a git dependency by
running the package's lifecycle scripts, and it blocks those for unpinned
git sources until you copy the `allowBuilds` key it prints into your profile's
`pnpm-workspace.yaml`; the failure message never mentions AI Terminal Pet. The
package therefore ships no lifecycle hook, and its vendored overlay is a
committed file rather than a build product. `vendor/manifest.json` records the
SHA-256 of that file, the SHA-256 of the Go sources it was built from, and the
Go version that produced it, so a stale or hand-edited vendor directory fails a
check instead of shipping quietly.

The GitHub and npm paths above need nothing from this repository at install time.
`dsh plugin add dsh-ai-terminal-pet` resolves through the npm registry; the
tarball and git forms resolve through GitHub. A marketplace that indexes npm
sees the package under its own name and can verify the published integrity
digest; a marketplace that indexes repositories sees the `dsh-plugin` topic and
the root shim manifest.

`add` is the whole install: the profile records the dependency, and the bundle
declares itself through `dsh.bundle.patch`, so no separate `enable` step exists.
The profile you add it to has to be the one Harness boots.

Two profiles are special. The reserved `desktop` profile is rejected by the
standalone `dsh` CLI (`profile "desktop" is managed exclusively by the Electron
application`); the Desktop app's own bundled CLI does accept it, and the in-app
plugin manager is the supported path there. Any other profile name is yours.

If the app reports restart-required after enabling the bundle, restart Harness.

## What it writes on disk

First use in a Harness process copies two files, and only when they are missing:

| File | Origin | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| %LOCALAPPDATA%\AI-Terminal-Pet\protocol.js | vendor/protocol.js | pipe name, state set, redaction, snapshot |
| %LOCALAPPDATA%\AI-Terminal-Pet\AI-Terminal-Pet.exe | vendor/AI-Terminal-Pet.exe | the Win32 overlay |

Nothing is ever overwritten: an existing file, including one placed by the
standalone installer, wins. Set DSH_PET_NO_BOOTSTRAP=1 to skip this step
entirely (for example when the overlay is managed by `scripts/install.ps1` already).

Reports also write the overlay's normal runtime snapshot under the same
directory, exactly like every other reporter.

### Optional download fallback

lib/release-pins.json is absent from the published package by default. When the
maintainer fills it in with pinned release asset URLs, sizes and SHA-256
digests, a machine that has no vendored binary downloads the two assets over
HTTPS with a 30 s timeout, verifies size and digest with node:crypto, and only
then installs them. Any failure is silent apart from one warning; the plugin
keeps working without an overlay.

## The overlay itself is still standalone

This bundle is a convenience. The overlay is a Go application that installs
normally with `scripts/install.ps1` from the repository, and every other reporter
(Claude Code, OpenCode, Antigravity, generic) talks to the same named pipe.
Those reporters are separate installs, not part of this package: a terminal that
has none of them hooked reports nothing, in this install or in any other. A
machine that only wants the overlay does not need this package; a machine that
only wants the plugin gets one installed automatically.

## Requirements and limits

- Windows only (named pipes plus a Win32 layered window).
- Node 22.19+ or 24+ in the Harness runtime.
- Nothing in this package can fail the host: every entry point is wrapped,
  every report is fire-and-forget, and there is no process.exit.
- Session id is the Harness session.header.id; pid is a synthetic per-session
  id and parentPid is the real Harness process, which is how the overlay ties a
  session to its terminal window.

# ai-terminal-pet

Stop glancing across terminal windows to track agent states. It costs one small executable with no account and no cloud.

![ai-terminal-pet](docs/assets/hero.png)

![Platform](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-Windows-blue) ![Go](https://img.shields.io/badge/go-1.23-00ADD8) ![Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/version-1.0.0-blue)
![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-green) ![Size](https://img.shields.io/badge/size-4.17%20MiB-blue) ![Dependencies](https://img.shields.io/badge/dependencies-3-informational) ![Tests](https://img.shields.io/badge/tests-190-brightgreen) ![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/dsh-ai-terminal-pet?label=dsh%20plugin)

> 🇬🇧 [English](#english)  ·  🇨🇳 [中文](#中文)

---

## English

### The problem

You run Claude Code, OpenCode, or Antigravity in multiple terminal windows at once. A background task prompts for permission to execute a tool, but you are focused in another window and never notice the prompt.

Fourteen minutes later, you switch back only to discover that your build has been sitting idle the entire time. Glancing across multiple terminal tabs wastes focus and breaks your concentration.

ai-terminal-pet anchors a 56px strip to the screen edge. It aggregates your sessions in real time, pulses when an agent needs permission, and displays which project is waiting and for how long.

The table below contrasts the everyday workflow before and after using the overlay:

| Context | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Multiple terminals | Four terminal windows open; you lose track of which window needs attention. | One 56px strip on the edge of the screen aggregates every active session. |
| Blocked build | You find out a build was blocked on a permission prompt fourteen minutes ago. | The overlay pulses immediately and shows which project is waiting and for how long. |
| Context switching | You click across tabs to check whether builds and tasks are still running. | A single glance reveals current states without touching your keyboard or mouse. |

### What it looks like

![Demo](docs/assets/demo.gif)
*The actual sequence: a session blocks on a permission prompt and the strip breathes, hovering unfolds the session list, and clicking the waiting row brings that terminal forward. Frames are rasterized from the shipped renderer; the ring stands in for the click, since a layered window draws no cursor.*

![Compact strip](docs/assets/overlay-compact.png)
*Compact strip: pulsing state orb with status glyph, session count, state word, and waiting project name.*

![Expanded list](docs/assets/overlay-expanded.png)
*Expanded list: active sessions showing per-row project name, state, source hook, and relative time.*

![Many sessions](docs/assets/overlay-expanded-many.png)
*Expanded list with many sessions: six session rows followed by the overflow line showing remaining sessions.*

![Auto-approve countdown](docs/assets/overlay-auto-approve.png)
*Auto-approve countdown: draining bar with "Allow (5s)" prompt allowing manual veto before automatic permission approval.*

![In context](docs/assets/desktop-scene.png)
*In context: the strip sits at the screen edge beside two terminals, so a blocked session is visible without switching windows. The panel is the real renderer output; the two terminals around it are drawn, since a real capture would contain somebody's project names.*

---

### Features

The table below outlines the core capabilities and exact runtime parameters of the application:

| Feature | What it actually does |
|---|---|
| State aggregation | Aggregates sessions across 7 states (`idle`, `thinking`, `working`, `tool_use`, `waiting_permission`, `error`, `closed`), showing the highest-priority state across all active sessions. |
| Compact and expanded panels | Compact panel occupies 56x156 logical pixels anchored to a screen edge; clicking expands to 200 px wide, displaying 1–6 rows before adding an overflow line. |
| Whole-panel gestures | Click anywhere toggles compact and expanded views, drag anywhere moves 1:1 with the cursor, and mouse wheel adjusts zoom between 65% and 160%. |
| Edge retract | Slides mostly off-screen when docked at an edge leaving a thin sliver; hovering restores it, while waiting_permission or error states override retraction to remain visible. |
| Tray menu | Right-click tray menu toggles visibility, resets position and zoom, opens settings, switches language, toggles autostart, and configures auto-approve. |
| Settings window | Native three-tab window (General, Sound, Sessions) where every change persists immediately to `config.json` without an OK button. |
| Synthesized alert tones | Generates 44.1 kHz 16-bit mono PCM WAV tones in memory across four sound schemes (`chime`, `bell`, `soft`, `pulse`), with separate gates for waiting, error, and finish. |
| Per-session alerts | Fires Windows tray notification balloons and audio alerts on transitions into `waiting_permission`, `error`, or finish states. |
| Auto-approve and denylist | Provides a 5-second veto window on permission prompts where a tap denies and silence approves; blocks commands matching the dangerous-command denylist. |
| Jump to terminal | Walks session process ancestry and matches window titles to bring the waiting terminal window or tab to the foreground. |
| Scriptable CLI | Outputs structured session state via `ai-terminal-pet --json` by reading disk snapshots, avoiding blocking on GUI processes. |
| Single instance | A named mutex makes a second launch activate the running overlay instead of starting another one. |
| Connection capacity | The pipe server accepts 32 concurrent connections with a 5 s read timeout, so IPC never blocks the UI thread. |
| Idle lifecycle | A session is dropped only after a 2-minute absence grace; with no session left, the process removes itself after 10 minutes. |

### How it works

```text
Host CLI (Claude Code / OpenCode / Antigravity)
       │
       ▼ (Fire-and-forget hooks)
reporters/*.js
       │
       ▼ (JSON line over Windows named pipe: \\.\pipe\ai-terminal-pet-v1-<8hex>)
AI-Terminal-Pet.exe (Go 1.23, single-instance mutex)
       │
       ├─► internal/pipeserver (32 connections, 5s timeout, OK/ERR response)
       ├─► internal/store (in-memory state, TTL, disk snapshots fallback)
       └─► internal/ui (Win32 layered window, GDI topmost canvas)
```

- **Per-user named pipe**: IPC flows through `\\.\pipe\ai-terminal-pet-v1-<8hex>`, where `<8hex>` is derived from the SHA-256 hash of the user home directory. The exact same pipe-name algorithm is implemented in Go and JavaScript, locked by a cross-language golden test.

- **JSON line protocol**: Sessions transmit one JSON line per message with a 1 MiB payload cap. The server replies with an exact `OK` or `ERR` acknowledgment, and reporters retry until a deadline without treating partial reads as success.

- **On-disk snapshots**: Snapshot files under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\AI-Terminal-Pet\runtime\` provide a fallback channel and serve as the authoritative on-disk record of active sessions.

- **OS observation over heartbeats**: Session existence is decided by operating system observation of the process table and window titles rather than reporter heartbeats. A session remains active as long as its terminal window exists, and removal requires the host to be unobservable for a continuous 2-minute grace period.

- **Disks beat heartbeats**: The disk snapshot is authoritative for session existence: a session that was on disk and is gone is over, while synthetic PIDs from hooks never participate in liveness probing.

- **Connection handling**: The server accommodates 32 concurrent connections with a 5s read timeout, keeping IPC processing off the UI thread.

- **GDI rendering**: A top-down 32bpp DIB section created with CreateDIBSection is painted through a memory DC and handed to the layered window with UpdateLayeredWindow.

### Install

There are three ways in. Pick the one that matches how you got here.

**A. DeepSeek Harness user — no Go toolchain, nothing to build**

```powershell
dsh plugin add dsh-ai-terminal-pet
```

The package carries a prebuilt overlay and the official `protocol.js`. On first load it copies them into `%LOCALAPPDATA%\AI-Terminal-Pet\` **only when they are missing**, so it never overwrites an install you maintain yourself. That is the whole setup: the panel appears on the next session. It is also on npm as [`dsh-ai-terminal-pet`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-ai-terminal-pet) (1.2.5), and the release tarball, a tag-pinned git source and a bare repository URL all work (`dsh plugin add <path-or-git-url>`); the same bootstrap runs either way.

**B. Everyone else — download a package, no Go toolchain**

Two packages are published for this release: a self-extracting `pet-setup.exe` and a portable zip. Both install the same 11 artifacts into the same directory; the zip additionally lets you look inside before running anything.

1. Download one of them from the [`pet-v1.0.0` release](https://github.com/jjjjjjjjnnjnn/ai-terminal-pet/releases/tag/pet-v1.0.0):
   - **`pet-setup.exe`** (13.5 MB): double-click it. It verifies its own payload against `SHA256SUMS.txt` **before** writing anything, then runs the installer inside itself. `pet-setup.exe --verify` re-checks the installed files at any time, `--uninstall` removes them, `--add-to-path` puts the commands on your PATH.
   - **`ai-terminal-pet-1.0.0-win-x64.zip`** (4.98 MB, 17 files): unzip it anywhere and double-click `install.cmd`. Everything is inspectable first; `install.cmd -VerifyOnly`, `-Uninstall` and `-AddToPath` work as they do in the source tree.
2. Verify that the installation works:
   ```powershell
   & "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\AI-Terminal-Pet\AI-Terminal-Pet.exe" --json
   ```

The zip and the setup exe carry the three binaries, `protocol.js`, the Harness bundle, the installer and a `SHA256SUMS.txt`, so the only thing on Windows is one download and one double-click. Neither needs Go, Node, or an installer framework. The release is **not code-signed yet**, so the first run shows SmartScreen's "unknown publisher" prompt:

![SmartScreen on an unsigned build](docs/assets/smartscreen-unsigned.png)
*What an unsigned build produces on a machine that has never seen it: click **More info**, then **Run anyway**. This image is a reconstruction of the documented dialog, not a capture - see [docs/assets/README.md](docs/assets/README.md).*

That prompt is a certificate the project does not have, not a problem with the file you downloaded — the per-file SHA256 values in `SHA256SUMS.txt` are the honest substitute until a certificate exists.

After installing, `--doctor` should look like this (paths shortened here, everything else is the program's own output):

![--doctor on a healthy install](docs/assets/doctor-green.png)
*Nine checks, and the one that matters when you see an empty panel is `instance` — if it says a live instance is listening, the overlay is healthy and the missing piece is the terminal's reporter, not the install.*

**C. Developers — build from source (Go 1.23+)**

```powershell
# 1. Build the overlay, the native statusline shim and the native hook
go build -trimpath -buildvcs=false -ldflags "-s -w" -o .\bin\AI-Terminal-Pet.exe ./cmd/ai-terminal-pet
go build -trimpath -buildvcs=false -ldflags "-s -w" -o .\bin\pet-statusline.exe ./cmd/pet-statusline
go build -trimpath -buildvcs=false -ldflags "-s -w" -o .\bin\pet-hook.exe ./cmd/pet-hook

# 2. Install (stops a running overlay, copies, re-hashes every artifact)
.\scripts\install.cmd

# 3. See it work
& "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\AI-Terminal-Pet\AI-Terminal-Pet.exe" --json
```

Re-verify the installed artifacts at any time with per-file SHA256 checks:

```powershell
.\scripts\install.cmd -VerifyOnly
```

It prints `install: verified - 11 file(s) match the repository, 0 warning(s)` and exits 0 only when every deployed artifact matches (the 11 artifacts are the overlay, the statusline shim, the native hook `pet-hook.exe`, `protocol.js`, and the 7 files of the DeepSeek Harness bundle). The installer itself stops a running overlay first and waits for the process to release its file handles; a plain file copy over a live binary fails at random, which is what the retry loop and the SHA256 comparison after every copy are for.

`install.cmd` is the entry point rather than `install.ps1` because a stock Windows install runs PowerShell at `RemoteSigned`, and `RemoteSigned` refuses a local `.ps1` that still carries the "downloaded from the internet" zone marker — the exact shape of a file you unzip from a release. The wrapper starts one `powershell.exe` with `-ExecutionPolicy Bypass`, changes no machine or user policy, forwards every argument and every exit code, and adds no install logic: `install.ps1` remains the only implementation, and `.\scripts\install.ps1 -VerifyOnly` works unchanged on a machine whose policy already allows it.

Put `ai-terminal-pet` on your PATH so you can type the bare command:

```powershell
.\scripts\install.cmd -AddToPath
```

It writes **only** `HKCU\Environment\Path` (never `HKLM`), backs the previous value up to `<install dir>\path-backup.txt` first, and does nothing if the directory is already listed. **Open a new terminal** for the change to take effect. `-Uninstall` also removes that PATH entry, so uninstalling does not leave a dead entry behind (the previous value is backed up again, this time into `%TEMP%`).
Without this step the installer does not touch your PATH at all, so keep using the full path `& "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\AI-Terminal-Pet\AI-Terminal-Pet.exe" --json`.

The installer lives under `scripts/` rather than at the repository root on purpose: market indexers fetch a root `install.ps1` by name and regex-scan it, and this script legitimately mentions the `HKCU` Run key and a `-Recurse -Force` cleanup. Moving it one level down takes those two false positives off the root without taking any behaviour off the script.

Run `ai-terminal-pet --doctor` at any point after installing to self-check the environment, install files, runtime state, pipe, autostart entry, and node availability. To remove the deployed artifacts, run `.\scripts\install.cmd -Uninstall`; it asks for a typed `yes` confirmation first, refuses unsafe target directories, and accepts `-Force` for unattended removal.

Installing a terminal hook is required for that terminal to report; see the next section to connect your tools.

### Connect your terminal

| Terminal | How to connect | What you get |
|---|---|---|
| OpenCode | Add `file:///C:/path/to/ai-terminal-pet/reporters/opencode.js` to `plugin` in `opencode.json` | Automatic session tracking for tool use, prompt handling, and task completion |
| Claude Code | Add `& "%LOCALAPPDATA%\AI-Terminal-Pet\pet-hook.exe" --mode=claude` for `SessionStart`, `SessionEnd`, `UserPromptSubmit`, `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, `Stop`, and `Notification` in `settings.json`. `node <repo>/reporters/claude-hook.js` still works and is the fallback when you cannot run the `.exe`. | Real-time status updates, tool execution tracking, and permission prompt alerts |
| Antigravity | Set `statusLine.command` to `pet-statusline.exe` and configure `pet-hook.exe --mode=antigravity` for agent and tool events (`antigravity-hook.js` is the fallback) | Fast statusline updates, agent state changes, and permission request forwarding |
| DeepSeek Harness | Install the Cordis bundle from `%LOCALAPPDATA%\AI-Terminal-Pet\bundles\ai-terminal-pet-bridge\` via the plugin manager (`install_bundle`) | turn/start to working, tool/call to tool_use, approval/asked to waiting_permission, tool/result with an error to error, turn/end to idle, process exit to closed |
| Anything else | Run `node reporters/generic.js` with `--source`, `--state`, and `--project` flags | Instant status reporting from any custom script or CLI tool |

Writing your own reporter for a tool that is not listed here needs no source reading: [docs/PROTOCOL.md](docs/PROTOCOL.md) specifies the wire protocol (fields, state semantics, pipe-name derivation, acknowledgment contract, and redaction rules) that a conforming reporter must implement.

The Harness side is a host-only Cordis bundle: it holds no pipe-name, state-set or snapshot logic of its own, it loads the protocol from `%LOCALAPPDATA%\AI-Terminal-Pet\protocol.js` and delegates everything to it.

The Harness side has a second, self-contained option since `dsh-ai-terminal-pet` `1.1.0`: a standalone DSH plugin package at [`packages/dsh-ai-terminal-pet`](packages/dsh-ai-terminal-pet), also shipped as a GitHub Release asset. # from git, pinned to the release tag

# Arya Computer Use

Computer use for [DeepSeek Harness / AryaCode](https://github.com/KonnectSuite): drive Windows desktop apps through **native accessibility refs** (UIA) instead of pixel coordinates, with a **takeover overlay** that frames the window being driven, shows what the agent is doing, keeps a synthetic ghost cursor where it acts (your own pointer is never followed), and stops on a global Esc. The agent calls itself **Arya** in that overlay by default, and the name is a setting.

Replaces [dsh-computer-use-win](https://github.com/Yu-tao-Li/dsh-computer-use-win) (wincu) completely — see [docs/PLAN.md](docs/PLAN.md) §7 for the retirement path.

## Why

| wincu complaint | Arya Computer Use |
| --- | --- |
| Slow (PowerShell + UIA backend) | Native Rust engine: ~90 ms per call measured on this devbox (snapshot 90 ms, ref action 85 ms, `list-windows` 56 ms). Every CLI call costs ~85 ms of process start plus UIA init, so the number of calls, not the tool, sets the latency — `batch` runs up to 20 steps in one call (6 steps: 332 ms engine vs ~510 ms step by step) |
| Pixel alignment off | Ref-based semantic UIA — coordinates are never the targeting mechanism; identical twins are refused, not mis-clicked |
| Chinese UI/docs | English throughout |
| (kept) DSH integration + setup UI | Settings page, chat step rows, takeover overlay, Esc kill, tool presets |

## Engines (not vendored — pinned npm dependencies)

- [`agent-desktop`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-desktop) `1.2.0` (Apache-2.0) — accessibility-tree computer use CLI, native Windows binaries on npm. Reference mirror: [KonnectSuite/dsh-arya-agent-desktop](https://github.com/KonnectSuite/dsh-arya-agent-desktop).
- [`agent-browser`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-browser) `0.41.2` (Apache-2.0) — web lane via CDP (`agent-browser mcp`).

## Requirements

- **DSH host must run elevated (Run as administrator).** The engine's interaction lease lives at `C:\ProgramData\agent-desktop\<user-SID>\interaction.lock` with a protected DACL `{SYSTEM, Administrators, token user}`; a non-elevated medium-IL token fails validation (`lease_directory_untrusted`). The adapter surfaces this as an explicit "run AryaCode as administrator" hint.
- Accessibility permission (`desktop_status` reports `accessibility: granted`).
- Engine state root is the engine default `~/.agent-desktop` — do **not** point `AGENT_DESKTOP_HOME` at `%LOCALAPPDATA%` (inherited AppContainer ACEs fail the engine's private-DACL check).

## Status

**Phases 0–2 complete (Phase 0 accepted 2026-11-06; takeover UI verified live 2026-11-07).**

| Phase | Deliverable | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | Evaluation spike: raw `agent-desktop mcp` row, drive Notepad/Explorer/Chrome — speed ✓, readable trees ✓, refs-not-pixels ✓ | ✅ accepted, spike removed |
| 1 | Adapter MCP server: Lite 22 tools, per-conversation session lifecycle, headed toggle + foreground promotion, screenshot→file path, WinRT OCR, skill | ✅ built, installed, driven in-host |
| 2 | Takeover UI: window rim + banner + Esc kill, configurable ghost cursor, settings page, chat step rows, driver lock, English UI | ✅ built + verified live |
| 3 | Web lane (`arya_browser` row), sign-in profiles, attach-to-your-Chrome, **wincu retirement** | planned |
| 4 | Lazy preset, notifications/clipboard/trace, npm publish | planned |

Lite 22 tool surface: `snapshot, find, get, is, click, focus, double_click, right_click, expand, collapse, toggle, set_value, type, press, scroll, list_windows, launch, wait, screenshot, ocr, batch, tools` (superset of wincu Lite 12; `set_value` fills a field through the accessibility value pattern without touching the pointer — **the headless text path, use it for text entry**; `expand`/`collapse`/`toggle` are semantic UIA patterns and stay headless; `focus`, `double_click` and `right-click` have no headless path on Windows, so each one drives the real pointer for that single call and never latches the conversation; `type` likewise synthesizes real keystrokes, which on Windows is physical input; `tools` manages headed/overlay/session state).

Full plan: [docs/PLAN.md](docs/PLAN.md).

## Layout

```
package.json          Cordis bundle manifest (dsh.bundle.patch) + pinned engine deps
cordis.patch.yml      rows: arya-computer-use (Host), mcp-arya-desktop, mcp-arya-browser
index.js              Host plugin entry (settings, driver lock, takeover mgmt, status route)
client.js             Settings page + chat step rows (client plugin)
mcp/adapter-server.mjs  adapter MCP server (Lite 22 tool surface)
scripts/windows-takeover.cs  window rim + banner + progress + ghost cursor + global Esc
scripts/ocr.ps1       WinRT OCR helper (Phase 1)
skills/arya-desktop/  observe-act loop guide (Phase 1)
locale/ icon.svg      Plugin Manager display metadata
docs/PLAN.md          complete v1 plan
```

## Install

### From the plugin market (recommended)

1. In AryaCode: **Plugins → Arya Plugin Market → add a source** and paste
   `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/KonnectSuite/dsh-arya-computer-use@main/index.json`
2. Install **Arya Computer Use** from the list, then restart AryaCode.

The published package is `@aryacode/dsh-plugin-arya-computer-use` (npm, public). Everything it needs ships in the tarball: the desktop adapter, the browser launcher, the takeover overlay sources and the skill. The two MCP lanes are mounted **in-process** by `index.js` (`ctx.plugin(<bridge>, …)`), so there are no absolute paths in the bundle patch and no `npx` child process — a 1.0.0 install works the same on any machine.

### From a checkout (development)

`plugin_manager` → `install_bundle` pointing at this directory. The bundle patch is a single row (`arya-computer-use`); the MCP lanes still mount in-process, so a checkout install and a registry install behave identically.

## Settings (Settings → Plugins → Computer Use)

| Setting | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Frame the app window | on | Rim only the driven window plus a banner; monitor edges are just the fallback before a target is known |
| Show a ghost cursor | on | Draw a synthetic cursor where the agent acts; your pointer is never followed |
| Agent name | `Arya` | Drives the ghost-cursor tag and the progress-panel header (`Arya · Step 3 · acting`), 1–16 characters |
| Banner text | `Arya is controlling your computer` | One line, 1–120 characters |
| Real mouse and keyboard | off | Opted-in headed input for one conversation: **every** action then drives the real pointer and keyboard. It releases on `session_end` and expires after 5 minutes. Text entry never needs it — `set_value` is headless; `type` is physical on its own. |
| One conversation drives at a time | on | Refuses desktop tools in other conversations while a drive is live |
| Progress panel detail | `summary` | What the on-screen step panel prints: `summary` = short action lines, `source` = the assistant's raw text stream (the old default — it paints model text on your desktop) |
| Stop shortcut | Esc | Global kill switch; synthetic keystrokes are ignored, so it needs a real keypress. It now also gates the driver: desktop input tools return `COMPUTER_USE_STOPPED_BY_USER` for that turn (reads keep working) |
| Tool preset | `lite` | `lite` lists all 22 desktop tools; `lazy` starts with tools/snapshot/click and reveals the rest on demand |
| Tool surface (web) | `core` | agent-browser tool profile: core 29, network 9, state 27, debug 40, tabs 13, react 8, mobile 15, webmcp 4, all 156 |
| Chrome profile / Session | – / `arya` | Reuse a Chrome login state and name the browser session |
| Connect to my browser | – | `--cdp` port or URL to attach to a Chrome you already have open |
| Saved sign-in state | – | Absolute path to a cookies+localStorage JSON to reuse |
| Show the browser window | off | `--headed` for the web lane |

## Web lane

The second MCP row (`arya_browser`, server `agent-browser`) runs through `mcp/browser-launcher.mjs`, a transparent stdio pipe that reads the control file and spawns the real server with the settings applied:

```
node mcp/browser-launcher.mjs          # → agent-browser mcp --tools core [--profile X] [--session Y] [--state Z] [--cdp ...] [--headed]
```

So sign-in reuse and attaching to your own Chrome are settings, not hand-edited rows. Web-lane changes land on the next MCP restart; the settings page says so.

## Plugin market

Installing from Plugins -> Arya Plugin Market needs no manual source: on first run the plugin registers
`https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/KonnectSuite/dsh-arya-computer-use@main/index.json`
with the market (existing sources are kept) and every npm release shows up there as an update. Releases go
through npm staged publishing, so a publish is visible in the market once the version is approved on npmjs.com.

The plugin manager blocks dependency build scripts by default. The engines (`agent-desktop`, `agent-browser`)
fetch their native binary in a postinstall script; approve those two builds when installing, or let 1.0.1+
repair them itself at start-up - the status route reports the outcome under `mcp.engines`.

## Tool presets

- `lite` (default) — all 22 desktop tools listed up front.
- `lazy` — starts with `tools`, `snapshot`, `click`; everything else appears after `tools {operation:"load", names:[...]}`. The adapter advertises `tools.listChanged` and emits `notifications/tools/list_changed`, which DSH's MCP client re-syncs (`listChanged.onChanged → refreshTools`), so the new tools become callable immediately.

## License

MIT (KonnectSuite original code). Engines stay Apache-2.0 — see [NOTICE.md](NOTICE.md).

# dsh-voice

Voice input for the DeepSeek Harness Web GUI — as an **official plugin bundle**.

A microphone button (SVG icon) sits next to the send button in the composer.
Clicking it brings up a ChatGPT-style recording "pill" above the composer:

```
[ ✕ cancel ] [~~~~~~~~ waveform ~~~~~~~~] [ ⏹ stop ] [ ↑ send ]
```

- **✕** — cancel the recording;
- **⏹** — stop, transcribe and insert the text into the input (without sending);
- **↑** — stop, transcribe and send to the chat immediately.

The waveform is a row of vertical bars: fresh signal arrives on the right,
history fades left into a dim dotted baseline (like ChatGPT's voice mode).

## Installation

### Requirements

- A running DeepSeek Harness with the Web GUI (Node.js quick start:
  `npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web`, default `http://127.0.0.1:3080`).
- A **POSIX host** (Linux/macOS): the host half runs `bash`, `curl` (engine and
  model downloads) and `ffmpeg` (audio conversion). Windows is not supported —
  there `ctx.shell` is PowerShell, so the plugin logs one warning and registers
  nothing. The transcribe.cpp engine is downloaded automatically per
  OS/architecture from this repository's Releases — or adopted from `PATH` / a
  sibling `.engine/` dir if a `transcribe-cli` binary already exists.
- A browser with mic access over HTTPS or localhost.

### Install into a profile (all sessions)

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add github:KotDath/dsh-voice
```

For a local test build instead:

```sh
npm install && npm run build
dsh plugin --profile web add file:/path/to/dsh-voice
```

The install lands in the **running** process when the profile mounts the `hmr`
row — no restart. A profile without that row reads its composition at boot, so
restart the web process (`dsh web`) there. Either way the plugin is then active
in **every session** of the profile: no per-session `cordis_define`, no source
edits.

Updating an install that already exists is the one case that still needs a
nudge: pnpm replaces the package directory, so the mounted row can keep running
the previous module until it is re-mounted — toggling the plugin in the plugin
manager re-mounts it live (and `/api/voice/config` reports the version that is
actually loaded).

The package declares `dsh.bundle.patch` (→ `cordis.patch.yml`, one row
`id: voice, name: dsh-voice`) and `dsh.client` (→ the browser half
`lib/client.js`). `dsh plugin` installs it with pnpm into the profile and
reconciles `dsh.profile.bundles` automatically.

To remove:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-voice
```

### First-run flow (for the end user)

1. Open **Settings → Voice** — the engine is either `✓ installed` or
   downloadable with one click ("Download engine", releases built by CI).
2. Pick a model from the catalog and press **Download** if it is not marked ✓.
3. Use the mic button next to the send button in the composer.
4. Record → `✕` cancel / `⏹` insert / `↑` send.

### Keyboard activation

`Ctrl+E` (or the **Record** value in Settings → Voice) toggles recording:
the first press starts it, the second one finishes it — by default the
transcript is inserted into the draft **and sent**, exactly like `↑`.

- The combination is configurable in **Settings → Voice → Voice input
  shortcut** (Record + Test + a fallback combination), and it is stored with
  the rest of the settings in `.dsh-voice/state.json`.
- A **fallback** combination (`Ctrl+Alt+E` by default) is live at the same
  time: browsers reserve plenty of `Ctrl+<key>` combinations (`Ctrl+E` opens
  the address bar in some), and **Test** tells you whether a press actually
  reached the page.
- The shortcut is a plugin-owned listener, not a Harness command: the Harness
  shortcut registry (`ctx.shortcuts`) refuses `Ctrl+E` on Web/Linux (`Ctrl+/`,
  `Ctrl+Shift+,` and `Ctrl+Shift+.` are the only admitted Web/Linux bindings),
  so the layer listens on `window`, defers to events the application already
  handled, and stays out of terminals, dialogs and text composition.
- `⏹` in the pill keeps working for "insert without sending"; the same is
  available as the **Second press → Insert only** option.
- **In place, like Codex.** While a recording runs the controls appear in the
  composer's **own tool row**: `✕` and the live waveform on the left, the mic
  button turning into `⏹` in place, and the model select stepping aside. Nothing
  changes height, so the ambient stats row under the card stays put and the stop
  button stays exactly under the microphone — no floating pill above the
  composer. `⏹` stops and inserts the transcript, and a dedicated **send**
  button appears next to the composer's own `↑` for sending the dictation
  straight away; `Ctrl+E` does insert-and-send in one press.
- **Question cards.** While an `ask_user_question` card occupies the composer
  (the option list with its “type your own answer” field), the same shortcut
  records and inserts the transcript into that card's answer field at the
  caret — it never submits the answer, so you can review it and press Enter
  yourself. The composer's pill is not mounted in that presentation, so a small
  floating indicator (Cancel / Stop) appears just above the card instead.

## Architecture

```
[Client: browser]                                [Host: Node]
┌─────────────────────────────────┐  fetch      ┌────────────────────────────────┐
│ slot conversation.input.right   │ ──────────► │ /api/voice/transcribe          │
│  • MediaRecorder (webm/opus)    │ base64+meta │  • base64 -d → file           │
│  • AnalyserNode → waveform      │              │  • ffmpeg → 16 kHz mono wav    │
│  • timers, states               │ ◄─────────── │  • provider:                  │
│ inputActions.setDraft + submit  │   { text }   │     tcpp:  transcribe-cli      │
└─────────────────────────────────┘              │     local: whisper-cli -oj     │
                                                 │     api:   curl multipart     │
                                                 │     codex: ChatGPT backend    │
                                                 │       ($CODEX_HOME auth.json) │
                                                 │  • temp file cleanup           │
                                                 └────────────────────────────────┘
```

Unlike the earlier dynamic-plugin versions, the two halves do **not** use the
`harness.handle`/`host.call` bridge: the Node half registers plain HTTP
endpoints on the harness webserver (`/api/voice/*`), and the browser half
calls them with `fetch`. That is the pattern used by other static bundle
plugins (e.g. dsh-track).

## Transcription providers

Switchable in **Settings → Voice**. The choice (provider, language, paths and
the host-only API key) is persisted on the host in
`<launch-dir>/.dsh-voice/state.json` — directory `0700`, file `0600` — so it
survives both a `dsh web` restart and a plugin re-mount. Delete that file to
reset the plugin to its defaults.

| Provider | How it works | Requirements |
|---|---|---|
| `tcpp` (default) | the **transcribe.cpp** engine (the same one inside Handy) — a static `transcribe-cli` binary (~5 MB). A catalog of **67 models** (GigaAM v3 CTC/RNN-T/E2E, Voxtral Mini 3B/4B/24B, Whisper tiny…large-v3 (+turbo), Qwen3-ASR, Parakeet, Canary, Moonshine, Nemotron, Granite, SenseVoice, Fun-ASR, Cohere, MedASR…). Model picker dropdown, one-click Hugging Face download with progress | engine (self-downloads for Win/macOS/Linux) |
| `codex` | the **ChatGPT subscription** behind your local Codex CLI login: the recording goes to the ChatGPT backend speech-to-text endpoint with the OAuth token from `$CODEX_HOME/auth.json` | a `codex login` on the host; no API key, no model download |
| `local` | whisper.cpp (`whisper-cli`) + one GGML model | paths to the binary and model; offline |
| `api` | OpenAI-compatible `POST /v1/audio/transcriptions` (multipart) | URL, API key, model name (`gpt-4o-transcribe`, `whisper-1`, Groq, a local faster-whisper server, etc.) |

### Codex / ChatGPT subscription

If the host is already signed in to the Codex CLI with a ChatGPT plan, that
subscription can transcribe voice input — nothing to download and no API key:

1. `codex login` on the host (once), then **Settings → Voice → Transcription
   provider → Codex**. The panel shows the account, the plan and the token
   expiry, and **Test** sends one second of silence through the real path to
   prove the login, the endpoint and `ffmpeg` in one click.
2. Record as usual. The whole recording (up to the 5-minute cap) is sent as a
   single 16 kHz WAV request — unlike the local models, this endpoint keeps
   context across several minutes, so long dictations no longer need the 20 s
   chunking used by `tcpp`.

How it behaves:

- **Credentials**: the host reads `$CODEX_HOME/auth.json` (default
  `~/.codex/auth.json`) and passes the access token to `curl` through the
  `DSHVOICE_CODEX_TOKEN` environment variable — never in argv, and the token
  never reaches the page (the settings only ever see the account, plan and
  expiry). The file can be pointed elsewhere in **Advanced**.
- **It is never written to.** The plugin does not refresh or rewrite the
  login: ChatGPT refresh tokens rotate, and a second writer would invalidate
  the login the Codex CLI itself depends on. If the token expires, the panel
  says so — run any `codex` command (or `codex login`) to refresh it.
- **Language**: the endpoint takes a concrete language code (the Language
  setting is forwarded for `ru`/`en`/`uk`/`de`). `Auto` is not a valid value
  there and is simply omitted, which is why auto-detect works.
- **Errors are decoded**, not dumped: an expired login reports the 401 plus
  the fix, a Cloudflare block reports the 403, and a rate limit reports 429.
- An `auth.json` in API-key mode is reported as such — that mode cannot use the
  subscription endpoint.

Measured on this machine: a 5-minute Russian dictation transcribed in one
request in ~68 s, a 50-second one in ~13 s.

### transcribe-cli engine: out of the box, no Handy app needed

- The plugin **does not depend on the Handy application**: the ASR engine is the
  open-source library [handy-computer/transcribe.cpp](https://github.com/handy-computer/transcribe.cpp).
- The binary is downloaded with the "Download engine" button from this
  repository's GitHub Releases for the current OS/architecture
  (`transcribe-cli-{platform}-{arch}`, `.exe` on Windows).
- If a `transcribe-cli` already exists on `PATH` or next to the configured
  engine path, the plugin **adopts it** (copies it into its own directory) — no
  download needed. Discovery is explicit; there is no filesystem sweep.
- Downloads are verified against a `.sha256` sidecar when one is published
  (best-effort integrity check).
- Plugin data (engine, models, temp files) lives in the DSH process launch
  directory (`.engine/`, `.models/`, `.tmp/`) — the sandbox only allows writes
  there. Paths are shown in the settings.
- Release binaries are built by CI (`.github/workflows/build-engine.yml`):
  Linux x86_64/arm64, macOS arm64/x86_64, Windows x86_64.
- Models are GGUF files from Hugging Face (`handy-computer`); the catalog is
  embedded in the plugin (sizes drive the progress bar). Models already
  downloaded by Handy into the HF cache are picked up automatically — no
  re-download required.
- **Long recordings**: many models have a ~25 s window (e.g. GigaAM) and silently
  lose the rest of a long recording. The plugin splits audio longer than 22 s
  into 20 s segments and transcribes them in one batch run (single model load,
  full text concatenated).

Verified on this machine: GigaAM v3 E2E-RNN-T — 30× realtime, Voxtral Mini 4B
Realtime — 1.7× realtime (20 s of Russian audio), excellent quality.

### API key and Codex credential handling

The OpenAI-compatible API key is **host-only**: it is set via its own endpoint
(`POST /api/voice/api-key`), never echoed back to the page (the settings show
only whether a key is set), and is passed to the provider via the
`DSHVOICE_API_KEY` environment variable — never in argv.

The Codex provider applies the same rules to the ChatGPT login: the host reads
`$CODEX_HOME/auth.json`, passes the access token as `DSHVOICE_CODEX_TOKEN`
(again never in argv), surfaces only the account, plan and expiry to the page,
and never writes to the file.

## Development

```
npm install          # dev deps (uses .npm-cache/ if ~/.npm is read-only)
npm run build        # gen-catalog → tsc → tsdown (lib/index.js + lib/client.js)
npm test             # both Node suites (plain Node, no browser)
```

`npm test` runs `test/run.mjs` (bundle/catalog contract) and `test/codex.mjs`
(the Codex provider, mounted on a fake Cordis context — offline by default).
Add `DSH_VOICE_LIVE=1` to also drive the real ChatGPT backend with the Codex
login of this host:

```
DSH_VOICE_LIVE=1 node test/codex.mjs
```

The installable artifact is the npm package at the repository root. See
[AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) for the full agent instructions (layout, endpoints,
security rules, troubleshooting).

## Repository layout

```
src/plugin/          — Node half (index.ts, HTTP /api/voice/*) + browser half
                       (client/: state, recorder, waveform, components,
                       settings, hotkey, voice.module.css) + generated catalog
scripts/gen-catalog.mjs — injects models.json into generated-catalog.ts
tsdown.config.ts     — node ESM bundle + browser CJS-closure bundle
cordis.patch.yml     — the bundle's composition patch (one row: id voice)
package.json         — dsh.bundle.patch + dsh.client declarations
models.json          — model catalog (source of truth)
test/                — Node suites: run.mjs (bundle contract), codex.mjs
                       (Codex provider; DSH_VOICE_LIVE=1 adds real API calls),
                       hotkey.mjs (the Ctrl+E layer's pure helpers)
.github/workflows/build-engine.yml — CI: plugin tests + 5-platform engine builds
AGENTS.md            — agent install/update instructions
README.md            — this document
```

Released versions are pinned by git tags (`v0.4.0`, …).

## v1 limitations

- Recording uses the browser `MediaRecorder` (HTTPS or localhost required).
- Transcription is batch (after the recording ends); streaming partials are
  planned.
- Upstream whisper.cpp does not support Handy's Qwen3-ASR GGUF (needs the
  transcribe-cpp engine); standard ggml models (tiny…large-v3) work.

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-foxy-game

让 Foxy 陪你玩游戏。不是“让模型看一张截图然后祈祷它能操作”，而是把**感知、决策、操作、交流**拆成可替换的适配器，先跑通一个可控的小闭环，再逐个游戏加适配。

> 当前是 `0.1.4` 开发预览版。默认关闭所有自动操作；不会主动碰带反作弊的网游。

### 开发进度（2026-11-12 04:14）

- 已跑通 DSH 侧栏、窗口枚举、窗口截图、SHA-256 跳帧、视觉模型 JSON 决策、后台动作接口、自测游戏 HTTP 闭环。
- `npm test`：11/11 通过（设置/脱敏/裁剪参数/键位/视觉解析/策略/自测游戏/memory/插件路由）。
- 真实 DSH `foxy-test` profile：侧栏 `Foxy Game` 已出现，`/api/dsh-foxy-game/status` 返回 200。
- 真实窗口截图：`captureWindow` 对系统设置窗口返回 640×379 JPEG（约 15 KB）；mock 视觉接口收到图片并返回决策。
- 自测游戏 memory 闭环：观察 → BFS 决策 → HTTP 动作 → 状态更新，已验证。
- 自动循环：能启动、按截图间隔跳帧、停止；画面未变化时只记 `skip` 日志。
- `F12` 全局紧急停止：已用 `keybd_event` 注入 F12 实测，能写入停止标志；启动时自动拉起隐藏热键进程，停止时清理。
- 语音录音停止改为给 ffmpeg 发 `q` 正常收尾，避免直接 kill 留下损坏 WAV；真实麦克风录音仍待验证。
- 后台输入：`SendMessage` 对原生 WinForms 测试窗实测成功（`D` 使玩家 x+1），且不抢前台；Edge 会忽略合成消息，真实游戏兼容性必须逐个测。
- 完整屏幕闭环：原生 WinForms 测试窗 `hwnd 122882056` 截图 640×436（8.5 KB）→ mock 视觉返回 `{type:'key',key:'d'}` → 后台 `SendMessage`，玩家 x 从 0 变为 1，前台未切换。

## 设计原则

1. **先适配，再通用**：屏幕、内存、游戏 API 都只是“观测源”；键鼠、后台消息、内存写入都只是“动作端”。
2. **默认低成本**：截图先做窗口裁剪、缩放、JPEG 压缩，再按哈希跳帧；不是每帧都发给视觉模型。
3. **默认不抢前台**：优先后台 `SendMessage`（同步调用，可能被不处理消息的游戏卡住），前台 `SendInput` 作为兼容回退；MAA 的 `AnchoredTouch` 说明“合成输入不移动真实光标”是可行的，但需要游戏窗口支持。
4. **语音是本地回路**：按住快捷键说话 → 本地 STT → 模型 → 悬浮字幕 + TTS；不依赖游戏内聊天框。
5. **危险能力显式开启**：读内存、写内存、自动点击都默认关闭，并在 UI 里单独警告。

## 三条感知路线

| 模式 | 原理 | 适合 | 风险/限制 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `screen` | 窗口截图 → 视觉模型 → 动作 | 解密、视觉小说、回合制、慢节奏策略 | 延迟高、token 贵、精确坐标难 |
| `memory` | 读游戏进程/游戏 API 的结构化状态 | 本地小游戏、模拟器、带 API 的游戏 | 需要偏移/结构；反作弊风险；版本一变就坏 |
| `hybrid` | 内存给数值，屏幕给空间/文字 | 大多数可组合场景 | 两套适配器都要维护 |

当前版本实现了 `screen` 和 `hybrid` 的骨架；`memory` 目前只有受控的 HTTP 状态源（给自测游戏），**没有**真实游戏进程的内存读取偏移或写入能力。

## 已实现（开发预览）

- DSH 侧栏 `Foxy Game`：窗口选择、截图间隔、跳帧、视觉模型配置、动作模式、自动循环开关、实时日志。
- `capture.ps1`：枚举窗口，`PrintWindow`/屏幕回退截图，缩放 + JPEG，返回 base64；Node 侧做 SHA-256 跳帧。
- 安全：自动循环运行时可用 `F12` 全局紧急停止；默认 `enabled:false`，不会自行启动。
- `vision.js`：OpenAI 兼容的视觉请求，严格 JSON 输出（`analysis/action/say/confidence`）；解析失败会保留原文并报错。
- `actions.js` + `input.ps1`：键盘按下/抬起/点按、鼠标移动/点击、文本；支持 `background`（SendMessage）和 `foreground`（SendInput）。
- `test-game/`：一个本地小游戏 + HTTP 状态/动作 API，用来在没有视觉模型时验证“观测→决策→动作→记忆”闭环。
- 语音/悬浮字幕：`voice.js`、`overlay.ps1`、`hotkey.ps1` 的本地回路骨架（默认关闭，需要麦克风设备名）。悬浮字幕已实测：原生长文本会自动扩高到 760×208，并保持置顶。
- `scripts/stt.py`：本地 SenseVoice 转写后备；TTS 优先 DSH Speech，回退 Windows SAPI。

## 调研结论

- **Neuro-sama** 不是纯屏幕 AI：游戏通过 [Neuro API](https://github.com/o9nn/neuro-sama) 这类游戏侧 SDK 暴露状态/动作，AI 与语音是独立管线。结论：能给游戏加 API 时，API 永远优于截图。
- **ARC-AGI 多模态 Agent** 常用“每步截图 → 视觉模型分析 → 动作 → 累计规则/历史”，但会把图缩到很小（如 128×128）来控制成本。结论：全量每帧视觉不可持续，必须跳帧 + 变化检测 + 结构化缓存。
- **MAA Win32** 的输入分层：`Seize`（SendInput，兼容性最好但抢鼠标）、`Message/Post`（后台消息，部分游戏屏蔽）、`AnchoredTouch`（`InjectSyntheticPointerInput`，不移动真实光标/不切前台，MaaFramework v5.13.0）。参考 [MAA Win32 控制器](https://deepwiki.com/MaaXYZ/MaaFramework/4.2-win32)、[MAA PR #18341](https://github.com/MaaAssistantArknights/MaaAssistantArknights/pull/18341)。结论：默认后台，失败再回退前台；不要默认抢鼠标。
- **LLM 游戏 Agent** 的共同点是“观察→行动→结果→短期记忆”的循环，而不是一次性长提示。参考 [Human Strategy Meets AI Execution](https://dl.acm.org/doi/pdf/10.1145/3715014.3724375)。

## 快速开始

```powershell
# 在 DSH 工作区
cd D:\Documents\deepseek-harness\default-workspace\dsh-foxy-game
npm test

# 启动自测游戏（另一个终端）
npm run test-game
# 浏览器打开 http://127.0.0.1:8787

# 或者启动原生 WinForms 测试窗，专门测后台输入
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File test-game/win.ps1
# 状态文件：%TEMP%\foxy-win-game.json
```

安装到 DSH（开发时）：

```powershell
dsh plugin --profile desktop add file:D:\Documents\deepseek-harness\default-workspace\dsh-foxy-game
```

然后在侧栏打开 `Foxy Game`：

1. 点“刷新窗口”，选择游戏窗口；
2. 配置视觉模型（OpenAI 兼容 `/chat/completions`，模型必须支持图片输入）；
3. 先点“观察一次”，看日志里的分析/动作；
4. 确认动作模式（建议先 `background`）再开“自动循环”。

## 配置

设置保存在 `~/.dsh/foxy-game/settings.json`。关键字段：

```jsonc
{
  "enabled": false,
  "mode": "screen",              // screen | hybrid | memory
  "windowHwnd": 0,
  "windowTitle": "",
  "captureIntervalMs": 1500,
  "skipUnchanged": true,
  "maxWidth": 1280,
  "jpegQuality": 65,
  "visionBaseUrl": "https://api.deepseek.com",
  "visionApiKey": "",
  "visionModel": "deepseek-chat",
  "actionMode": "background",    // background | foreground | none
  "autoPlay": false,
  "maxStepsPerMinute": 20,
  "memorySource": "none",        // none | test-http
  "memoryUrl": "http://127.0.0.1:8787",
  "voiceEnabled": false,
  "pttKey": "F8",
  "micDevice": "",
  "ttsProvider": "sapi",         // sapi | dsh
  "overlayEnabled": true
}
```

## 目录

```
lib/            DSH 服务端插件、截图、视觉、动作、语音
scripts/        PowerShell 窗口/截图/输入/悬浮窗/热键，Python STT
test-game/      本地自测游戏 + HTTP API
test/           Node 内置测试
```

## 已知问题 / 下一步

- [ ] 真实游戏窗口的 `PrintWindow` 在部分 DirectX 游戏返回黑屏；需要 `Windows.Graphics.Capture` 或 `ffmpeg gdigrab` 回退。
- [ ] 后台合成消息在 Edge 窗口实测无效（浏览器忽略）；原生 WinForms 测试窗用 `SendMessage` 已通过。真实游戏是否接受需逐个验证，不接受时只能回退前台 `SendInput` 或做 `AnchoredTouch`。
- [ ] 变化区域目前只做整图哈希；块级 diff / 只发变化区域还没做。
- [ ] 视觉模型的动作坐标是归一化坐标，未做窗口 DPI 校正；高 DPI 需要实测。
- [ ] 内存适配器目前只有自测 HTTP 源，**没有**真实进程内存读取或写入。
- [ ] 悬浮字幕已单独验证；语音热键/麦克风录音需要在真实 Windows 会话中验证，当前默认关闭。
- [x] 自动循环支持 `F12` 全局紧急停止（`scripts/stop-hotkey.ps1`）；默认仍不自动启动。
- [ ] 没有做反作弊检测/规避；这是有意为之，不提供绕过能力。

## License

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# DSH 归档管理 2.3.0

目标宿主为 DeepSeek Harness 0.2.2-rc.1。

## 使用

- **直接删除**。会话空闲时，点击对话顶部的删除按钮，或在侧栏会话菜单选「删除会话…」。也可以先点「停止」，随即打开删除入口。插件会等待宿主收尾，确认后才保存并释放会话。仍有任务或排队输入时，页面会显示原因。
- **批量删除归档会话**。在「设置 → 归档管理」可删除当前筛选中已选的会话，或使用「删除搜索结果」处理当前结果。「继续清理」会重新列出上次未完成的会话及文件，待确认后继续。
- **单独删除子智能体**。在「设置 → 归档管理」点「子智能体」，选择会话后点「删除所选」。确认框会一并列出所选会话派出的各级子智能体。单独删子智能体时，父会话中已收到的消息及历史引用会保留。

核对确认框中的会话、文件和检查范围，点击「确认删除」。若保存和释放后待清理范围有变化，确认框会显示更新后的清单。再次确认后才删除。提交后可查看处理进度和索引同步状态。完成后会话从归档和搜索列表中移除，未完成的项目会显示标题和原因。

取消归档可将尚未清理的会话放回普通列表。用量校验在写入清理标记前失败时，仍可以取消归档。删除不可恢复，没有回收站或第二次删除入口。

## 删除内容与保留内容

- 清理本机当前 v4 会话日志、已登记扫描目录中同一会话的日志副本，以及对应的 `session_projcache` 会话缓存及可核验缓存备份。
- 先核对主日志和登记副本的用量。任一来源报告异常用量时暂停清理当前会话。可核对的最新用量保存在独立摘要中，删除和重启后仍可查看。摘要不含聊天正文。
- 保留项目文件、共享附件、用量存储及空目录。未登记的外部备份、云端副本不在此次核验范围内。
- 删除父会话时，子智能体后代会逐个清理，最后删除父会话。普通分支独立保存，存在普通分支时需先处理该分支。
- 同一批次按目录和文件指纹复用清单及日志头，逐条持租约复核。文件处理后同步一次已启用的本地全文搜索索引，复查主日志和副本均已清理后写入完成标记。
- 保存用量失败、文件或子智能体关系改变、被占用、路径异常或清理失败时，页面会显示跳过或未完成。部分清理中断后，可从归档管理继续处理。

确认框会列出每个会话的精确文件路径和检查的会话根目录。出现新的子智能体、副本或原文件变化，需要重新确认。清理以这些目录中的文件和应用搜索记录为范围，磁盘取证层面的擦除另计。

无法解析的备份日志会显示路径并保留。若损坏日志所在目录与目标会话或已识别的子智能体匹配，该组需先处理损坏文件才能继续。主存储或目录结构异常时会阻止清理。

## 副本扫描目录

本机 `cordis.patch.yml` 登记：

```yaml
backupScanRoots:
  - F:/dsh-youhua/dsh-usage-stats/.sandbox
  - F:/dsh-youhua/dsh-archive-manager/.sandbox
```

在这些目录中寻找会话根目录；不全盘搜索、不跟随链接、不进入依赖目录。`copy-tests` 和 `purge-tests` 为合成单元测试夹具，不属于历史聊天副本来源。将来若把会话备份到其他目录，需要把目录加入 `backupScanRoots` 后重新启动 DSH。

归档列表和删除确认框会显示已登记目录的状态。目录缺失、无法读取或路径异常时暂停清理。恢复目录后，刷新列表并重新核对。未配置额外备份根目录的环境只检查当前会话存储。

副本按日志内的会话 ID 验证，不按标题或模糊字符串删除。清理前会读取已登记日志副本的完整用量。旧前缀可由现有摘要覆盖，含有可核对新增用量的较新副本会先补齐摘要。日志分歧、无法完整读取副本，或主日志已不存在且没有摘要时，保留该会话的日志和副本。

## 安装与更新

本机 desktop profile 使用安装包。构建后运行 `install.ps1` 安装 `dist/dsh-archive-manager-local-2.3.0.tgz`，再完全退出并重新打开 DSH。

```powershell
npm ci --ignore-scripts
npm test
npm run pack:plugin
```

后端构建引用相邻 `../dsh-usage-stats/src/ledger.js`，开发时保留两个源码目录。共享代码打入构建产物，安装后不依赖源码目录，也不要求统计插件已启用。

正式发版从工作区根目录运行 `node scripts/release.mjs`，统一测试、打包和校验两个插件。

## 验证

- `npm test`：单列表直接删除、旧记录迁移、确认批次、文件变化、身份核验、占用和失败保护。
- `node scripts/verify-live-archive-sandbox.mjs` 验证运行中拒绝、停止后直接删、单独删子智能体、父子清理顺序、文件与搜索索引复查，以及既有归档流程。
- `node ../dsh-usage-stats/scripts/verify-retention-sandbox.mjs`：真实宿主中的合成会话及副本/缓存清理，检查重启后用量。
- `npm run preview`：`http://127.0.0.1:19423` 的模拟数据界面，不操作真实会话。
- `scripts/clean-legacy-copies.mjs`：显式离线核对并清理已彻底删除会话的旧副本，先核对每个模型/日期的用量已保留。日常使用无需运行。

源码、构建产物和安装包分别在 `src/`、`lib/`、`dist/`；验证记录在 `qa/`。测试数据、真实数据副本与 QA 报告均不打包。来源与许可证见 NOTICE.md。

# DSH 本地插件工作区说明

更新日期：2026-11-11。

本工作区用于开发和维护 DeepSeek Harness 的本地插件。目前包含「使用统计」和「归档管理」两个独立项目，功能和界面参考 ZCode 官方项目，没有采用 dsh-scope。插件通过 DSH 扩展机制加载，不修改主程序 `app.asar`。

## 插件导航

| 项目 | 包名与当前版本 | DSH 入口 | 主要用途 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [使用统计项目说明](dsh-usage-stats/项目说明.md) | `dsh-usage-stats-local` 1.2.4 | 设置 → 使用统计 | 本机会话 Token 总量与四项明细、活动热力图、模型趋势与占比 |
| [归档管理项目说明](dsh-archive-manager/项目说明.md) | `dsh-archive-manager-local` 2.3.0 | 对话顶部、侧栏会话菜单、设置 → 归档管理 | 停止后直接删除，支持筛选删除、清理进度、子智能体清理和中断后续删 |

两个项目可以分别构建、安装和卸载，不要求同时启用。工作区根目录没有统一的 npm 工程，开发命令应在对应插件文件夹执行。

## 目录结构

```text
F:\dsh-youhua\
├─ README.md                      工作区总说明
├─ dsh-usage-stats\               使用统计插件
│  ├─ 项目说明.md                 功能、实现、维护与验证说明
│  ├─ README.md                   安装与使用指南
│  ├─ src\                       后端统计与前端页面源码
│  ├─ lib\                       DSH 实际加载的构建产物
│  ├─ dist\                      tgz 安装包和 SHA-256
│  ├─ test\                      自动测试
│  ├─ scripts\                   构建、预览、数据核对与隔离环境工具
│  └─ qa\                        测试记录、汇总快照和截图
└─ dsh-archive-manager\           归档管理插件
   ├─ 项目说明.md
   ├─ README.md
   ├─ src\                       归档状态、清除逻辑与设置页面
   ├─ lib\
   ├─ dist\
   ├─ test\
   ├─ scripts\
   └─ qa\
```

各插件的 `package.json` 定义包版本、DSH 声明及构建命令；`cordis.patch.yml` 注册宿主插件；`install.ps1` 安装对应打包版本；`NOTICE.md`、`LICENSE` 和 `licenses/` 保存来源与许可证。

`.research/` 是调研资料，`.sandbox/` 是隔离测试环境，`node_modules/` 是开发依赖。使用统计项目还可能有 `.preview/` 预览产物。这些目录和本机 `qa/` 验证记录均保存在本地。使用统计的隔离环境会复制本机真实会话。

## 本机环境与安装状态

当前适配和验证的宿主版本是 **DeepSeek Harness 0.2.2-rc.1**；开发需要 Node.js 24 或更新版本。宿主升级后需要重新检查插件接口，尤其是归档管理的内部兼容接口。

| 用途 | 本机路径 |
| --- | --- |
| DSH 桌面程序 | `D:\deepseek\DeepSeek Harness.exe` |
| DSH CLI | `D:\deepseek\resources\runtime\cli\bin\dsh.cmd` |
| 日常数据根目录 | `C:\Users\ASUS\.dsh` |
| 桌面 profile 声明 | `C:\Users\ASUS\.dsh\profiles\desktop\package.json` |
| 归档管理删除标记 | `C:\Users\ASUS\.dsh\storages\archive_manager_local.json` |

2026-11-10 已将两个插件从工作区目录链接切换为 `.tgz` 安装。运行文件位于 `C:\Users\ASUS\.dsh\profiles\desktop\node_modules\` 下各自的插件目录，不再链接工作区；工作区完整保留，没有在 DSH 下额外保存安装包备份。已核对安装文件与当前构建一致、插件入口可独立导入、用量记录未变。

本工作区新增插件的首次安装和已有插件的更新，都必须从带版本号的 `.tgz` 安装包安装到 DSH。可在 DSH「添加插件」对话框顶部填写 `.tgz` 文件的完整路径，也可运行对应的 `install.ps1`。

## 更新与交付

每批改动都必须提升所涉及插件的版本号。涉及多个插件时，各自提升版本号。安装和版本同步要求见 [工作区插件管理](AGENTS.md)。

以归档管理为例，修改源码后执行：

```powershell
Set-Location 'F:\dsh-youhua\dsh-archive-manager'
npm ci --ignore-scripts
npm test
npm run build
```

本机现采用安装包安装，DSH 加载自己的已安装文件。工作区源码修改或构建不会自动改变已安装版本；更新时需要重新打包、运行对应 `install.ps1` 安装，再完全退出并重新打开 DSH。只修改工作区说明文档不影响已安装插件。

发版时从工作区根目录运行发布脚本。脚本检查两个插件的版本声明、锁文件和安装路径，跑完测试再构建两个包。两个插件都内嵌同一份台账源码。

```powershell
Set-Location 'F:\dsh-youhua'
node scripts/release.mjs
```

脚本核对包内版本和运行文件，将安装包写入各自的 `dist/` 并更新 `SHA256SUMS.txt`。已有同版本包内容有差异时会要求升版。各插件的 `npm run pack:plugin` 仍可单独用于开发打包。

当前安装包为使用统计 1.2.4、归档管理 2.3.0。旧版本安装包保留为历史文件。

## 两个插件的数据关系

使用统计将每个会话的日期、模型、用量摘要与事件指纹保存到独立的 usage_stats_local 存储域。归档和删除均保留已保存的统计。归档管理在持有写占用及租约期间核对主日志和登记副本，先保存可核对的最新用量。用量分歧或保存失败时保留当前会话的日志。刷新、重启、重复删除不会重计同一会话。

普通会话可以从菜单直接确认删除。归档管理支持按搜索结果删除，也可单独删除子智能体。确认后才释放会话。待清理文件或子智能体有变化时，会展示更新后的清单并再次确认。已经开始的清理可在归档页续删。插件复核日志、副本及缓存，同步该批次的搜索索引后再标记完成。主日志或副本有异常用量时保留当前会话。已登记目录不可用时暂停清理。无法核验归属的损坏备份会显示路径并保留。用量、项目文件与共享附件会保留。未登记的外部备份和云端副本在检查范围之外。

两个插件的接口均面向本机回环访问，不支持通过远程 DSH 地址使用这些扩展功能。

## 测试与维护记录

| 项目 | 已有验证证据 | 查看位置 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 使用统计 | 26 项自动测试，覆盖汇总复用、删除前写入和跨日刷新 | 本机 `dsh-usage-stats/qa/验证记录.md` |
| 归档管理 | 46 项自动测试，覆盖备份目录掉线、批量进度、目录复用和新增副本保护 | 本机 `dsh-archive-manager/qa/验证记录.md` |

2026-11-09 15:54:11，用户在日常 DSH 执行两条会话的彻底删除；随后只读检查确认两条记录均有 `purgedAt` 完成标记，原日志不存在，会话目录为空，项目目录仍存在。这与开发阶段的隔离测试分开记录。

2026-11-10 已复跑两组共 39 项自动测试，并在真实 0.2.2-rc.1 隔离宿主中验证删除前保存、删除后重启、重复提交与项目文件保留。结果见 dsh-usage-stats/qa/retention-integration.json。另从已有隔离副本补回两条先前已删除会话的 18,753,845 Token，仅代表副本时点；未恢复聊天日志。

维护时先阅读对应 `项目说明.md` 和 `README.md`。统计口径问题查看聚合与图表模型；归档删除问题查看管理服务与日志清除适配。不要直接手改日常删除标记来尝试恢复已经清除的日志。

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# DSH 使用统计 1.2.4

项目实现与维护说明见 [项目说明.md](项目说明.md)，工作区导航见 [总说明](../README.md)。

直接参考 [ZCode 官方源码](https://github.com/zai-org/ZCode/tree/a9fe401eede6e6e5e01be9048679c206fe6f02d9/packages/ui/src/settings/usage-stats)，在 DSH 的 **设置 → 使用统计** 中展示本机用量。源码、构建产物和安装包均放在此独立文件夹。

## 已实现

- 删除会话后保留历史用量；独立存储摘要，重启后仍可查看。
- 累计 Token、单日峰值、最长聊天跨度、当前与最长连续使用天数。
- 52 周热力图：每日 / 每周 / 累计三种模式。
- 最近 7 / 30 日逐模型趋势，点击图例显隐，悬停查看用量。
- 同一时间范围内分别展示未缓存输入、输出、缓存读取和缓存写入 Token。
- 同一时间范围内的模型用量环形图、数量和比例。
- 跟随 DSH 深浅主题；适配窄设置面板；刷新、打开页面时更新、前台每 30 秒更新。
- 导出汇总 JSON；加载、空数据、读取异常和部分统计缺失状态。

不需要 API Key，不调用模型。统计汇总在本机进行；界面只访问本插件的同源回环端点。当前仅提供应用用量，没有接入个人套餐。

## 本机安装

当前目标版本：**DeepSeek Harness Desktop 0.2.2-rc.1**。已在相同版本的独立测试 profile 验证。其他 DSH 版本没有宣称兼容。

本机日常 desktop profile 使用 `.tgz` 安装包。首次安装或更新时，在 PowerShell 运行安装脚本。

```powershell
& 'F:\dsh-youhua\dsh-usage-stats\install.ps1'
```

或使用桌面版自带命令直接安装已构建的包：

```powershell
& 'D:\deepseek\resources\runtime\cli\bin\dsh.cmd' plugin --profile desktop add 'F:\dsh-youhua\dsh-usage-stats\dist\dsh-usage-stats-local-1.2.4.tgz'
```

然后完全退出并重新打开 DSH，在设置左侧点击「使用统计」。此插件不修改主程序 app.asar。

卸载可在 DSH 的插件管理页移除，或运行：

```powershell
& 'D:\deepseek\resources\runtime\cli\bin\dsh.cmd' plugin --profile desktop remove dsh-usage-stats-local
```

## 开发与验证

```powershell
npm ci --ignore-scripts
npm test
npm run build
npm run pack:plugin
node scripts/check-local-data.mjs
npm run preview
```

本地预览地址：`http://127.0.0.1:19420/`。默认使用核对脚本生成的本机汇总快照；`?demo` 是明确标注的模拟数据样式演示，`?empty` / `?error` 可检查空状态和错误状态。预览不会写入 DSH 配置。

`scripts/setup-sandbox.mjs` 建立 `.sandbox/home`，复制会话文件用于隔离验证，不复制账户凭据。用以下命令运行隔离宿主：

```powershell
node scripts/setup-sandbox.mjs
$env:DSH_HOME = 'F:\dsh-youhua\dsh-usage-stats\.sandbox\home'
& 'D:\deepseek\resources\runtime\cli\bin\dsh.cmd' web --port 19419 --no-open
```

此环境与 desktop 正式配置独立；停止测试进程后，在当前 PowerShell 清除该测试环境变量，避免后续命令指向测试目录：`Remove-Item Env:DSH_HOME`。

## 数据口径和限制

- 汇总当前 DSH_HOME 中已保存的会话用量摘要，包含已删除会话。升级前已删除且没有摘要或可核对副本的历史无法自动补回；未持久化的流式响应和未写入 assistant/message 的调用不计入，不等同于服务商账单。
- 以完成的 assistant/message.usage 为准，优先使用 totalTokens；缺失时累计 DSH 的输入、输出、缓存读、缓存写四个互斥桶。不会额外叠加流式 usage。
- 首次升级会重读仍有日志的会话以补齐明细。无法拆分的总量继续计入「未拆分」，包括只有总量的旧摘要、缺失分项对应的差额，以及分项和超过总量的记录。导出 JSON 的每日 `tokenBreakdown` 包含这四个字段和 `unclassifiedTokens`，缺省分项表示无可用记录。
- 根据宿主提供的 inheritedEventCount 排除分叉继承前缀。供应商和模型共同区分统计序列。
- 首次创建统计存储时固定宿主本地时区，之后按该时区的自然日统计。近 7 / 30 日包含今天；当前连续天数允许最后活跃日为昨天。
- 最长聊天时长是单会话首末活动跨度，包含等待时间，非模型生成耗时。
- 会话摘要按 revision 更新并持久化到 storages/usage_stats_local/，源日志消失后仍保留摘要。宿主启动和每 30 秒会更新，无需打开统计页。读取和汇总在共享写队列之外完成，写入前会核对 revision 和最新摘要。
- 台账、当前会话集合和统计日期均未变化时，刷新复用已算好的汇总。删除前写入的用量会使汇总失效，下次刷新会使用最新台账。
- 有效用量事件以指纹核对。旧前缀可以沿用现有摘要。日志与已保存记录出现分歧时，页面保留已有用量并报告受影响的会话数。旧格式摘要按已有日期、模型和分项核对，可核对的日志会补上指纹。
- 配合归档管理 2.3.0，彻底删除前核对主日志和登记的备份，并保存可核对的最终总量及明细。主日志或副本含异常用量时会暂停清理当前会话。手工或其他程序直接删文件只能保留最后一次成功保存的用量。
- 个别会话无法读取时显示「统计不完整」，不静默伪装为完整总额。导出只包含汇总，不含聊天正文。
- 访问入口限制为本机回环、同源、GET 和专用请求头。远程访问 DSH 时本插件不提供统计。

## 文件

`src/` 源码；`lib/` 可加载插件；`dist/` 安装包；`test/` 聚合与接口测试；`qa/` 验证报告及截图；`scripts/` 构建和预览工具；`.research/` 本地调研资料（不打包）；`.sandbox/` 隔离测试数据（不打包）。

许可证与参考文件见 NOTICE.md。插件不使用 dsh-scope。

# DSH 本地插件工作区说明

更新日期：2026-11-11。

本工作区用于开发和维护 DeepSeek Harness 的本地插件。目前包含「使用统计」和「归档管理」两个独立项目，功能和界面参考 ZCode 官方项目，没有采用 dsh-scope。插件通过 DSH 扩展机制加载，不修改主程序 `app.asar`。

## 插件导航

| 项目 | 包名与当前版本 | DSH 入口 | 主要用途 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [使用统计项目说明](dsh-usage-stats/项目说明.md) | `dsh-usage-stats-local` 1.2.4 | 设置 → 使用统计 | 本机会话 Token 总量与四项明细、活动热力图、模型趋势与占比 |
| [归档管理项目说明](dsh-archive-manager/项目说明.md) | `dsh-archive-manager-local` 2.3.0 | 对话顶部、侧栏会话菜单、设置 → 归档管理 | 停止后直接删除，支持筛选删除、清理进度、子智能体清理和中断后续删 |

两个项目可以分别构建、安装和卸载，不要求同时启用。工作区根目录没有统一的 npm 工程，开发命令应在对应插件文件夹执行。

## 目录结构

```text
F:\dsh-youhua\
├─ README.md                      工作区总说明
├─ dsh-usage-stats\               使用统计插件
│  ├─ 项目说明.md                 功能、实现、维护与验证说明
│  ├─ README.md                   安装与使用指南
│  ├─ src\                       后端统计与前端页面源码
│  ├─ lib\                       DSH 实际加载的构建产物
│  ├─ dist\                      tgz 安装包和 SHA-256
│  ├─ test\                      自动测试
│  ├─ scripts\                   构建、预览、数据核对与隔离环境工具
│  └─ qa\                        测试记录、汇总快照和截图
└─ dsh-archive-manager\           归档管理插件
   ├─ 项目说明.md
   ├─ README.md
   ├─ src\                       归档状态、清除逻辑与设置页面
   ├─ lib\
   ├─ dist\
   ├─ test\
   ├─ scripts\
   └─ qa\
```

各插件的 `package.json` 定义包版本、DSH 声明及构建命令；`cordis.patch.yml` 注册宿主插件；`install.ps1` 安装对应打包版本；`NOTICE.md`、`LICENSE` 和 `licenses/` 保存来源与许可证。

`.research/` 是调研资料，`.sandbox/` 是隔离测试环境，`node_modules/` 是开发依赖。使用统计项目还可能有 `.preview/` 预览产物。这些目录和本机 `qa/` 验证记录均保存在本地。使用统计的隔离环境会复制本机真实会话。

## 本机环境与安装状态

当前适配和验证的宿主版本是 **DeepSeek Harness 0.2.2-rc.1**；开发需要 Node.js 24 或更新版本。宿主升级后需要重新检查插件接口，尤其是归档管理的内部兼容接口。

| 用途 | 本机路径 |
| --- | --- |
| DSH 桌面程序 | `D:\deepseek\DeepSeek Harness.exe` |
| DSH CLI | `D:\deepseek\resources\runtime\cli\bin\dsh.cmd` |
| 日常数据根目录 | `C:\Users\ASUS\.dsh` |
| 桌面 profile 声明 | `C:\Users\ASUS\.dsh\profiles\desktop\package.json` |
| 归档管理删除标记 | `C:\Users\ASUS\.dsh\storages\archive_manager_local.json` |

2026-11-10 已将两个插件从工作区目录链接切换为 `.tgz` 安装。运行文件位于 `C:\Users\ASUS\.dsh\profiles\desktop\node_modules\` 下各自的插件目录，不再链接工作区；工作区完整保留，没有在 DSH 下额外保存安装包备份。已核对安装文件与当前构建一致、插件入口可独立导入、用量记录未变。

本工作区新增插件的首次安装和已有插件的更新，都必须从带版本号的 `.tgz` 安装包安装到 DSH。可在 DSH「添加插件」对话框顶部填写 `.tgz` 文件的完整路径，也可运行对应的 `install.ps1`。

## 更新与交付

每批改动都必须提升所涉及插件的版本号。涉及多个插件时，各自提升版本号。安装和版本同步要求见 [工作区插件管理](AGENTS.md)。

以归档管理为例，修改源码后执行：

```powershell
Set-Location 'F:\dsh-youhua\dsh-archive-manager'
npm ci --ignore-scripts
npm test
npm run build
```

本机现采用安装包安装，DSH 加载自己的已安装文件。工作区源码修改或构建不会自动改变已安装版本；更新时需要重新打包、运行对应 `install.ps1` 安装，再完全退出并重新打开 DSH。只修改工作区说明文档不影响已安装插件。

发版时从工作区根目录运行发布脚本。脚本检查两个插件的版本声明、锁文件和安装路径，跑完测试再构建两个包。两个插件都内嵌同一份台账源码。

```powershell
Set-Location 'F:\dsh-youhua'
node scripts/release.mjs
```

脚本核对包内版本和运行文件，将安装包写入各自的 `dist/` 并更新 `SHA256SUMS.txt`。已有同版本包内容有差异时会要求升版。各插件的 `npm run pack:plugin` 仍可单独用于开发打包。

当前安装包为使用统计 1.2.4、归档管理 2.3.0。旧版本安装包保留为历史文件。

## 两个插件的数据关系

使用统计将每个会话的日期、模型、用量摘要与事件指纹保存到独立的 usage_stats_local 存储域。归档和删除均保留已保存的统计。归档管理在持有写占用及租约期间核对主日志和登记副本，先保存可核对的最新用量。用量分歧或保存失败时保留当前会话的日志。刷新、重启、重复删除不会重计同一会话。

普通会话可以从菜单直接确认删除。归档管理支持按搜索结果删除，也可单独删除子智能体。确认后才释放会话。待清理文件或子智能体有变化时，会展示更新后的清单并再次确认。已经开始的清理可在归档页续删。插件复核日志、副本及缓存，同步该批次的搜索索引后再标记完成。主日志或副本有异常用量时保留当前会话。已登记目录不可用时暂停清理。无法核验归属的损坏备份会显示路径并保留。用量、项目文件与共享附件会保留。未登记的外部备份和云端副本在检查范围之外。

两个插件的接口均面向本机回环访问，不支持通过远程 DSH 地址使用这些扩展功能。

## 测试与维护记录

| 项目 | 已有验证证据 | 查看位置 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 使用统计 | 26 项自动测试，覆盖汇总复用、删除前写入和跨日刷新 | 本机 `dsh-usage-stats/qa/验证记录.md` |
| 归档管理 | 46 项自动测试，覆盖备份目录掉线、批量进度、目录复用和新增副本保护 | 本机 `dsh-archive-manager/qa/验证记录.md` |

2026-11-09 15:54:11，用户在日常 DSH 执行两条会话的彻底删除；随后只读检查确认两条记录均有 `purgedAt` 完成标记，原日志不存在，会话目录为空，项目目录仍存在。这与开发阶段的隔离测试分开记录。

2026-11-10 已复跑两组共 39 项自动测试，并在真实 0.2.2-rc.1 隔离宿主中验证删除前保存、删除后重启、重复提交与项目文件保留。结果见 dsh-usage-stats/qa/retention-integration.json。另从已有隔离副本补回两条先前已删除会话的 18,753,845 Token，仅代表副本时点；未恢复聊天日志。

维护时先阅读对应 `项目说明.md` 和 `README.md`。统计口径问题查看聚合与图表模型；归档删除问题查看管理服务与日志清除适配。不要直接手改日常删除标记来尝试恢复已经清除的日志。

## 开源许可

本仓库的原创代码采用 Apache License 2.0，完整条款见 [LICENSE](LICENSE)。

上游署名和第三方依赖的许可信息见各插件的 `NOTICE.md` 和 `licenses/` 目录。[使用统计声明](dsh-usage-stats/NOTICE.md) · [归档管理声明](dsh-archive-manager/NOTICE.md)

# dsh-up-session 简体中文 | [English](./README.en.md) 一个简单的 DeepSeek Harness 侧边栏插件：在「工作区」列表顶部插入「置顶」和「最近」两个分组，把分散在各个工作区里的置顶会话汇总到一处，也把最近的会话收拢到一处。

## 安装与兼容 **建议升级到 DSH 0.2.2-alpha.3 以上版本，本插件使用该版本提供的会话菜单接口。** 插件 1.1.0 的 DSH 兼容版本为 `>=0.2.2-alpha.3`，在更早的 DSH 版本上安装可能导致 DSH 无法启动。 **Web 端** ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-up-session ``` 安装后重启 DSH。如果使用自定义 profile，将命令中的 `web` 替换为对应名称。 **桌面端** 打开侧边栏「插件」，点击「添加插件」，输入 `dsh-up-session`，安装完成后点击「立即启用」。 ### 在旧版 DSH 上安装 1.0.3 如果你的 DSH 版本早于 0.2.2-alpha.3，且符合插件 1.0.3 的兼容范围 `>=0.2.1-rc.2`，请指定版本安装 `dsh-up-session@1.0.3`。 **Web 端** ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-up-session@1.0.3 ``` 安装后重启 DSH。如果使用自定义 profile，将命令中的 `web` 替换为对应名称。 **桌面端** 打开侧边栏「插件」，点击「添加插件」，输入 `dsh-up-session@1.0.3`，安装完成后点击「立即启用」。 ## 置顶区 汇总所有工作区里被置顶的会话，按最近更新时间排序，可展开收起。每行悬停时出现归档和取消置顶两个按钮。 在置顶区或最近区的会话行上右键，或聚焦该行后按菜单键 / Shift+F10，会打开与工作区列表相同的会话菜单（置顶或取消置顶、重命名、分叉会话、复制 Session ID、在文件管理器中显示、归档）。这些菜单项由宿主注册，因此和下面工作区里的同一条会话保持一致。插件还在「在文件夹显示」下方增加「在原位置显示」：点击后展开所属工作区（包括工作区树中收起的祖先和会话的「展开更多」），并将列表滚动到原会话行，以 DSH 当前主题主色进行三秒的背景渐显渐隐提示，颜色随主题变化；此操作不受「展开工作区中的原会话」设置影响。重命名对话框预填的是会话自己的标题，未命名会话不会被填成「未命名」。 置顶区和最近区都位于「工作区」列表顶部，是该列表的前两个分组，会和下方的工作区分组一起滚动；使用「工作区」的搜索功能时，两个区暂时隐藏，把列表让给搜索结果。 ## 最近区 位于置顶区与工作区列表之间，按最近更新时间排序显示尚未置顶的会话，默认显示最新的 5 条，样式与置顶区一致，同样可以展开收起。默认展示多少条可在设置中调整（1–50），「展开更多」每次固定增加 5 条。会话多于当前显示的条数时，列表底部出现「展开更多」： - 每点一次「展开更多」再显示 5 条； - 全部会话都显示完后，按钮变为「收起」； - 点击「收起」把列表收回到默认展示的条数。 每行悬停时出现归档、置顶和「从最近隐藏」三个按钮。右键菜单与置顶区相同。已置顶的会话只出现在置顶区，两区不会重复显示同一个会话。 ## 从最近隐藏 每条最近区会话的行尾都有一个「从最近隐藏」按钮（悬停时出现，使用眼睛加斜线图标，排在归档和置顶右侧）。点一下，这条会话从最近区消失，但它仍然留在原来的工作区里：位置、标题、历史、置顶与归档状态都不变。 插件只记住「隐藏那一刻该会话的活动时间」。之后你在工作区里打开它、发一条新消息，活动时间被推进，它就会自动回到最近区，不需要任何额外操作。 隐藏记录存在浏览器本地，只含会话编号和那一刻的时间，不含标题与内容；换浏览器或清缓存后不再生效，这也说明它不会改动你的会话数据。误点了可以在设置里一键全部放回。 ## 会话悬浮卡片 鼠标在置顶区或最近区的会话行上停留约 0.8 秒，行右侧会弹出与工作区列表一致的会话悬浮卡片：完整的会话标题、工作目录、相对时间和当前状态。空闲时会显示「空闲」；等待回应或子智能体运行时逐行列出。卡片还会在标题下多显示一行该会话所属工作区的标题，会跟随工作区重命名而变化，而不是项目目录名。 卡片里的时间和状态与工作区列表读同一份数据；从一行移到相邻会话行时卡片会立即切换，移开后收起。触摸设备没有悬停，不会弹出卡片。 ## 设置 「置顶」和「最近」的标题栏右侧各有一个齿轮按钮，鼠标移到标题栏上才出现；点击后打开本插件的设置弹窗，样式沿用 DSH 原生设置页。 也可以从侧边栏「插件 → 已安装插件 → dsh-up-session」进入插件详情页，点击「打开设置」打开同一个设置弹窗。 目前有四项设置： - **显示置顶**（默认开启）：显示或隐藏整个置顶区。 - **显示最近**（默认开启）：显示或隐藏整个最近区。两个列表可以同时关闭，之后仍可通过原生插件详情页的「打开设置」重新开启。 - **展开工作区中的原会话**（默认开启）：从置顶区或最近区点击会话时，同时展开它在工作区列表中所在的分组，让原生会话行可见。关闭后只打开会话，不改变工作区的展开状态。 - **最近区默认展示的会话数**（默认 5）：最近区默认显示最新的多少条会话。可填 1–50，超出范围会被拉回到最近的边界值。输入后按回车或离开输入框才生效，输入框右侧的上下按键每点一次增减 1。「展开更多」每次固定增加 5 条，不受这个数量影响。 另外，设置里还有一行「已隐藏的会话」，显示当前从最近区隐藏了多少条，右侧按钮可以把它们一次性全部放回。没有隐藏记录时这一行不显示按钮。 ## 许可 本项目基于 [MIT 许可证](./LICENSE) 授权。

decision.reason: Held for public installation mapping. MIT and engines.dsh at least 0.2.2-alpha.3 are explicit; the no-op host plus real client is a native UI plugin. The README advertises npm installation, but that exact package/version returned 404. Public installation identity remains unresolved. No candidate code or lifecycle hooks were executed; runtime safety and compatibility are unproven.
