evidence.readmeExcerpt:
Oh My Claude

English | 中文

Claude Code, native inside dsh

Drive your logged-in Claude Code CLI as a first-class dsh provider: no API key, no extra services, no runtime dependencies.

Built with AI assistance, and open to more. Contributions from AI coding agents are welcome; start with CONTRIBUTING.md.

--- Claude Code CLI as an LLM provider for [dsh](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/dsh). Every request drives `claude -p` with stream-json in and out, so it uses whatever login, hooks, CLAUDE.md files, MCP servers and rate limits Claude Code already has. No API key needed. The plugin speaks the CLI's own protocol (the one the Agent SDK wraps) directly, so it has no runtime dependencies. ## Tour

The shield is dsh's own control. In a Claude session its rows become Claude's six permission modes, each labelled with the dsh access level it sets underneath.

One `✻` button beside the composer opens the whole plugin: Memory, Instructions, Skills, Rewind, Changes, MCP, Asides, Diagnostics, Tasks and Tune, plus a Restore tab while the session is still blank.

Cost and cached token count, two figures dsh cannot compute, join dsh's footer stats row. The pill turns orange once a session passes the spend line you set. The dollar figures are what the turns would cost at API rates; on a Claude subscription you are not billed them.

Plan usage and the CLI's own context breakdown live in dsh's context ring popover. On a phone the panel becomes a sheet.

Once an SSH box is saved, dsh's own Add workspace dialog gains a box dropdown: a folder on that box becomes a workspace here, and the session in it runs Claude Code there. Shots by tools/playwright/tour.ts. ## Install You need the Claude Code CLI on `PATH` and logged in (`claude --version` works, `claude` opens without asking you to sign in), and dsh 0.2 (0.2.2-alpha.2 or newer). On dsh 0.2.0 or 0.2.1, install 1.5.14 (`dsh-oh-my-claude@dsh-0.2.1`); on dsh 0.1.x, install the npm tag for your line from the Compatibility table below. Nothing else: no API key, no Node build step. **From dsh's Plugins page**, in the web app or DSH Desktop: 1. Open **Plugins** in the sidebar and press **Add plugin**. 2. Enter `dsh-oh-my-claude` and press **Install**. 3. Press **Enable now**, or turn on its switch later under **Installed plugins**. It loads without a restart. Reload the page and "Oh My Claude" appears in the model picker with the models your login can use. Pick one and chat. **From a terminal**, then restart dsh however you run it: ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-oh-my-claude systemctl --user restart dsh-web.service ``` To install straight from the repository instead of npm, use `github:lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude` as the package name in either route. The plugin speaks English and Chinese and follows dsh's own language setting (Settings → General → Language), switching as soon as you change it. If the picker lists it as `Oh My Claude (not logged in)`, run `claude auth login` in a terminal on the box that runs dsh, or press Log in under Settings → Oh My Claude → Boxes. **DSH Desktop** (macOS and Windows) uses the Plugins page steps above. The plugin looks for `claude` in the usual install folders, since an app started from the Dock does not see your shell's PATH. On Windows it runs Claude as a plain child of dsh, so restarting the app ends a running turn, and the parts that need a Unix shell (Log in from Settings, SSH boxes) are not available. The server half has run under Electron on Linux the way Desktop runs it, and on Windows 11 with Claude Code installed from npm. When a newer version is on npm, an orange pill with the version number appears in Settings and on the panel's Runtime line. A click opens Oh My Claude on dsh's Plugins page, where dsh's own Update button installs it; the copy button beside the pill puts the update command on the clipboard for a terminal. DSH Desktop gets the pill too, without the copy button, since its CLI has no command to copy. Details, and the repairs the plugin makes on its own after a dsh upgrade, are under [Plugin updates](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/how-it-works.md#plugin-updates). Optional, in `~/.dsh/settings.yaml`: ```yaml agent-default-model: # make Claude Code the default for new sessions provider: claude-code model: claude-fable-5-1 # any model id the picker lists subagent-model-selection: # let dsh subagents run on Claude Code too enabled: true allowedModels: - provider: claude-code model: claude-haiku-5-5 # any model id the picker lists ``` Working on the plugin itself? Start at [docs/developing.md](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/developing.md). ## Compatibility dsh ships prereleases only and moves client APIs between them, so every release of the plugin records the dsh line it was written for and the dsh it was driven on. "Runs on" is the range the code carries branches for; "tested on" is the dsh installed on the box when the release was cut. The update pill reads the floor off the registry: a box whose dsh is below it is never offered the update command, and the pill names the dsh that release needs instead. | Plugin | Runs on dsh | Tested on dsh | npm tag | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 1.6.2 | 0.2.2-alpha.2 through 0.2.2-rc.1 | 0.2.2-rc.1 | `latest` | | 1.6.1 | 0.2.2-alpha.2 through 0.2.2-rc.1 | 0.2.2-rc.1 | none, superseded by 1.6.2 | | 1.6.0 | 0.2.2-alpha.2 through 0.2.2-rc.1 | 0.2.2-rc.1 | none, superseded by 1.6.1 | | 1.5.14 | 0.2.0-rc.1 through 0.2.2-rc.1 | 0.2.2-rc.1 | `dsh-0.2.1`, `dsh-0.2` | | 1.5.13 | 0.2.0-rc.1 through 0.2.2-rc.1 | 0.2.2-rc.1 | none, superseded by 1.5.14 | | 1.5.12 | 0.2.0-rc.1 through 0.2.2-alpha.2 | 0.2.2-alpha.2 | none, superseded by 1.5.13 | | 1.5.11 | 0.2.0-rc.1 through 0.2.2-alpha.2 | 0.2.2-alpha.2 | none, superseded by 1.5.12 | | 1.5.10 | 0.2.0-rc.1 through 0.2.2-alpha.2 | 0.2.2-alpha.2 | none, superseded by 1.5.11 | | 1.5.9 | 0.2.0-rc.1 through 0.2.1-rc.4 | 0.2.1-rc.4 | none, superseded by 1.5.10 | | 1.5.8 | 0.2.0-rc.1 through 0.2.1-rc.4 | 0.2.1-rc.4 | none, superseded by 1.5.9 | | 1.5.7 | 0.2.0-rc.1 through 0.2.1-rc.3 | 0.2.1-rc.3 | none, superseded by 1.5.8 | | 1.5.6 | 0.2.0-rc.1 through 0.2.1-rc.3 | 0.2.1-rc.3 | none, superseded by 1.5.7 | | 1.5.5 | 0.2.0-rc.1 through 0.2.1-rc.2 | 0.2.1-rc.2 | none, superseded by 1.5.6 | | 1.5.4 | 0.2.0-rc.1 through 0.2.1-rc.2 | 0.2.1-rc.2 | none, superseded by 1.5.5 | | 1.5.3 | 0.2.0-rc.1 through 0.2.1-alpha.1 | 0.2.1-alpha.1 | none, superseded by 1.5.4 | | 1.5.2 | 0.2.0-rc.1 through 0.2.0-rc.2 | 0.2.0-rc.2 | none, superseded by 1.5.3 | | 1.4.2 | 0.1.5-rc.1 through 0.1.7-rc.2 | 0.1.7-rc.2 | `dsh-0.1.7` | | 1.4.1 | 0.1.5-rc.1 through 0.1.7-rc.2 | 0.1.7-rc.2 | none, superseded by 1.4.2 | | 1.4.0 | 0.1.5-rc.1 through 0.1.7-rc.2 | 0.1.7-rc.2 | none, superseded by 1.4.1 | | 1.3.1 | 0.1.5-rc.1 through 0.1.6-alpha.2 | 0.1.6-alpha.2 | `dsh-0.1.6` | | 1.2.1 | 0.1.5-rc.1 through 0.1.6-alpha.2 | 0.1.6-alpha.2 | `dsh-0.1.5` | ## What you get 1. Any Claude model your login can use, in dsh's own picker. Hide the ones you don't use with a switch in Settings, or with `hiddenModels` in the plugin config. Add one the lineup doesn't list, such as a name your local router sends to another model, in the same Settings block or with `customModels`. The menu follows the router: switch one such as CC Switch on and it lists the router's models, switch it off and Claude's are back, with no reload. [Models](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/how-it-works.md#models) 2. Every dsh session resumes its Claude Code session, tool history included, and a terminal `claude /resume` sees the same one. [Sessions](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/how-it-works.md#sessions) 3. Restart dsh without killing a running Claude turn. [Restarts](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/how-it-works.md#restarts) 4. dsh's access shield sets Claude's six permission modes per session. [Permission mode](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/how-it-works.md#permission-mode-per-session) 5. Claude's permission prompts, questions and plan reviews become dsh dialogs, each option's preview under the question. [Approvals](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/how-it-works.md#approvals-and-questions) 6. One spark button opens Memory, Rewind, Changes, MCP and seven more tabs, all reachable from the keyboard. [The panel](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/panel.md) 7. Cost and cached tokens in dsh's footer, with a spend line that turns the pill orange. [Cost pill](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/panel.md#cost-pill) 8. Plan usage (5-hour, weekly, extra usage) in dsh's context ring, which turns amber near a limit and red at one, with a notice above the composer. Only limits the session's model counts against, graded by Anthropic, so a new model needs no update. [Plan usage](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/panel.md#plan-usage) 9. Restore or import any past Claude transcript, from dsh or from a terminal, and search inside them for what was said. [Session browser](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/panel.md#session-browser) 10. Claude's slash commands and skills show up in dsh's slash menu under their own names, as `/claude-` where dsh already uses the name. A skill dsh also serves runs on any model, and so does one only Claude Code has: typed in a session on another model, it goes to that model with its instructions (switch it off in Settings). [Command bridge](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/how-it-works.md#command-bridge) 11. Claude gets dsh's subagents, jobs, goals and web search over MCP. It can also open a new dsh session, send it follow-ups and read its replies (`open_session`, `prompt_session`, `wait_session`). [dsh tools over MCP](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/how-it-works.md#dsh-tools-over-mcp) 12. Edit CLAUDE.md, settings.json and MCP servers from the panel, on this box or a remote one, and sign in to an MCP server that needs it. [Instructions](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/panel.md#instructions), [settings.json editor](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/panel.md#settingsjson-editor), [MCP](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/panel.md#mcp) 13. Run Claude on another box over SSH, or mount several accounts. [Remote boxes and accounts](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/remote.md) 14. Report a problem with a redacted box report, copied or filed as an issue. [Report a problem](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/panel.md#report-a-problem) 15. All the orange is a switch, per group, any colour. [Claude look](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/panel.md#claude-look) 16. Pick what dsh adds to your prompts, with the size of each block on the label. [dsh context](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/panel.md#dsh-context) 17. A card offers each new Claude Code release for the box a session runs on, and installs it from dsh; a headless `claude -p` never updates itself. Channel, auto-install and history per box sit under the switch in Settings. [Claude Code updates](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/how-it-works.md#surviving-claude-code-updates) 18. What the last five versions changed, read from the plugin's own changelog, in Settings. [Changelog](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/panel.md#changelog) 19. Every skill the CLI can reach, grouped by scope, with add, edit and remove for your own and the project's. What each costs, from the CLI's own `/skill-doctor`, is a table you can sort, beside what else drives your usage: the MCP servers behind the most requests, and how the work was shaped. [Skills](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/panel.md#skills) 20. A mark on the browser tab and an optional desktop notice when a session you are not looking at finishes, or stops to ask you something. [Session notices](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/panel.md#session-notices) 21. dsh's own goal and every earlier goal of the session, beside Claude Code's goal and its scheduled tasks. [Tasks](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/panel.md#tasks) 22. Edit or remove a message you steered in while Claude works, or all of them as one, until Claude reads it. A file or image on the message stays on it; only the text changes. Nothing goes out while you edit. Send now stops Claude and sends one as the next turn. [Steering](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/how-it-works.md#dsh-tools-over-mcp) 23. Claude's working line (spinner, verb, figures) repeats above the composer once you scroll up past it, so reading back through a long turn never hides what Claude is doing. A switch in Settings turns it off. [Turn status](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/how-it-works.md#turn-status) 24. Select text in a reply and dsh's popover (dsh 0.2.2) shows Ask beside its Quote text, or on a phone a row above the composer does: ask Claude about the passage as a side question that leaves the conversation alone; ask with the question blank and Claude explains the passage. [Asides](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/panel.md#asides) 25. A finished turn keeps a closing line where the working verb was, the way the terminal ends one: `✻ Crunched for 27s · done 3:21 AM`. A turn you stopped reads `Interrupted · What should Claude do instead?`. [Turn status](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/how-it-works.md#turn-status) 26. Claude's tool calls show as dsh's own tool cards, the way every other provider's do, with the text streaming between them. Inline text is a switch away in Settings ("Native tool rows"). [Native tool rows](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/panel.md#native-tool-rows) 27. A new session in a workspace opens on the Claude box, model and effort that workspace last ran, and a workspace with nothing remembered opens on a default model and effort you pick. [Remember model per workspace](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/panel.md#remember-model-per-workspace) 28. After each reply, Claude's guess at your next prompt shows above the composer: Use writes it into the box, Send sends it as it is, and it folds away while you type something else. On by default, as in the terminal; a switch in Settings turns it off. [Suggested next prompt](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/panel.md#suggested-next-prompt) 29. Claude's background shell tasks and subagents are listed on the Tasks tab while they run, each with Stop and, for a shell task, Output, plus Stop all once two or more run. A shell task that ended keeps its row and its Output for the last ten; the subagents a session already ran sit under Earlier subagents, each openable as Markdown. A subagent's row in the chat names each step as the CLI reports it. [Tasks](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/panel.md#tasks) 30. If an `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in dsh's environment is what Claude Code bills instead of your login, the session says so in one line at its start. [Where things live](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/how-it-works.md#where-things-live) 31. Each plan window says where it is heading at the current rate: the percent it ends at, or when the cap lands. [Plan usage](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/panel.md#plan-usage) 32. Once the context window is 75% full (adjustable in Settings), a card above the composer says so and offers Compact, which sends Claude's own `/compact`. [Context nudge](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/panel.md#context-nudge) 33. A Run button on every shell snippet Claude writes puts it in the composer as a prompt; Enter sends it, and it runs through Claude's Bash tool and dsh's approval. [Run a snippet](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/panel.md#run-a-snippet) 34. A session renamed in dsh keeps that name in `claude --resume`, and a name set on the Claude side renames the dsh session. [Command bridge](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/how-it-works.md#command-bridge) 35. Switch a session between Claude and another model, such as DeepSeek or a local one, and back: Claude sees the prompts, replies and tool use the other model had in between. [Sessions](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/how-it-works.md#sessions) 36. Up in an empty composer brings back your last prompt, Up again older ones, Down newer ones and back to empty, as in the Claude Code terminal; typing a character ends the walk. A new session recalls from the workspace's latest transcript. Switch it off under Settings ("Prompt recall"). 37. Ctrl+R in the composer searches the prompts typed before: this session, the workspace or everywhere on the box (Ctrl+S or Ctrl+Up/Down cycles). Enter sends the row, Tab writes it into the composer, Esc closes. Switch it off under Settings ("History search"). 38. Esc Esc in an empty composer while nothing runs opens the Rewind tab on the latest prompt, as the terminal's double Escape opens /rewind; after the rewind that prompt is back in the composer to edit and resend. Switch it off under Settings ("Edit last prompt"). The three composer gestures are listed in dsh's Keyboard shortcuts dialog too. 39. Three commands of the plugin's own: `/btw ` asks Claude a side question without adding to the conversation, `/temporary` keeps no Claude transcript for the session, and `/ultracode` turns Claude Code's ultracode on or off without a relaunch. [Asides](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/panel.md#asides), [Temporary sessions](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/how-it-works.md#temporary-sessions), [Ultracode](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/how-it-works.md#ultracode) Defaults you never have to touch, such as secret redaction in tool results and surviving the CLI's own updates, are on [How it works](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/how-it-works.md). ## Configure Settings come in two kinds. The switches under Settings → Oh My Claude and in the panel's Tune tab are saved at once and kept on the box, so every browser sees the same ones. A Tune row reaches Claude when its process next starts. The keys below are install-time: they go as `config:` on the bundle row in the profile's `cordis.patch.yml` and take effect when dsh next loads the plugin, which a dsh restart does. dsh's own Plugins page lists the plugin with an on/off switch but has no form for these keys. Three keys people change first: ```yaml permissionMode: dsh # follow the session's shield (default), or pin one of the CLI's six modes # spawn: node # unset: the Settings switch below decides; node or dsh here wins sshHost: "" # "[user@]host" drives a claude on another machine over ssh ``` Every key, with its default, is in [docs/configuration.md](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/configuration.md). ### Keep Claude running across dsh restarts This switch under Settings → Oh My Claude picks how Claude Code is started, and it is on unless you turn it off. `spawn: node` or `spawn: dsh` in the config overrides it and locks the switch; `spawn: keeper` leaves it free. A flip reaches each session on its next turn. | | On (`keeper`) | Off (`dsh`) | `node` (config only) | |---|---|---|---| | A turn running when dsh restarts | Keeps running; the new dsh reattaches and shows what it did | Ends; about ten seconds after the restart the session gets a "dsh restarted while this turn was in progress" prompt and carries on | Same as off | | Left running after dsh exits | Claude, until it has gone `processIdleMs` (30 min, never under 5 min) with no dsh attached and no output | Nothing after a normal shutdown: dsh ends Claude and everything it started | Claude ends when dsh does; what it started is not tracked | | dsh's environment | Passed whole | Passed whole except `DSH_*` names: dsh's seam drops names with KEY, TOKEN, SECRET or PASSWORD, and the plugin passes them back | Passed whole | | SSH boxes and remote workspaces | The far `claude` is held on the box and survives too; the idle limit above does not reach it, so it runs until a dsh reattaches or the box restarts | The far `claude` ends with the ssh connection | Same as off | | Platforms | Linux and macOS; Windows runs `node` | All; `node` when dsh mounts no subprocess seam | All | DSH Web and DSH Desktop run separate dsh profiles, so each reattaches only to the Claude processes it started. Two dsh started on the same profile directory still share them. ## Remote boxes and accounts Mount the plugin twice with different `configDir` values for two logins. List other boxes running dsh and this plugin under Settings → Oh My Claude → Boxes and jump between them. Or give a box a name and `user@host` and drive the `claude` there over SSH, with nothing on the far side but the CLI; Tailscale and WireGuard peers appear as hosts to pick from. All of it is on [docs/remote.md](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/remote.md). ## What it touches - **Runs** the `claude` binary you already have, on this box or on one you add over SSH. - **Reads** Claude Code's login (`~/.claude/.credentials.json`, on macOS the `Claude Code-credentials` Keychain entry when that file has no live token, or `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` when set) to fetch the model list and your plan usage. That token goes only to `api.anthropic.com`. - **Writes** its own state under `~/.local/state/dsh-oh-my-claude/`; login tokens for SSH boxes are files only you can read. CLAUDE.md, settings.json and MCP servers change only when you edit them from the panel. - **Listens** on a Unix socket for the keeper that holds Claude across a dsh restart. Its HTTP routes live inside dsh's own server, so on DSH Web it opens no TCP port. Under DSH Desktop, whose web server answers 403 to anything but its own window, the bridge that hands dsh's tools to Claude also listens on 127.0.0.1, behind the same key. - **Calls out** to `api.anthropic.com` (models, plan usage), `status.anthropic.com`, `downloads.claude.ai` (the CLI's release pointer), `registry.npmjs.org` (plugin update check) and `api.github.com` (the repo's star count). SSH goes only to boxes you add. ## Not covered - dsh's shell and file tools are not proxied (except `bash` for background jobs); Claude Code uses its own, under its own permission mode. - Claude Code sessions are not deleted when dsh sessions are. ## Bugs and feedback Found a bug, or something that reads wrong? Open an issue at [github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/issues](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/issues) with the dsh and Claude Code versions (`dsh --version`, `claude --version`) and what you expected to see. Settings → Oh My Claude → Report a problem writes that report for you. ## License [MIT](LICENSE). Claude, Claude Code and the Claude spark mark are trademarks of Anthropic, PBC. This project is an independent dsh plugin that drives the Claude Code CLI you already have; it is not made, endorsed or supported by Anthropic. The spark is drawn here only to say which sessions and controls belong to Claude Code, in the way the CLI itself draws it.

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
dsh-hero-theme

A HeroUI v3 theme builder for DeepSeek Harness Web and the embedded Desktop workspace.
Six live controls regenerate the complete DSH token layer — no rebuild, no profile restart.

English · 中文

## Preview

Preview renders of the generated light and dark palettes in a representative DSH layout.

## Highlights | | | | --- | --- | | **Six live controls** | Accent hue, Base chroma, Font Family, Radius, Radius Form, Light / Dark / System. | | **167 tokens × 2 schemes** | Every alias, specific, Shiki, radius, shadow and timing token is regenerated from the config. | | **HeroUI builder formulas** | Accent `oklch(62.04% 0.195 hue)`, neutral chroma scaling, semantic hue rotation, radius scale. | | **Component geometry** | HeroUI Slider, Tabs, Select, Button, MenuSurface, Dialog and Tooltip geometry plus enter/exit motion. | | **No rebuild loop** | Changes apply through one `ctx.theme.overrideTokens()` layer and persist to the profile Cordis patch. | | **Reduced motion aware** | All added transitions and enter/exit animations stop under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`. | ## Theme builder

Settings → General → HeroUI theme. The sliders, Tabs and Select are HeroUI-styled controls.

| Control | Range | Default | What it changes | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Accent | hue `0–360` | `253.83` | Accent `oklch(62.04% 0.195 hue)` (`#0485F7` at the default), focus ring, gradient start | | Base | chroma `0–0.02` | `0.0015` | Chroma of every neutral (background, surfaces, text, borders) | | Font Family | Inter / System UI / Geist / Manrope / IBM Plex Sans / JetBrains Mono | Inter | `--dsw-font-family` and the brand stack | | Radius | `0–1.25rem` | `0.5rem` (8px) | HeroUI radius scale and card radius (`3×`) | | Radius Form | `0–1.5rem` | `0.75rem` (12px) | Inputs and form fields | | Theme | Light / Dark / System | Dark | Base color scheme and `ctx.theme.setTheme()` | The default accent is HeroUI blue `#0485F7` at hue `253.83`; the secondary gradient color is generated 31.67° around the wheel toward the HeroUI violet. Fonts must be installed locally — the stack falls back to System UI. ## Generated palette The generator mirrors the HeroUI v3 theme builder formulas: | Token | Light | Dark | | --- | --- | --- | | background | `oklch(97.02% base hue)` | `oklch(12.00% base hue)` | | foreground | `oklch(21.03% base hue)` | `oklch(99.11% base hue)` | | surface | `oklch(100% 0.53×base hue)` | `oklch(21.03% 2×base hue)` | | surface-secondary | `oklch(95.24% 0.8×base hue)` | `oklch(25.70% 1.53×base hue)` | | accent | `oklch(62.04% 0.195 hue)` | same | | success / warning / danger | HeroUI semantic hues, rotated by `12%` of the accent hue delta | same | Radii: HeroUI component tokens use `3×` (cards), `2.5×` (tabs), `2× + 6px` (popovers) and a separate form radius. DSH's semantic scale is `xs 0.5× / sm 1× / md 1.5× / lg 2× / xl-panel 3×`, so native rows, menus and cards keep their intended proportions. ## Brand layer On top of the generated tokens, `src/hero.css` adds the recognizable HeroUI details: - **Gradient primary actions** — accent → `accent + 31.67°` (blue → violet at the default) with a soft glow. - **Aurora wash** — accent/violet gradients on the conversation canvas and sidebar. - **HeroUI surfaces** — composer and dialogs use the card radius; Dropdown/Select menu popovers use the 22px dropdown radius. Bubbles, selected sessions, menus and overlays never show the page through. - **HeroUI controls** — 36px secondary buttons with the 0.97 press scale, a sliding-indicator Tabs switch for the theme, and a Select with a rotating chevron, 150ms scale/fade popover, 100ms exit and a stroke-drawn check. - **HeroUI sliders** — 20px track with 12px end caps, a 28×20 accent thumb and a 24×16 inner face; an invisible native range input keeps pointer, keyboard and aria semantics. - **Motion** — button `scale(0.97)`, popover/dialog/tooltip enter scales, 2s skeleton shimmer, user-message entrance; all disabled under `prefers-reduced-motion`. ## Install ```sh # DSH Web dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-hero-theme # DSH Desktop dsh plugin --profile desktop add dsh-hero-theme ``` Or install manually into the Web profile: ```sh cd ~/.dsh/profiles/web pnpm add dsh-hero-theme ``` Add `"dsh-hero-theme"` to `dsh.profile.bundles` in that profile's `package.json` and restart the profile. Then open **Settings → General → HeroUI theme**. Drag Accent/Base/Radius/Radius Form, choose a font and theme; every change applies immediately and is saved into the active profile's Cordis patch. **Reset** returns to the builder defaults. ## How it works ```mermaid flowchart LR A[Profile Config
6 volatile fields] --> B[src/palette.js] B --> C[167 tokens
light + dark] C --> D[ctx.theme.overrideTokens] D --> E[DSH Web / Desktop UI] ``` 1. The Host declares six volatile Config fields: `theme`, `accentHue`, `baseChroma`, `fontFamily`, `radius`, `fieldRadius`. 2. The browser half reads that config and calls `buildAllTokens()` to generate both light and dark palettes. 3. The result is applied as one `ctx.theme.overrideTokens()` layer; `ctx.theme.setTheme(config.theme)` switches the built-in base scheme. 4. The settings row writes each field through ConfigForms (range writes are debounced by 180ms). 5. An external change to the built-in Appearance row is adopted into `theme`, so reloads keep the same appearance. The override disposer is deferred with `queueMicrotask` so removing the layer never re-enters the `theme/change` dispatch. ## Platform compatibility `dsh-hero-theme` is a Web client plugin (`dsh.client.platform: "web"`). DSH Desktop embeds the Web application, so the theme applies there through the Web client plugin loader; Desktop has its own profile. This package styles the embedded workspace only — it does not add native menu, tray, or window-shell UI. Requires DSH `^0.2.2-rc.1`. ## Develop ```sh npm run build # regenerates lib/client.js + lib/index.js npm run check # build, syntax, API contract, palette and contrast checks ``` `src/palette.js` is the single source of truth for colors, radii and fonts. It is injected into the client bundle at build time; its default output is covered by contrast and token-set checks. ## Repository layout ``` dsh-hero-theme/ ├── package.json # dsh.bundle.patch + dsh.client manifest ├── cordis.patch.yml # loader entry insert (id: dsh-hero-theme) ├── src/ │ ├── index.js # Host Config schema (six volatile fields) │ ├── palette.js # HeroUI v3 palette generator │ ├── client.tpl.js # browser half: builder row + token application │ └── hero.css # brand gradient, aurora, opaque surfaces, motion ├── scripts/ │ ├── build.mjs # zero-dependency build │ └── check-compat.mjs # DSH API, palette, contrast and CSS contract ├── .github/asset/ # README banner and preview renders ├── LICENSES/ # Apache-2.0 text for the HeroUI-derived material └── lib/ # generated artifacts (rebuilt on install/pack) ``` ## Attribution and license The plugin code is MIT-licensed (see [LICENSE](LICENSE)). Design tokens and interaction values are derived from **HeroUI**, which is Apache-2.0 licensed; see [NOTICE](NOTICE) and [LICENSES/Apache-2.0.txt](LICENSES/Apache-2.0.txt). This is an independent theme. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by HeroUI.

# dsh-ensp 面向华为 eNSP 的自动化工具。生成拓扑、启动设备、按顺序下发配置，并在每条命令后核对结果。 提供三种调用方式，共用同一套核心： - CLI：适合脚本化批量操作 - MCP Server：接入 Claude Desktop、Cursor 等客户端 - DeepSeek Harness 插件：以模型工具的形式在会话内使用 ## 功能 ### 生成拓扑 生成 eNSP 可直接打开并正常显示的 `.topo` 文件。支持内置场景，也可自定义设备与链路。 ```js import { twoPcLab, writeTopology } from 'dsh-ensp' await writeTopology('lab.topo', twoPcLab({ vlan: 10 })) ``` ```js import { buildTopology, autoLayout } from 'dsh-ensp' const topo = autoLayout( buildTopology() .add('R1', 'AR2220', { x: 180, y: 120 }) .add('R2', 'AR2220', { x: 460, y: 260 }) .link('R1', 'GigabitEthernet0/0/0', 'R2', 'GigabitEthernet0/0/0') .finish() ) ``` 拓扑格式有几处约束来自 eNSP 本身：接口分组必须与机型一致，链路锚点必须落在图标包围盒内。写错任意一项，eNSP 会打开一个没有任何设备的空白画布，并且不报错。规则见 [`docs/ENSP-FORMAT.md`](docs/ENSP-FORMAT.md)。 ### 启动与停止设备 自动定位工具栏按钮，无需手动点击。启动后按设备逐一确认就绪，窗口随即最小化，桌面可继续使用。 ```bash ensp probe # 重新标定按钮位置 ensp up lab.topo # 打开、启动、确认就绪、最小化 ensp stop # 关闭全部设备 ``` eNSP 只允许运行一个实例，异常退出时可能留下不占线程的僵尸进程，它会一直持有这个单实例锁，使下一次启动打开空白窗口。工具在启动前会识别并清理这种进程。 ### 下发配置 逐条发送，每条命令确认提示符返回后才继续。任一命令出错即中断，并回报行号、命令与设备原始输出。 ```js import { pushConfig } from 'dsh-ensp' const result = await pushConfig({ device: 'SW1', port: 2000, script: ` system-view vlan 10 quit interface GigabitEthernet0/0/1 port link-type access port default vlan 10 quit `, }) if (!result.ok) { console.log(result.failedAt.line, result.failedAt.command, result.failedAt.error) } ``` ### 等待协议收敛 路由协议是异步收敛的，配置下发完不代表邻居已经建立。这类断言一律走轮询，直到状态达成或超时。 ```js import { waitForOspfFull, waitForOspfRoute, waitForOutput } from 'dsh-ensp' await waitForOspfFull({ port: 2000, neighbourId: '2.2.2.2' }) await waitForOspfRoute({ port: 2000, prefix: '2.2.2.2/32' }) await waitForOutput({ port: 2000, command: 'display ip routing-table', until: /2\.2\.2\.2/ }) ``` 三个函数都返回 `{ ok, converged, output, attempts, waitedMs }`。固定等待一段时间再查询，在慢机器上会误判为失败，在快机器上纯属浪费。 ### 场景预设 内置 50 个场景，覆盖 VLAN、STP、堆叠、链路聚合、静态路由、RIP、OSPF、BGP、IS-IS、MPLS、组播、NAT、DHCP、ACL、QoS、端口安全、IPsec、IPv6、WLAN、防火墙与高可用等主题。 ```bash ensp preset # 按难度列出全部 ensp preset ospf-single # 查看某个场景 ensp preset --search bgp # 按关键词搜索 ensp preset campus-network --topo campus.topo # 生成该场景的拓扑 ``` 每个场景给出三项信息：需要创建的对象、配置顺序、用于确认结果的检查命令。具体命令由使用者按设备补全。 场景自带拓扑蓝图：设备、链路、地址规划都是现成的，加上 `--topo` 就直接得到一个 eNSP 能打开的 `.topo`，不用先自己画图再算 IP。蓝图不含配置命令，场景仍然只是骨架。 ```bash ensp preset ospf-single --topo ospf-single.topo ensp up ospf-single.topo ``` 场景清单与蓝图都是可生成、可校验的。`docs/SCENARIOS.md` 由 `src/core/presets.mjs` 与 `src/core/labs.mjs` 渲染而来，`npm run docs:check` 在两者不一致时返回非零，CI 也会执行这一步。 ```bash npm run docs # 重新生成 docs/SCENARIOS.md npm run docs:check # 只检查是否过期 ``` ### 设备镜像检查 部分机型只有设备目录条目、没有随装镜像，最典型的是 `USG6000V`（eNSP 安装时需勾选该组件）。这类机型放上画布、存成 `.topo` 都没问题，但 eNSP 打开后会先渲染再自行退出，事后只能看到一堆“控制台无响应”，很容易误判成拓扑或插件的问题。 `ensp up` 启动客户端之前会读 `res/items.xml` 与各插件的镜像文件，把启动不了的设备连同缺什么一起报出来： ```console $ ensp up firewall-hrp.topo error: topology uses devices this eNSP installation cannot start: USG6000V (FW1, FW2): NGFW 镜像未安装（eNSP 安装时需勾选 USG6000V 组件） This is not a bug in the topology: eNSP opens it, renders it, then quits. ... ``` `ensp preset ... --topo` 生成文件时也会给出同样的提示，`ensp_build_topology` 的返回值里带 `unsupportedDevices`。检查只读本机文件，不启动 eNSP。设备清单见 [docs/SCENARIOS.md](docs/SCENARIOS.md) 每个场景的“设备镜像”一行。 ### 窗口遮挡检查 启动设备只能点 eNSP 的工具栏按钮，而合成点击落在**拥有那个像素的窗口**上。别的程序盖住 eNSP 时，鼠标事件全被它接走，eNSP 一条都收不到，结果就是报了一连串成功、然后等一批从未启动的设备。 插件在点击前用 `WindowFromPoint` 查落点属主，不是 eNSP 就不点，直接报： ```console $ ensp up lab.topo error: eNSP is covered by another window at 1307,426: vmware (unknown). The mouse events would go to that window, so nothing was clicked. Bring eNSP to the front (restore it from the taskbar) and try again. ``` 标定之前还会扫一张 5×4 的采样网格，任一采样点被外人占住就拒绝开始，因为标定量的是屏幕像素，被遮挡时量到的全是别人的画面。点击后再查一次，防止点击瞬间被抢。 插件不能自己把 eNSP 提到前台，这一点值得说清楚，因为它决定了你该怎么用。eNSP 的 exe 要求管理员权限，所以它总以 High 完整性级别运行；普通进程属于 Medium，Windows 的 UIPI 会拦下所有发往高完整性窗口的输入消息（`WM_LBUTTONDOWN` 返回 `err=5`）。提到 High 之后 UIPI 放行，但 Windows 的前台锁仍然不允许一个后台进程改前台（`SetForegroundWindow` 返回 `False`，`AttachThreadInput` 被拒）。两条路都堵着，所以 eNSP 必须由你保持在最上层，并且你在那个桌面上。 还有一点：**不要用管理员身份运行本工具**。提权只让 `PrintWindow` 能拍到画布，点击照样进不去，还多过一次 UAC。 Windows 不允许一个进程把别人的窗口提到前台，`SetWindowPos`/`ShowWindow`/`BringWindowToTop` 全返回 `ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED`，所以这里没有自动修复，只能由人把 eNSP 放到最上层。细节与实测记录见 [docs/UI-ANCHORS.md](docs/UI-ANCHORS.md)。 ## 安装 ### 作为 DSH 插件 在插件市场搜索 `dsh-ensp` 并安装，或： ```console dsh plugin --profile desktop add dsh-ensp ``` ### 作为 CLI 或库 ```console npm install -g dsh-ensp ensp status ``` ### 作为 MCP Server ```json { "mcpServers": { "ensp": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "dsh-ensp", "mcp"] } } } ``` 提供 12 个工具：`ensp_status`、`ensp_build_topology`、`ensp_open`、`ensp_start`、`ensp_stop`、`ensp_apply`、`ensp_apply_dir`、`ensp_query`、`ensp_probe`、`ensp_scenarios`、`ensp_scenario`、`ensp_preset_config`。 ## 环境要求 | 项 | 要求 | |---|---| | 操作系统 | Windows。eNSP 仅有 Windows 版本 | | eNSP | 已安装且可正常运行，需要管理员权限 | | Node.js | 18 或更高版本 | | 权限 | 插件与 eNSP 需处于相同权限级别 | 系统缩放设为 125% 或 150% 时，程序会自行完成坐标换算，不需要手动调分辨率。若 eNSP 升级后按钮位置改变，执行 `ensp probe` 重新标定。 ## 快速开始 ```bash ensp preset vlan-access # 查看场景方向 node -e "import('dsh-ensp').then(async m => { await m.writeTopology('lab.topo', m.twoPcLab()) })" ensp up lab.topo # 启动设备 ensp status --topology lab.topo # 查看控制台状态 ensp apply ./configs --topology lab.topo --save ``` 一次两级 OSPF 实验的完整耗时（本机实测，Windows 11、i5、系统缩放 150%）： | 阶段 | 耗时 | |---|---| | 生成 `.topo` | 2s | | 打开并渲染拓扑 | 14s | | 两台 AR2220 启动到可登录 | 64s | | 下发两侧各 9 条配置 | 8s | | OSPF 邻居到 Full | 40s | ## 致谢与许可 ### 开源协议 采用 [GPL-3.0-or-later](LICENSE)。 基于本项目修改并对外分发时，需要： 1. 保留 `LICENSE` 中的版权声明； 2. 在源码及随附文档中注明原项目名称 `dsh-ensp` 与仓库地址 ； 3. 使所分发的作品同样以 GPL-3.0-or-later 授权。 仅自行使用而不对外分发时，上述要求不适用。 未选用 MIT 或 Apache-2.0，是因为这两者允许二次修改后闭源，与"二次修改也须开源"的意愿冲突。 ### 致谢 - Huawei eNSP：仿真器本体。 - 在 issue 中反馈问题的使用者。 ## 免责声明 本项目是一个自动化外壳，不包含 eNSP，也不包含任何华为软件或镜像。使用前请自行安装，并遵守华为的软件许可。 自动化操作图形界面存在固有风险，例如窗口被遮挡、eNSP 版本升级、系统缩放变化。建议先在非关键环境中验证。 ## 相关文档 | 文档 | 内容 | |---|---| | [`docs/ENSP-FORMAT.md`](docs/ENSP-FORMAT.md) | `.topo` 格式规则 | | [`docs/UI-ANCHORS.md`](docs/UI-ANCHORS.md) | 界面坐标与启动流程 | | [`docs/SCENARIOS.md`](docs/SCENARIOS.md) | 场景预设说明 |

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-tower

[![CI](https://github.com/louifinn/dsh-tower/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg?branch=main)](https://github.com/louifinn/dsh-tower/actions/workflows/test.yml)
[![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/dsh-tower.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-tower)
[![Listed on dsh-plugin.org](https://dsh-plugin.org/badges/listed.svg)](https://dsh-plugin.org/plugins/louifinn/dsh-tower)
[![Listed on dshfind](https://dshfind.com/api/badge/louifinn/dsh-tower)](https://dshfind.com/en/plugins/louifinn/dsh-tower?ref=badge)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[English](README.en.md)

**Tower** 是 [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness)（DSH）的多代理编排插件。它把一个 agent 会话变成一个小型工程团队：会话本身是*控制塔*，worker agent 在隔离的 Git worktree 里实现任务，改动经 scope/合并门禁合入基线分支；独立审查可在配置中强制开启。

Tower 模式与 mission/审查工作流的灵感来自 Moonshot AI 的 **Kimi Code** 中实验性的 Tower 模式（[Kimi Code](https://www.kimi.com/code)）。本项目是面向 DSH 的独立实现，与 Moonshot AI 无隶属关系；详见[致谢](#致谢)。

仓库根目录**就是** DSH bundle 包根：`package.json` 声明 `dsh.bundle.patch`，`cordis.patch.yml` 位于根目录，符合 DSH 插件规范。

## 特性

- **可配置的 Tower 模式。** `/tower` 切换会话级模式：收窄工具面并注入 Tower 协议；`/tower on|off <指令>` 还能把指令作为下一步用户消息转发给模型。默认也允许 Agent 通过 `tower_control` 带理由进出；设 `mode.allowAgentControl:false` 可改为仅人类控制。
- **显式的所有权交接。** 仓库状态绑定初始化它的会话。旧会话结束后，新会话可用 `/tower takeover <原因>` 接管（人类命令，任何配置都可用）；模型也可在 Tower 模式中通过 `tower_control({action:"takeover"})` 请求接管，但必须得到用户明确批准。旧属主仍活跃、仍有运行中的 roster Agent 或外部工作区锁时会拒绝；交接保留全部历史与未读消息，并写入一条 `takeover` 活动记录，不会自动释放所有权。
- **任务级隔离。** 每个 mission 使用独立分支和 Git worktree，worker 不会碰到你的主检出。
- **两种 mission 形状，一个注册表。** 每个 mission 是 `build` 或 `survey`，其状态、完成证据、
  供给方式、路径权限与 spawn 契约都由 shape 拥有，不再散落 `if (kind === …)` 分支。survey 只读：
  固定一个 `readCommit`（默认在 detached sandbox 中）即可完成，不需要提交、分支或合并。
  `npm run shape:audit` 会拒绝第二套词汇、`domain/shapes/` 之外的按 kind 条件、
  `domain/evidence.js` 之外的证据读取，以及角色检查与 shape 检查混合的写法。
- **审查门禁合并。** 审查策略是插件页上的一个三态控件：`off`、`optional`（默认）或 `required`（配置键 `review.mode`）。设为 `required` 时，审查者针对当前分支 tip 给出 `clean` / `merge` 结论；合并门禁重新校验 scope、分支新鲜度、任务完成度、审查记录与 worktree 归属，通过后才执行 `--no-ff` 合并。独立审查默认可选；策略为 `required` 时，单个 mission 可用 `reviewPolicy:"none"` + 理由并开启 `gates.allowReviewExemption:true` 做更窄豁免。升级提示：旧的布尔审查开关是保留一个版本的别名；映射关系见[安装、升级与迁移](docs/zh/guide/install-upgrade-migration.md)。
- **可恢复的协作状态。** roster、inbox、findings、reviews 与 mission 状态持久化在 `.git/dsh-tower/` 下，重启不会丢计划。
- **受控的状态增长。** worktree 已移除的终态任务在达到 `archive.afterDays`/`archive.maxMissions` 后移入 `.git/dsh-tower/archive/`，保留 tasks、reviews、findings 与完成报告；此后 mutation 只重写活跃工作。`tower_status includeArchived` 列出压缩后的归档摘要，`tower_doctor` 报告归档大小、数量与策略。
- **默认安全。** Tower 模式开启期间拒绝 `create_goal`、`update_goal(resume)`、`todo_write`、Team 任务板与 `spawn_teammate`；被暂停的 goal 不会被自动恢复。
- **可追溯的 finding 生命周期。** `tower_findings` 列表、读取并按 `open → triaged → fixed` / `wontfix` 流转，也可重新打开；只有 tower 或 worker 能改状态，reviewer 只能读。
- **仓库级配置。** 每个仓库可用 `<git-common-dir>/dsh-tower/config.json` 覆盖 review/merge/worktree/spawn 策略，工具参数再覆盖仓库配置；无需为不同仓库改 profile。
- **稳定错误码。** 工具失败统一带 `[tower:<code>]` 前缀（如 `mission-not-found`、`preset-missing`、`config-invalid`），调用方可稳定分支处理。
- **角色强制与可控中断。** worker 不能直接完成/放弃 mission 或扩界（完成必须走 `tower_complete` 证据门），tower 可随时用 `tower_interrupt` 停止跑偏的 agent；`tower_send(interrupt:true)` 可中止运行中的 turn。
- **仓库互斥与限流。** 可选 `mode.workspaceLock` 让同一仓库只有一个 Tower 会话；`spawn.maxLiveWorkers`、`send.maxPerMinute`、roster stale 标记约束并发与消息风暴。
- **可热重载。** 在带 DSH HMR 的 profile 中，`/tower reload`、`tower_reload` 与 `npm run dev:hmr` 让 linked 插件代码改动无需重启即生效；`plugin_manager` 安装/更新本身即时生效。
- **测试证据门与事件。** worker 可在 `tower_complete` 记录 `checks`，`gates.requireChecks` 可强制；每次 mutation 后发射 `tower/*` 事件并刷新 `MISSIONS.md`。
- **2.1 验证与运营。** `tower_test` 执行 worktree 声明的 `tower.testDiscovery`（TAP/json-array，准入可设 spawn/complete），`tower_doctor` 只读健康契约，`tower_batch` 批次证据收口，`tower_resource` advisory lease，`tower_import_legacy` / `tower_legacy_map` 只读旧版导入与审计映射；新增 `worker-stale`、tests 门禁、plan/tower 互斥、`workspaceLockScope`、`docs.boardLocation` 与交付 ack。

## 何时使用 Tower

Tower 是**面向 Git 仓库变更的交付协议**，不是所有多代理场景的默认答案。它适合：

- 一个特性/重构能拆成 2–8 个 scope 清晰、可独立审查的 mission；
- 有依赖顺序、需要分支新鲜度与 scope 约束的迁移；
- 敏感仓库、发布绑定变更，或需要"可审计合并 + 测试证据"（需要时开启独立审查）的工作；
- 跨上下文压缩、重启、多天协作，需要从本地状态恢复的工作；
- 需要把"完成"定义成任务 + 测试（可选独立审查），而不是聊天里的一句"好了"。

不适合：单文件/一行 hotfix、需求仍在探索、开放式研究、大量极小的独立任务、交互式 UI 配对、或跨仓库工作。判断标准：**如果你不会为它开 PR，Tower 很可能太重。**

与其他模式的区别（详见[完整指南](docs/guide/scenarios-and-philosophy.md)）：

- **普通并行子代理**：便宜、灵活，适合只读探索/试方案；没有 worktree、审查与合并门禁。
- **Agent Teams**：共享任务板与多人/多 agent 协作，适合设计、研究、横切决策；集成通常由人做，没有 Git 隔离的硬门禁。
- **Ralph 循环**：用新鲜 agent 对同一目标反复尝试，适合迭代搜索/修复；没有 mission 契约与合并审查。
- **Workflow 编排**：脚本化高扇出/流水线，适合批量分析、审计、验证；不做 Git 分支隔离与合并门禁。
- **Tower**：少量 mission + 隔离写入 + 可选独立审查 + 证据 + 合并门禁，适合"决定要做、需要安全落地"的仓库变更。

Tower 模式会拒绝 Team/Workflow/Ralph/普通 subagent 工具并清除 plan mode，避免两套编排协议同时驱动一个会话；请按阶段组合，例如先用 Workflow/Team 分析决策，再用 Tower 执行仓库变更。

## 环境要求

- DeepSeek Harness `0.2.2-rc.1`（已验证的 host 构建见 [COMPATIBILITY.md](COMPATIBILITY.md)）
- Node.js 24.9+
- Git（worktree 在本地创建，不需要联网）

`scripts/support.json` 是唯一的公开支持基线。当 package engines、mount-smoke host pin、live CI 矩阵
或 COMPATIBILITY 最新行与它不一致时，`npm run support:check` 会失败。

## 安装

把已发布的包安装到 DSH profile：

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-tower
```

在 DSH 中也可以用插件管理器指定同一目标：

```text
plugin_manager({ action: "install_bundle", target: "dsh-tower" })
```

开发时改为从 GitHub 安装或链接本地 checkout：

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add github:louifinn/dsh-tower
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add <本仓库的绝对路径>
```

Host 插件在 DSH 进程启动时加载，**安装或更新后需重启 DSH**。卸载使用 `remove_bundle`，包名 `dsh-tower`。

可选的 Web UI 随 npm 包一起发布在 `ui-bundle/`：npm 安装后目标为
`<profile>/node_modules/dsh-tower/ui-bundle`，源码安装时为目标仓库的 `ui-bundle/` 目录。用
`plugin_manager({action:"install_bundle", target:"<该目录>"})` 安装并重启 DSH，然后刷新页面。

### 已知冲突

不要同时安装 `dsh-plugins-tower`（第三方包）。它的 loader row 也使用 `name: dsh-tower`，会解析到
本包，导致本包被加载两次或对方代码不生效。`tower_doctor` 的 `loader-conflicts` 检查会报告该情况；
卸载冲突包并重启 DSH。

## 快速开始

```text
/tower on

tower_init      repoRoot=D:\work\repo            # 首次初始化，记录 base（默认当前分支）
tower_plan      repoRoot=D:\work\repo missions=[{"title":"Feature A","scope":["src/a/**"],"tasks":["implement","commit"],"kind":"build"}]
tower_spawn     repoRoot=D:\work\repo missionId=M1 role=worker
# worker 在 worktree 内实现并提交，调用 tower_complete；最终报告会返回本会话
# 可选：需要强制独立审查时，先设 review.mode:required
tower_spawn     repoRoot=D:\work\repo missionId=M1 role=reviewer
# reviewer 只读审查并调用 tower_review（clean+merge 或 p1-Nitems/p2-Nitems）
tower_preflight repoRoot=D:\work\repo missionId=M1    # 默认审查可选（review.mode:optional）；设为 review.mode:required 时审查前预期 no-review，审查后 ok:true
tower_merge     repoRoot=D:\work\repo missionId=M1
tower_teardown  repoRoot=D:\work\repo

/tower off
```

小改动通常一轮 worker 即可完成；需要独立审查时再加一轮 reviewer。完整可复制示例见 [docs/examples/first-mission.md](docs/examples/first-mission.md)，逐工具参数见 [docs/reference/tools.md](docs/reference/tools.md)。

## 命令

| 输入 | 行为 |
|---|---|
| `/tower` | 开启 Tower 模式（已开启则保持） |
| `/tower on` | 开启或保持 |
| `/tower on <指令>` | 开启/保持，并把 `<指令>` 作为下一条用户消息转发 |
| `/tower off` | 退出 Tower 模式 |
| `/tower off <指令>` | 退出并转发 `<指令>` |
| `/tower ack` | 记录人类确认，供 `mode.requireHumanAckOnFirstEntry` 使用 |
| `/tower <指令>` | 确保开启，然后转发 `<指令>` |

图片与文件附件会随指令一起作为一条完整的 `UserMessage` 转发。

运行时前置条件（preset 行、组件行与配置的冲突）只在**进入**模式的路径上重新校验：
裸 `/tower`、`/tower on`、`/tower on <指令>`，以及模式关闭时的 `/tower <指令>`。已经开启
模式后的 `/tower <指令>`、`/tower off`、`/tower off <指令>` 与 `/tower ack` 不再重复校验，
因此会话中途关掉某一行之后，人仍然退得出去、指令也仍然转发得出去；`tower_spawn`、规划与
合并/预检各自保留自己的护栏。详见 [组件行与消息语言](docs/guide/quickstart.md#component-rows-runtime-preconditions-and-message-language)。

## 组件模型

本 bundle 采用 **强制 host 锚点 + 可单独启停的可选行**（#121）：`cordis.patch.yml` 插入顶层
`tower` group（挂载 Host 插件与强制的 `preset-tower-worker`），随后是可选组件 `tower-skills`、
`tower-batch`、`tower-import`、`tower-leases`、`tower-tests`、`tower-hmr`（随包关闭）与
`preset-tower-reviewer`。在插件页关闭某一行，只会移除该能力；模式、规划工具、`tower_status`
与其余工具继续工作。

进入 Tower 模式与 `tower_plan` 前会校验必需的 preset。worker preset 是强制依赖；reviewer
preset 只在 `review.mode` 为 `required` 时必需，因此策略为 `off` 或 `optional` 时允许关闭
reviewer 行，策略为 `required` 时会以带解释的 `preset-missing` 锁定。`tower-tests` 关闭且
`gates.requireTests:true` 时同样拒绝。`tower_doctor` 与 `tower_recover` 不是组件、也没有配置键：
任何配置都会注册它们（#122）。

原则 11（[PRINCIPLES.md](PRINCIPLES.md)）与
[ADR 0005](docs/adr/0005-component-surface.md) 要求：只有关闭后仍不破坏其余能力的 capability
才能成为组件；host、健康检查、恢复通道与合并门禁永远不是开关。审查策略是唯一的
三态配置控件（off/optional/required），不是组件行。逐键答案见生成的
[组件表面](docs/reference/component-surface.md)，由 `npm run docs:check:components` 强制。

## 配置

```yaml
- id: tower-host
  name: 'dsh-tower'
  config:
    section: '（可选，兼容别名）覆盖 Tower 模式系统提示文案'
    allowAgentControl: true   # 兼容别名；等价于 mode.allowAgentControl
    mode:
      allowAgentControl: true
      autoPauseGoal: true
      denyTools: [create_goal, todo_write, team_task_create, team_task_update, team_task_reopen, spawn_teammate]
    review:
      mode: optional             # 一个三态控件：off、optional（默认）或 required
      maxRoundsPerReviewer: 5
    merge:
      timeoutMs: 900000
    worktrees:
      root: ''                 # 空 = <主检出父目录>/.dsh-tower-worktrees/<hash>
    spawn:
      workerPreset: tower-worker
      reviewerPreset: tower-reviewer
      maxDepth: 1
```

- 代码中 `mode.allowAgentControl` 默认 `true`；随包 `cordis.patch.yml` 也显式设为 `true`：模型可在用户意图/任务状态明确时自行进出，但必须给出理由；设为 `false` 时只有人类能切换。随包 patch 还默认开启 `mode.workspaceLock`（单活塔）、`send.interruptDefault`、`init.autoGitInit`，并把 `spawn.staleMs` 设为 15s。
- `/tower base <branch>` 可设置会话级 init base 偏好；`/tower on` 会清除活跃 plan mode（`mode.planModePolicy:"refuse"` 则拒绝进入），保证 plan/tower 互斥。
- 仓库级配置：在 `<git-common-dir>/dsh-tower/config.json`（通常是 `.git/dsh-tower/config.json`）放入同样的 JSON 结构，可覆盖 `review`/`merge`/`worktrees`/`spawn`；优先级为代码默认 < profile < 仓库配置 < 工具参数。`mode.*` 属于会话级，只在 profile 生效。
- 所有键与默认值见 [docs/reference/config.md](docs/reference/config.md)；未知键（顶层与分组内）都会被拒绝，防止拼写错误静默失效。三种审查模式、插件页控件位置与单版本别名迁移见[安装、升级与迁移](docs/zh/guide/install-upgrade-migration.md)。工具错误码见 [docs/reference/errors.md](docs/reference/errors.md)。

## 工具（29 个：22 个核心 + 7 个可选）

`tower_init` · `tower_plan` · `tower_mission` · `tower_status` · `tower_spawn` · `tower_roster` · `tower_adopt` · `tower_diff` · `tower_send` · `tower_inbox` · `tower_complete` · `tower_interrupt` · `tower_finding` · `tower_findings` · `tower_review` · `tower_preflight` · `tower_merge` · `tower_rebase` · `tower_teardown` · `tower_mode` · `tower_doctor` · `tower_recover` · `tower_test` · `tower_batch` · `tower_resource` · `tower_import_legacy` · `tower_legacy_map`

上面列出的是 22 个核心工具加 5 个由组件行拥有的可选工具。`tower_control` 是第 6 个可选工具，默认注册（`allowAgentControl:true`）；设为 `false` 可禁用。`tower_reload` 是第 7 个，仅在 `tower-hmr` 组件行开启时注册（随包关闭），无 HMR 服务调用会返回 `reload-unavailable`（因此最多 29 个工具：22 个核心 + 7 个可选）。`tower_doctor` 与 `tower_recover` 属于核心：任何配置都会注册它们（#122）。mission 级工具同时接受 `id` 作为 `missionId` 的别名；`task_done`/`taskDone` 等 snake/camel 写法均可。

## 安全与约束

- **门禁不全绿不合并。** `tower_preflight` 是只读检查，返回稳定的 blocker code；存在 blocker 时 `tower_merge` 拒绝合并。
- **审查绑定提交。** 策略为 `review.mode:required` 时，审查后分支 tip 变化会报 `tip-moved`，必须重新审查；reviewer 使用只读 preset，若在审查期间改动分支，提交审查会被拒绝。`off` 是受支持的模式，会移除 `tower_review`；`optional` 记录审查但从不阻塞合并。非 clean 的一轮审查会让 mission 回到 active，此后其他 route 仍可为同一 reviewed tip 提交结论并追加到同一轮；依赖为 `completed` 的 survey 视为已满足（build 依赖仍需 merged）。
- **scope 强制。** mission 只能修改其 scope glob 匹配的文件，越界会以 `out-of-scope` 阻止合并。
- **worktree 归属。** 脏工作树、运行中的 worker、已关闭 mission 的分支都会阻止合并或 teardown。
- **goal 隔离。** 进入 Tower 模式会暂停活跃 goal 并记录；退出不会自动恢复，需要你自行恢复。

表面计数（实时，由 `npm run docs:check` 校验）：29 个工具、41 个工具错误码、34 个进程内事件、57 个配置键、33 个稳定 blocker/failure code、12 个可见组件。

稳定 blocker/failure code（含 gate 守卫、`no-check-evidence`、worker-stale、tests 门禁与 merge/rebase 操作失败码）——完整清单、触发条件与修复动作见 [docs/reference/blockers.md](docs/reference/blockers.md)。工具本身抛出的错误码见 [docs/reference/errors.md](docs/reference/errors.md)，事件见 [docs/reference/events.md](docs/reference/events.md)。

## 工作原理

mission 生命周期：`planned → active → completed → merged`（或 `blocked` / `paused` / `abandoned`）。状态位置：

| 路径 | 内容 |
|---|---|
| `.git/dsh-tower/state.json` | missions、roster、reviews、findings、inbox |
| `.git/dsh-tower/activity.jsonl` | 只追加的活动日志 |
| `<主检出父目录>/.dsh-tower-worktrees/<hash>/<missionId>` | 每个 mission 的 worktree |
| `$DSH_HOME/tower-mode/modes.json` | 每个 agent/session 的 Tower 模式状态 |

worker 与 reviewer 是使用内置 `tower-worker` preset 的普通 DSH 子代理；它们的工具被限制在 mission 允许面（文件系统、shell、Tower 协议工具），不包含 merge/spawn。

```bash

```

热重载开发：`npm run dev:hmr` 把本仓库加入当前 profile 的 HMR watch root（需重启 DSH 一次），之后编辑 `host/`、`adapters/`、`app/`、`domain/` 代码可用 `/tower reload` 或自动 watch 生效；详见 [docs/guide/hot-reload.md](docs/guide/hot-reload.md)。

## CI 证明了什么

每次 push 与 PR 都运行同一组 job；每个 job 对应一条可检查的声明，而不是一句 README 承诺。

| Job | 声明 | 证据 |
|---|---|---|
| `test (24.9)`、`test (25)`（Ubuntu） | canonical 支持运行时 leg：每条 leg 只运行一次 `npm run check`——离线套件、文档一致性、生成文档、发布文件清单、架构、类型、支持清单、workflow 契约与 domain 纯度全部成立 | `npm run check` |
| `test (24.9, windows)`（`windows-latest`，必需检查） | 同一套 canonical `npm run check` 在真实 Windows 文件系统上成立；路径大小写、`pwsh` shell、rename/unlink 重试都不是只在 Linux 上被假设 | `npm run check` |
| `test (24.9)` 的 `Coverage (Node 24.9)` 步骤 | 覆盖率在 CI 中真实测量（只报告，不设阈值、不加徽章） | `npm run test:coverage` |
| `test (24.9)` 的 `Release check`（Node 24.9）步骤 | tag 是一种声明：tag 是 annotated tag 对象、其 commit 在 HEAD 历史中、工作树干净、版本已越过上一个版本 tag、CHANGELOG 带有该版本的发布内容、支持清单一致 | `npm run release:check` |
| `publish` 的 `prepublishOnly` 钩子（本地，`npm publish` 自动运行） | 发布前重跑同一套 release 断言，加上支持清单、生成文档与发布文件清单；只读、离线、不写工作树 | `npm run release:prepublish` |
| `mount`（Node 24.9） | 打出的 tarball 经 plugin CLI 装进一次性 profile 后，真实 loader 挂载并注册了 bundle 声称的表面 | `npm run smoke:mount` |
| `mount-fixtures`（Node 24.9，非必需检查） | mount smoke 仍会因正确的种子失败而变红（改名一个工具 id、删除 skills 段），三次运行共用一次缓存的 host 安装 | `npm run smoke:fixtures -- --host-dir <缓存的 host>` |
| `live (<固定 host 版本>)`（nightly/手动，非必需检查） | 浏览器 live suite 在固定 host 版本矩阵上仍能驱动真实 Web 运行时；push/PR 只做无浏览器的环境与解析检查 | nightly 跑 `npm run test:live -- --script nightly`；push 跑 `npm run test:live -- --check` |

canonical 三条 leg 在 job 内用 `matrix.label` 固定各自的 context 字符串：`test (24.9)`、`test (25)` 与 `test (24.9, windows)`，名字逐字节不变；把 `os` 直接塞进 matrix 会把它们改名成 `test (24.9, ubuntu-latest)`，保护规则将永远等不到该 context，所以矩阵用显式 `include` + `label`。`main` 在 `strict` 保护下有四条必需 context：`mount`、`test (24.9)`、`test (25)`、`test (24.9, windows)`。两步切换已经完成：三条 legacy `test (22)` 风格的 context 已移除，冻结的 legacy job 已删除。Windows leg 运行完整的 `npm run check`（无浏览器、无 live suite、无 release/coverage），与 Ubuntu leg 并行，不延长关键路径。切换过程、校验命令与回滚方式见 [docs/operations/ci.md](docs/operations/ci.md)。

live suite 需要下载浏览器并真实启动 host，因此移出 push/PR，改为 nightly `schedule`（另支持 `workflow_dispatch`），在固定 host 版本矩阵上运行；它的输出第一行打印解析后的 `DSH_HOME` 与 host 版本。push 上只保留 `--check`（环境 + Playwright 解析，无浏览器）。Playwright 由 `tests/live/package-lock.json` 固定，root 的 `npm ci` 不下载浏览器。

`tests/platform.test.mjs` 用注入的 `platform`/`rename`/`unlink` 在任意 OS 上同时断言 win32 与 POSIX 两条分支；唯一需要真实 Windows 的“rename 覆盖被打开的目标文件”用例在 Linux 上以 `# SKIP` 计入 TAP（`tests 11`、`skipped 1`），而不是静默消失。macOS 不单设 runner：它与 Linux 走同一条 POSIX 分支，这是 #86 的非目标。

`mount` 断言一次性 profile 的**已加载表面**，而不是 `cordis.patch.yml` 的文本：随包 profile 加载 28 个 `tower_*` 工具（27 个 `tools/*.js` 模块 + `tower_mode` / `tower_control`，减去因 `tower-hmr` 随包关闭而不注册的 `tower_reload`；所有可选能力行全开时为 29 个）、3 个内置 skill、`tower-worker` / `tower-reviewer` 两个 preset、`/tower` 命令、一个顶层 `tower` host group 以及可选的顶层能力行（`tower-hmr` 随包关闭）。它不调用模型、不打开浏览器。在维护者的 Windows 机器上实测：host 冷装（含安装）约 100 秒，host 已缓存约 85 秒；CI 中该步骤上限为 3 分钟（`timeout-minutes: 3`），`mount` job 上限 5 分钟。红叉会打印解析后的 profile 路径、host build、已加载计数与每一条未满足的声明。

host build 固定在 `scripts/mount-smoke/host.json`；`scripts/support.json` 记录公开支持基线，`npm run support:check` 保证 package engines、host pin、live 矩阵与 `COMPATIBILITY.md` 最新行一致，单元测试再保证该行与 pin 相等，发布时不再各写一遍。`npm run smoke:fixtures` 用两种种子失败（改名一个工具 id、删除 skills 段）证明 smoke 会以正确原因变红；CI 中它作为非必需的 `mount-fixtures` job 运行，control 与两个种子通过 `--host-dir` 共用一次缓存的 host 安装（本机热跑约 2 分钟）。

## 常见问题

- **安装/更新后插件不出现。** Host 插件在 DSH 启动时加载，请重启 DSH；并确认安装目标指向本仓库根目录（含 `package.json` 与 `cordis.patch.yml` 的那一层），而不是子目录。
- **没有 `tower_control`。** 配置中被设为 `allowAgentControl:false`；改回 `true` 并重启。
- **合并被阻止。** 运行 `tower_preflight` 查看 blocker code；`stale-base` 表示先执行 `tower_rebase`。
- **基线前进后分支过期。** `tower_rebase` 在 worktree 内完成 rebase；干净且无冲突的 rebase 可免去上一轮审查的重审。
- **合并提交已经存在，但 `tower_merge` 报了失败。** 重新执行 `tower_merge` 即可：它会检测已落地的合并提交（或分支已包含在 base 中）并记录为 reconciled，不会重复合并。
- **仓库的 `pre-merge-commit` 钩子很慢。** 合并超时默认 15 分钟，可按次通过 `tower_merge({ ..., timeoutMs: 900000 })` 调大；钩子输出缓冲上限 64 MB。钩子失败返回 `merge-hook-failed`（超时带 `timeout: true`），并保持仓库干净以便重试。

# Tower UI (optional Client bundle)

An **optional** Web Client bundle for the Host `dsh-tower` plugin. It never touches Tower state directly: everything it renders is derived from the conversation the user is already looking at, or from the tool results already in that conversation. There is no Host → Client remote channel, no `host.call`, no DOM manipulation, no iframe, and no import of Harness Client packages (the only browser module-table word it requires is `react`).

Version: **0.2.2** (private, not published). The Host plugin version is unchanged.

This revision fixes GitHub **#11** (persistent, history-derived Tower-mode indicator in the composer dock) and **#12** (mode-aware `Tower mode · disabled` rows for guard-denied tools), see below.

## What it registers

| Surface | Slot | Registration | Data source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tower tool cards | `tool.call.toolview` (keyed, session) | 12 entries, one per `key`: `tower_status`, `tower_roster`, `tower_spawn`, `tower_mission`, `tower_complete`, `tower_review`, `tower_preflight`, `tower_merge`, `tower_teardown`, `tower_interrupt`, `tower_doctor`, `tower_batch` | The Chat tool-call tree's owner props: `toolName`, `phase` (`preparing` / `start` / `result`), `block` (streaming start block or settled `tool/result` block), `callId`. |
| Composer dock | `conversation.composer.dock` (list, session) | `id: "tower-hint"`, `order: 6` | `useChat` standard selector hook (the durable Chat legacy slice). In Tower mode: a `Tower · on` chip. Otherwise, a Tower tool result in the conversation: a compact latest-status line. Otherwise: the static `/tower` hint. |
| Denied-tool rows | `tool.call.toolview` (keyed, session) | dynamic entries for the Tower-mode deny list, `priority: -10`, plus `update_goal` | The same history-derived Tower mode. Registered only while the displayed session is in Tower mode and disposed when it leaves, so the native toolviews (priority 0) return. |
| Overlay status strip | `shell.overlay` (list, root) | `id: "tower-status-strip"`, `order: 20` | The overlay slot is root-scoped, so it receives no chat hooks. The chat-driven toolview components publish a start/result notice into a module-local observable that this entry injects as `useTowerNotice`; a single timer auto-dismisses it after 4.5 s and is disposed by `ctx.effect`. |
| Locale | Client locale service | namespace `tower-ui` (`en`, `zh`) | Bound `t` seats come from each registration's `locale` option. |

The cards are deliberately compact: mission status/counts, task checklist progress, blockers, roster live/stale counts, review verdict, merge/preflight state, and check/test evidence (exit codes included). All of it is rendered as React elements with inline styles; **theme references are restricted to `--dsw-alias-*` tokens**, so light/dark and token renames degrade gracefully.

The overlay strip is `pointer-events: none` end-to-end and uses `role="status"` / `aria-live="polite"`; it never blocks the composer or the page.

## Source layout (#71)

The bundle is split along the surfaces above. `client.js` is the entry: it owns
the diagnostics seam and the registrations, and loads the package-local chunks
through the DSH client module system's `require.async("./client.<surface>.js")`
(bundles execute as classic scripts, so the entry cannot require a sibling
synchronously). Every chunk registers through the same `window.__ModuleLoader__`
surface as `{ id: 'dsh-tower-ui', chunk: 'client.<surface>.js', factory }` and
receives the shared helpers/styles/locales through the `env` the entry composes;
no chunk reaches the Host or another chunk.

| File | Surface |
|---|---|
| `client.js` | entry: diagnostics, `apply`, the five registrations |
| `client.toolview.js` | toolview card: lifecycle + `TowerToolCard` |
| `client.cards.js` | the per-tool card models behind the card |
| `client.dock.js` | composer dock: mode chip, unknown state, latest summary |
| `client.mode.js` | history-derived mode model + observable |
| `client.denied.js` | mode-aware `Tower mode · disabled` rows |
| `client.overlay.js` | transient `shell.overlay` status strip + notice store |
| `client.locales.js` | `en`/`zh` dictionaries and the `t`-seat helpers |
| `client.styles.js` | the `--dsw-alias-*` inline style table |
| `client.helpers.js` | tool vocabulary + defensive payload helpers |
| `index.js` | Host half (empty `apply`) |

The client tier is gated by `scripts/architecture.mjs` like any other source
root: `client-no-node` (no `node:*` imports; DOM globals are fine),
`client-size` (800-line ceiling per file) and `client-ambient` (no module-level
`let`; state lives in the `create*` closure), each with a seeded fixture in
`tests/architecture.test.mjs`. Every client source file stays under 400 lines
and the split preserves the pre-split line total within 10%
(`tests/ui-bundle.test.mjs`).

## Persistent Tower-mode indicator (#11)

Tower mode is a Host-side session stance and there is no Client RPC for it. The dock derives it from the durable session history that the Chat projection exposes in `useChat(snapshot.legacy)`:

- the `/tower on|off` command node (`kind: "command"`, `name: "tower"`, `args`, `outcome.kind`); bare `/tower` and `/tower <message>` mean "ensure on", while `/tower ack`, `/tower takeover [reason]`, `/tower reload` and `/tower base <branch>` operate on other state and leave the stance unchanged; a failed command is ignored;
- `tower_mode` results (`mode: "on" | "off" | "unknown"`, `deniedWhileActive`, `workspaceLock`, `lastChange`);
- `tower_control` results (`action: enter|exit`, `mode`, `changedBy`, `reason`).

The last recognized event wins. A page refresh re-derives the same stance from the loaded history; when that history window no longer contains a mode event, the dock falls back to a browser-local last-known value for the same session and labels it as such. An old value expires after seven days and never drives the denied-tool shadowing by itself.

While the mode is on the dock shows a `Tower · on` chip with `role="status"` / `aria-live="polite"`, and its tooltip carries the actionable hint plus, when known, the repository basename, workspace-lock state (`held`/`free`), and who changed the mode last. The chip is **deliberately non-interactive**: the only existing standard affordance is `inputActions.setDraft` + `inputActions.submit`, which submits the composer draft and would clobber what the user is typing. The tooltip tells the user to run `/tower off`; the bundle itself does not toggle the mode (the model's supported path is the Host `tower_control` tool when `allowAgentControl` is enabled).

## Mode-aware denied-tool rows (#12)

The Host guard returns a plain tool error like `tower mode: <tool> is disabled while Tower mode is active; use the Tower tools or /tower off` (and `tower mode: goals cannot be resumed while Tower mode is active; use /tower off first` for `update_goal` resume).

While the displayed session is in Tower mode the bundle dynamically registers `tool.call.toolview` entries for:

- `tower_mode.deniedWhileActive` when the latest `tower_mode` output lists it, otherwise `host/config.js` `DEFAULT_DENY_TOOLS` (`create_goal`, `todo_write`, `team_task_create`, `team_task_update`, `team_task_reopen`, `team_task_list`, `spawn_teammate`, `wait_agent`, `workflow`, `ralph`, `subagent`, `subagent_fork`);
- `update_goal` unconditionally, because the guard special-cases its `action: "resume"`.

Those entries register with `priority: -10`. The slot core renders the lowest priority for a key, so this shadows the native keyed views without replacing them; disposing the entries (mode off) restores the native views exactly. A denial result renders as a distinct **`Tower mode · disabled`** row (warn marker, label, the preserved denial message, and the `/tower off` hint) — not the generic error text styling. `update_goal` resume denials get the same row. A non-denial result that lands in one of those slots while the mode is on renders a defensive generic row (there is no native view to delegate to while the registration shadows it); ordinary tool errors are not misclassified as Tower-mode denials.

## Accessibility and persisted state contract

The bundle is a status surface, not an interactive control surface, so the
minimum contract is deliberately small and test-enforced in
`tests/ui-bundle.test.mjs`:

- **Dock chip / unknown state**: `role="status"`, `aria-live="polite"`,
  `aria-atomic="true"`, and an `aria-label` carrying the same text as the
  tooltip. The chip is non-interactive on purpose (see above), so it has no
  focus target and no click handler.
- **Dock summary**: `role="status"`, `aria-live="polite"`, `aria-atomic="true"`,
  and an `aria-label` with the tool label plus the localized summary text.
- **Tool cards**: `role="group"` with the card headline as `aria-label`;
  `aria-busy="true"` while the call is running. Rows whose tone is
  error/warning/success also carry `data-tower-tone`, `role="note"`, and an
  `aria-label` of the localized tone word plus the row text, so status is never
  conveyed by colour alone.
- **Overlay strip**: `role="status"`, `aria-live="polite"`,
  `aria-atomic="true"`, `aria-label` equal to the notice text, and
  `pointer-events: none` end-to-end.
- **Review-policy settings control** (root `client.js`, native radios): the
  section is a labelled group with a heading, the radiogroup is named by the
  heading and described by the intro, each input is labelled and described by
  its option spans, and the current/saved state is `role="status"` with
  `aria-live="polite"`/`aria-atomic="true"`. The restart note, inserted only
  after a save away from a profile that started with review off, is
  `role="note"` with `aria-live="polite"` and `aria-atomic="true"` so the
  dynamic insertion is announced instead of silently appearing beside the
  "Saved." status. Keyboard and focus behaviour is the browser's native radio
  group; nothing is implemented with a div that only looks interactive.

The dock stores a last-known mode per browser session. It validates the whole
snapshot before display (plain object, exact keys, boolean `on`, bounded text,
`denied` and `lock` shapes, a sane timestamp, and a 4 KiB raw cap) and discards
foreign, corrupt, stale or oversized values in a `try`/`catch`; storage failure
never breaks the dock, which then falls back to the history-derived model.

The client locale dictionary is gated in `tests/locale-copy.test.mjs`: the test
loads `client.locales.js` as a browser chunk, requires identical `en`/`zh` key
sets, and runs the shared copy gate for empty text, the glossary terms and
untranslated English. The banned config-key/tool-id/command/module rules are
not applied to this dictionary because a few tooltips intentionally quote
`/tower` and `tower_mode`.

## Verification status

Verified **statically** against the installed DSH **0.2.1-rc.2** sources:

- `tool.call.toolview`: declared by `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-tool` as `{ kind: "keyed", scope: "session" }`; the Chat tool-call tree dispatches with `entryKey = toolName` and passes `{ callId, toolName, ...call, openFile, cwd, home, loadImage, useDisclosure, inspect }`, where `call` is `{ phase, block }`. A keyed hit replaces the generic tool row; a miss falls back to it.
- Keyed priority/shadowing: the Client slot core (in the web shell bundle) allows a second keyed registration only at a different `priority` and resolves a key with the **lowest** priority first — `register at a different priority to shadow it (lowest renders)`. Native views use the default priority 0.
- `conversation.composer.dock`: declared by `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-conversation` as `{ kind: "list", scope: "session" }`, rendered as `div[data-composer-dock]`. Owner props are empty; session-scope standard props (including `useSession`, `useChat`, `useConversation`) are supplied by the renderer.
- `shell.overlay`: declared by `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-layout` as `{ kind: "list", scope: "root" }`, rendered inside `[data-shell-overlay]`. Root standard props are `useSessions`, `useSessionStatus`, `useWorkspaces`, `usePanelInfo` and keyed access hooks — **no chat hook**; hence the toolview-published notice design above.
- `/tower` history: DSH logs `command/run` with `{ name, args: parsed.rawInput, source }` and `command/done` with `{ kind, text }`, which the Chat command node exposes as `{ kind: "command", name, args, outcome }` in the legacy slice.
- Guard denial shape: the Host tools pipeline materializes a denial as `{ content: [{ type: "text", text: "Error: <reason>" }], isError: true, error: { message: <reason> } }`.
- Locale: `ctx.locale.register(ns, { en, zh })`, dictionaries are flat `key → template` maps with `{param}` interpolation; a slot declaration's `locale` option supplies the bound `t` seat.
- The bundle's `dsh.client.inject` orders activation after `ui-conversation` and `ui-tool`, the two packages that declare the slots it targets. `ctx.slots.inject` only installs a registration while its owner declaration exists; each injection is guarded and reported in diagnostics instead of crashing the whole Client half.

Automated offline coverage: `tests/ui-bundle.test.mjs` loads `client.js` through a fake `window.__ModuleLoader__` (and each split chunk through the same loader when the entry calls `require.async`), asserts the 12 keys / dock id / overlay id, en–zh dictionary parity, theme-token discipline, every file's loader format and the split-size budget, and renders every card plus the dock/overlay components with fake hooks. It also drives fake chat history through the dock to assert the off hint, the on chip (including refresh re-derivation), `tower_mode`/`tower_control`/command updates, dynamic registration for default and configured deny lists, disposal on mode off, `update_goal`, denial-row treatment, generic fallbacks, and locale parity — no browser required.

Live/browser verification is **opt-in** (`tests/live/ui-slots.cjs`) because it needs an isolated profile with the bundle installed. From a teammate/subagent session the Client `Slots` inspect query times out by design (the page answers only the agent whose session it displays), so this phase did not run a live inspection; the source-level contract above is the evidence. When the script runs against an installed profile it binds a session with a bare `/tower` command and asserts, through the read-only `window.__TOWER_UI_DIAG__` report, that apply() ran without errors, that all 12 toolview keys and the dock/overlay entries registered, that the dock outlet is visible, and — since the bind command turns the Host mode on — that the history-derived `Tower · on` chip rendered (#11). The chip can be inspected visually in the same run (`data-tower-ui="dock-mode"`).

## Tests

```powershell
# offline, no browser
node --check ui-bundle/client.js
Get-ChildItem ui-bundle -Filter 'client*.js' | ForEach-Object { node --check $_.FullName }
node --test tests/ui-bundle.test.mjs

# opt-in live check (isolated profile only)
node tests/live/ui-slots.cjs
```

`tests/live/ui-slots.cjs` prints `SKIP` and exits 0 when `DSH_TEST_URL` (or Playwright) is missing; it never installs anything and never opens the desktop profile. Set `DSH_TEST_EXPECT_HINT=1` when the bundle is installed so a missing client module or missing dock entry fails instead of skipping the assertion, and `DSH_TEST_EXPECT_MODE=1` to require the history-derived `Tower · on` chip after the script's `/tower` bind step (otherwise that check is a warning, since the bind step is best-effort).

## Why it is a separate bundle

It is not installed by default and does not affect installing or running the Host `dsh-tower` plugin. The Host plugin is fully functional without it; the UI half only decorates the conversation that is already on screen.

## Install (isolated profile only)

```text
# throwaway profile, not the desktop profile
dsh --profile towertest --from-default-profile web --dump-config
dsh plugin --profile towertest add <absolute path to this ui-bundle>
dsh --profile towertest --port 59001 --no-open
# open the tokenized URL printed at boot, then verify:
$env:DSH_TEST_URL='http://127.0.0.1:59001/?token=<token>'
$env:DSH_TEST_EXPECT_HINT='1'; node tests/live/ui-slots.cjs
```

From a session in that profile, `plugin_manager({ action: "install_bundle", target: "<absolute path to this ui-bundle>" })` performs the same add + enable. Do not install it into the live desktop profile without the user's explicit request.

## Remove

```text
dsh plugin --profile towertest remove dsh-tower-ui
```

Without HMR a bundle that has been running since process start may need a DSH restart for removal; with HMR a reconcile can unload it. A page refresh (or hard refresh) is enough to update the Client half after a linked-directory change.

## Known limitations

- **No live Host state / no new RPC.** The mode chip is inferred from the **loaded history window** of the displayed session. If the `/tower on` command (or a `tower_mode` result) sits outside that window, the dock falls back to the static hint and the mode-aware rows are not registered; a later `/tower`, `tower_control`, or `tower_mode` result corrects it. The dock summary is likewise the latest visible Tower tool result, not a dashboard, and does not poll.
- **Mode-driven registration is slot-global.** The dock follows the displayed session. While that session is in Tower mode, the denied-tool shadow entries also apply to other sessions' rows for those tools (they render the defensive generic row); leaving the mode disposes them globally and restores the native views.
- **A custom `mode.denyTools` list needs a `tower_mode` result in the visible history.** The dock learns `deniedWhileActive` only from a `tower_mode` output; if the mode was inferred from `/tower on` alone (or the `tower_mode` result is outside the loaded window), the bundle shadows the default list instead, and a custom denied tool falls back to the native error row until a `tower_mode` output appears.
- **The on-chip is not a button.** `inputActions.submit()` submits the composer draft, so programmatically sending `/tower off` would overwrite the user's draft; the actionable tooltip asks the user to run it. There is no click handler and no automatic toggle from the bundle; the Host `tower_control` tool remains the model's supported path.
- **The overlay is root-scoped.** It cannot read chat state directly, so a result that lands while every Tower toolview is unmounted (for example the user switches sessions before the result renders) shows no strip. The strip itself carries no actionable content by design.
- A tool result whose payload is not JSON (older/foreign shape) renders as a plain one-line summary rather than a card; errors render as an error card.
- Client bundle updates are not auto-rebuilt: edit → reconcile/link → **refresh the page**. Profile patch or manifest changes may need a restart.
- `window.__TOWER_UI_DIAG__` is a read-only diagnostic seam for tests. It contains no session content — only plugin version, applied flag, slot/toolview names, current mode summary, dynamic deny keys, and guarded registration errors.
