# dsh-planning-with-files Native [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (`dsh`) plugin for [planning-with-files](https://github.com/OthmanAdi/planning-with-files): persistent file-based planning for AI coding agents. The plan lives on disk in `task_plan.md`, `findings.md` and `progress.md`; this plugin keeps it in the model's context on every prompt and can hold a gated turn open until the plan reports complete. ## Install ```bash npx skills add OthmanAdi/planning-with-files --skill planning-with-files -g dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-planning-with-files ``` The first line installs the skill text into `~/.agents/skills/planning-with-files/`, one of the paths dsh reads natively. The second adds this bundle to the `web` profile; restart `dsh web` afterwards. The same `dsh plugin --profile add dsh-planning-with-files` works for the `headless`, `sdk` and `acp` profiles. `dsh --profile web --dump-config` shows the `dsh-planning-with-files` layer. Built against the published `@deepseek-ai/dsh` 0.1.5-rc.2 and the `@deepseek-ai/*` 0.1.5-rc.2 libraries it installs. ## What the plugin does | Lifecycle point | Behavior | |---|---| | `agent/pre-step` | Appends the active plan to the step that carries the user's prompt: the framed head of `task_plan.md`, the normalized tail of `progress.md`, a pointer to `findings.md`. Resolves `PLAN_ID`; with one named plan, `.planning/.active_plan` or the plan directory itself; two or more named plans without `PLAN_ID` get the `Multiple plans are available` notice instead of a plan; then the legacy root file. Steps that carry only tool results, steering or the plugin's own messages get nothing | | `tools/post-execute` | Attaches a progress reminder to successful `write` and `edit` calls, and to mutating `str_replace_editor` calls (`create`, `str_replace`, `insert`) where a profile mounts that tool, while a plan exists | | `session/event` with a successful `compaction/end` | The next step of that agent (the continuation of an automatically compacted turn, or the prompt after a manual `/compact`) carries the compaction note (plan pointer, flush instruction, attestation hash) and the framed plan as one message, so the continuation resumes at the current phase | | `agent/turn-stopping` | Completion gate in gated mode: while an `in_progress` phase remains, the plugin steers the agent into another step with the gate reason. Block cap `PWF_GATE_CAP` (default 20) and ledger stall detection release the turn; subagent children are never held | Commands: `/pwf [--autonomous|--gated] [--template analytics] [plan name]` creates the planning files (a name creates `.planning/YYYY-MM-DD-/` and makes it active; `--gated` or `--autonomous` writes the v3 markers and attests the plan) and queues the framed plan for the next model request; `/pwf-status` reports the active plan. Tools: `pwf_init`, `pwf_status`, `pwf_check` with the same contract as the OpenCode plugin, resolving the plan from the calling agent's session workspace. Environment, read from the `dsh` process: `PLAN_ID=` binds a plan and ends resolution when the slug names none; `PWF_PLAN_ROOT=` pins the project root and fails closed when it does not resolve; `PLANNING_DISABLED=1` silences every listener, command and tool; `PWF_GATE_CAP=` caps the gate blocks. Autonomous and gated plans inject only when `.attestation` (slug) or `.plan-attestation` (root) matches the SHA-256 of `task_plan.md`. A live plan in a direct child project makes a cwd guess ambiguous and nothing is injected, with a one-line notice. Row configuration: `enabled` (default `true`) and `gate` (default `true`, set `false` to keep injection and drop the completion gate). Full guide: [docs/deepseek-harness.md](https://github.com/OthmanAdi/planning-with-files/blob/master/docs/deepseek-harness.md). ## License MIT

Planning with Files   

The planning skill your agent cannot ignore.
Not a prompt it might follow. A hook that fires every turn, a plan on disk that survives /clear, and 3 out of 3 blind A/B wins to show it works.

### Sponsor

**Your agent keeps the plan. Scrape.ly brings the web data.** **Sponsor:** [Swiftproxy](https://www.swiftproxy.net/?ref=planningwithfiles) · Residential proxies for browser automation. --- **OSS code review support**
Provided through [CodeRabbit’s open-source program](https://www.coderabbit.ai/oss). ---

Your agent's context window dies. The plan does not.

Persistent file-based planning for AI coding agents and long-running agent tasks: the skill keeps task_plan.md, findings.md, and progress.md on disk. Activated lifecycle hooks inject selected project planning context, so the plan survives context loss, /clear, crashes, and compaction. Automatic recovery reads project files only. Reading same-project local agent session records for aggregate counts or bounded replay requires an explicit catchup mode. Installs across 60+ agents via the Agent Skills standard, with native plugins for Claude Code, Codex CLI, Qoder CLI, Pi, Hermes Agent, OpenCode and DeepSeek Harness.

See it survive /clear · Install · Long-running tasks · First-class hosts

Open the Commands, Multi-agent runs, Benchmarks & more section below for the reference · Full install guide

# dsh-llm-manage

A persistent [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) plugin that
manages the model inventory of a configured LLM route: pins and favorites, a per-model
reason why each model is unusable, gateway directory reconciliation, and automatic
fallback when one model's quota runs out.

**No screenshots are committed, on purpose.** `screenshot.mjs` captures a *running* harness,
so the images show whatever routes and model inventory that harness has — the maintainer's own
deployment. A route name rendered into a PNG cannot be found by a text scan, which is how a
set of them was published once. Run the script against your own harness (see
[Looking at the panel without restarting](#looking-at-the-panel-without-restarting)) and you
get your own routes, which is the only version of that picture that means anything to you.

## Why

A route that aggregates many providers behind one gateway exposes its whole catalogue as
one flat list. Five things then go wrong at once, and none of them is the gateway's fault:

| Pain | What this plugin does |
|---|---|
| A long list, favorites buried | Pin and favorite models; the picker lifts them into their own sections at the top, and the panel sorts pinned → favorite → recent → rest |
| No sense of which models you actually rely on | A local ledger levels each model by how often you use it and ranks the rest by 14-day heat, shown as a **Most used** card in the panel and a ranked section in the picker |
| Retired models still listed; selecting one errors | Reconciles the route's `models:` list against the gateway's own `GET {baseURL}/models` directory and flags anything missing as retired |
| Quota exhausted, manual switching | Watches `agent/request-error`, moves the session to the next usable model on a model-scoped failure, and reports the switch only once the model that answered confirms it |
| The same model served by several providers | Marks each row with how many other routes also serve it, instead of hiding the copies |
| Models that cannot be called at all | Probes with a minimal request and labels the incompatibility honestly |

Nothing here is hard-coded to one gateway or one model id.

## Install

From the npm registry (the packaged release, no toolchain needed):

```
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-llm-manage
```

`dsh plugin` forwards the arguments after `--profile <name>` to pnpm inside that profile's
directory, so anything pnpm accepts works here (`add`, `remove`, `why`, …). The profile maps
`node_modules/dsh-llm-manage` to the package from the registry.

### Development installs

Prefer the npm package for a normal installation. Two alternatives are useful while working
on the plugin itself:

- Install from a **path** to link the directory, so local edits show up without reinstalling:
  ```
  dsh plugin --profile web add /absolute/path/to/dsh-llm-manage
  ```
  This symlinks the working copy — ideal when you are the author. Every edit is live, which
  is why "Applying a change" below is written for it.
- Install from the **git URL** to get a fixed copy of the latest source rather than the npm
  release:
  ```
  dsh plugin --profile web add git+https://github.com/PhilYue/dsh-llm-manage.git
  ```

The package installs as a bundle: its `dsh.bundle.patch` row inserts one Host plugin, and
its `dsh.client` declaration makes the web shell load the browser half. The Host half
needs a **full harness restart**; the browser half is picked up by the client HMR watcher,
so a page refresh is enough. See "Applying a change" below.

## Configuration

Every value lives in the plugin row's `config`, so your own patch layer keeps overrides
across upgrades. Defaults:

```yaml
- id: llm-manage
  name: 'dsh-llm-manage'
  config:
    selector:
      mode: managed     # our picker owns the seat; 'native' hands it back to the shipped one
    probe:
      intervalMs: 1200  # delay between deep probes
      timeoutMs: 30000
      batch: 40         # probes accepted per request
    directory:
      ttlMs: 1800000    # how long a gateway directory read is trusted
    fallback:
      enabled: true
      chain: []         # 'route/model' entries, tried first
    recovery:
      retryFirst: true  # let the platform retry a transient failure before we move
      autoContinue: true  # pick the work back up once the model has moved
      maxSwitches: 3    # automatic switches allowed per request (0 = never move)
      maxContinuations: 2  # pickups allowed per request (0 = move and stop)
      idleWaitMs: 1000  # how long to wait for the session to go idle before giving up
    usage:
      enabled: true     # local proficiency/heat counters
      seed: true        # one pass over existing session logs at startup
      flushMs: 5000     # counters are batched to disk on this interval
```

The fallback chain order is: `fallback.chain`, then pinned models, then favorites, then the
remaining models on the same route, then other routes. Models already known to be retired,
protocol-incompatible, hidden, or inside their quota cooldown are skipped. At most three
automatic switches happen per turn by default — see "Budgets are policy, not constants"
below for the three numbers and where to change them.

### The host has to be new enough

`package.json` declares `engines.dsh`. DSH reads it before installing and before
activating a plugin, and it decides compatibility on its own (peer dependencies are
ignored once it is present), so a host outside the range fails **at install time** instead
of installing and then quietly rendering less than it should.

That matters more here than it usually does: this plugin takes over UI seats
(`conversation.input.model` and the session options that hang off it), a projection
(`agentTeam`), and SDK calls (`agent.followup`, `sessionProjections`, `remote.agentTeams`)
that only exist from 0.2.2 onwards. Installed into an older host it would still load, still
look right, and silently drop the rows whose plumbing is missing — which reads as "the
plugin forgot to implement it". A refused install is the honest failure.

### Budgets are policy, not constants

Three numbers used to be constants in the Host. They are the ones an outage actually
makes you want to change, so they are now config, and editable from **Model manager →
Failover → Automatic handling**:

| Setting | Default | What it bounds |
|---|---|---|
| switches per request | 3 | automatic model switches inside one request |
| continuations per request | 2 | pickups of the interrupted work (0 = move and stop) |
| idle wait (ms) | 1000 | how long we wait for the session to go idle before giving up |

`0` is a real value, not "unset": zero switches means never move automatically, zero
continuations means move but leave the work for you. Writing any of them stores an override
in the plugin's own config document — never in your `cordis.patch.yml` — and the dialog
reads the effective value back from the Host, so what you see is what the next failure will
use. Out-of-range input is refused both in the field and at the Host (`400`), because a
number that silently becomes something else is worse than a rejected edit.

### Which failures switch, and which never do

The rule is **scope**, not severity:

| Failure | Scope | Switches? | Recorded against the model? |
|---|---|---|---|
| model not found / retired | one model | yes | yes |
| wrong protocol for this route | one model | yes | yes |
| per-model quota exhausted | one model | yes | yes |
| needs authorization on this account (401/403, OAuth, star-gated) | one model | **never** | yes |
| other per-model failures | one model | yes | yes |
| no adapter registered for this route | the whole route | yes | **no** |
| malformed request / context too long | the request itself | **never** | no |
| account-wide rate limit | the whole API key | **never** | no |
| account-wide quota | the whole API key | **never** | no |
| the route does not answer at all (DNS, TLS, refused socket) | the whole route | **never** | no |

A model-scoped failure moves to another model, because a different model can serve the
turn. An account-scoped failure never moves: every model shares that key, so switching
would only hide the real problem and burn another request.

A switch cannot rescue the turn that just failed. DSH freezes the provider, model and
reasoning effort at step preparation, re-validates them when the request is built, and
replays the same frozen selection on a retry — so the plugin commits the switch with
`agent.model.select()`, the one path the SDK documents, and the work continues on the new
model (see below). The failed turn reports its real error instead of a request-time
mismatch. If the Session still holds the broken selection when the next turn is claimed — a
refused controller call, or a level the session did not drop — the repair is finished
there, synchronously, before the step reads its selection.

A **route with no adapter** is its own scope. Switching models *on that route* cannot
help — every model there fails the same way — but switching to another provider can, so
Two of those scopes were learned the hard way, from a real log:

- **Needs authorization** (`AUTH`) is a fact about *this account and this model*: the
  gateway answered, and the answer was "not for you" — an OAuth grant nobody completed, a
  model behind "star the repo first". Switching models cannot fix it, so it never switches,
  and burning the continuation budget on it would only produce the same answer twice. It is
  still recorded against the model, because "this one needs authorization" is exactly what
  the next fallback chain should skip.
- **The route does not answer** (`NETWORK`) is a fact about *nothing in particular*: DNS
  never resolved, the socket was refused, the certificate did not verify. The model was
  never asked, so blaming it would remove a perfectly good model from future chains.

it still switches. What it must not do is land in the model's health record: `error` is
in the set of reasons that make the fallback chain skip a model, and unlike `quota` that
verdict has no staleness escape, so a single route misconfiguration would have removed
an innocent model from every future chain permanently.

### A probe is not a routing event

"Unusable" and "move the conversation" are two different conclusions, and only a **failed
request** reaches the second one:

- A **failed request** (`agent/request-error`) is the live conversation hitting a wall. If
  the failure is model-scoped, the turn is retried on the next usable model and a banner
  names the model it moved for.
- A **failed probe** is an answer to a question you asked about a model. It records that
  model's health — so the *next* real switch skips it — but it does **not** touch whichever
  session happens to be using it. Moving a live conversation because of a diagnostic you
  ran would be switching models behind your back, which is the thing this design forbids.

Concretely, with `model-gamma` selected and its quota exhausted:

| Event | Selected model afterwards |
|---|---|
| you deep-probe `model-gamma`, and the probe fails | still `model-gamma` |
| a real request on `model-gamma` fails with per-model quota | `model-beta` (next usable), banner shown |
| a real request fails with an account-wide key limit (2008) | still `model-gamma` |

At most three automatic switches happen per turn, and if the chain finds nothing usable the
failure is passed through untouched rather than retried in a way that cannot succeed.

### Picking the work back up

Switching the model is only half the job: the turn that failed is gone, and until now this
plugin stopped there and told you to send the next message yourself. That is the wrong
place for the work — you asked the question to get an answer, not to learn which model
answered it.

So when a switch is committed for a failure that interrupted work, the plugin queues the
next turn itself, with `agent.followup()` — the SDK's own path for "make this the sole
ordinary message of its own turn". The queued message does not pretend to be you: its
source is `llm-manage-repair`, and it says what happened and what to do about it. It asks
the new model to **check the actual state first** — the files it wrote, the task list it
updated, the command output it was reading — and only then continue, without repeating
work that already landed. A turn that died mid-tool-call may have finished its side
effects; continuing as if it had not is how a recovery turns into a mess.

What that buys, and what it does not:

- The queue is only filled at the turn boundary (`turn/end`), after the switch is a fact.
- If a message is already waiting — you typed while it was recovering — the plugin does not
  add another; yours gets answered on the new model, which is what you wanted anyway.
- At most **two** continuations per request. A model that fails, is replaced, and fails
  again is a fact about the route, not about the turn; three identical attempts is not
  resilience, it is a loop. Typing a new message resets the budget, because that is a new
  request.
- If it declines to continue it says so, in the same place it used to say "next message
  only" — the banner names the reason instead of leaving you to guess.
- **"Took over" is a claim with evidence, not a hope.** The turn boundary can only prove
  that the frozen turn did not come back, so the record is written as `did not take over`
  and keeps its id. When a later turn finally produces a message on the target model, that
  same record is amended to `took over`, with the time it happened. Records written before
  this version have no id and are marked `legacy` in the history rather than silently
  counted as failures.
- Ordering is deliberate: an ordinary transient failure goes to the harness's own retry
  policy first (it is bounded, it knows the backoff), and only a failure that survives it
  is treated as a model problem worth moving. A request that is malformed, too large for
  the context, or wrong in shape is never a model problem and never switches — that just
  spends another model's quota on the same invalid request.

Both halves are exposed where the rest of the policy lives: **Model manager → Failover →
Automatic handling**, two switches with their trade-off written underneath. They write the
moment they move (a switch that only took effect after pressing a Save button somewhere
else would be lying about what the plugin is doing), and they are stored in the plugin's
own config document — the same one the fallback chain uses, so `cordis.patch.yml` is never
edited behind your back. The Loader row still works as the default: `recovery.retryFirst`
and `recovery.autoContinue`, both on, and the UI switch simply overrides it.

The same dialog now also carries the numbers behind that policy — switches per request
(default 3), continuations per request (default 2), and how long to wait for the session to
go idle before giving up (default 1000 ms). They are ordinary number fields: Enter or blur
commits, an out-of-range value is refused on the spot instead of being sent, and `0` is a
real value ("switch nothing", "continue nothing"), not an empty box.

One more check belongs here: if the **default model** — the one new sessions start on — is
itself retired, missing from the gateway directory, or sitting on an unhealthy record, the
picker says so in one line and offers the model the fallback chain would pick, with a
button that writes it. Otherwise every new session starts on a model that is about to
fail, and the recovery machinery is doing nothing but cleaning up after a choice made
somewhere else.

### The switch happens, and the banner proves it

Two mechanisms move a model, and the difference matters:

- **The session's own selection** (`sessionController.selectModel`) is what makes the
  change real. It validates the target against a registered adapter and appends a durable
  `model/selection` event, so the model the conversation uses actually changes and every
  surface agrees. The saved **default model is put back** afterwards: an automatic
  recovery has no business permanently changing which model new sessions start on.
- **A per-request override**, bound to the exact turn and step it was decided for, is what
  recovers the turn already in flight. It is needed because the harness applies the
  session selection during prompt assembly, which happens once per step — before the retry
  loop — so the session change alone would only take effect on the *next* turn.

The banner then reports what was **proven**, not what was decided. A switch is recorded as
pending, and only promoted to something you are shown once a committed assistant message
names the model that actually produced the response:

| What the answering model was | What the banner says |
|---|---|
| the model we switched to, work queued again | *Model switched and the work was picked back up* |
| the model we switched to, nothing queued | *Model switched*, with **Switch back** |
| a different model | *Switch did not take effect*, naming the model that actually ran |
| no message — the turn ended | *Switch attempted, turn not recovered* |

The earlier version wrote the banner when the switch was decided, so a retry that failed,
was aborted, or ran on a third route produced the same "switched automatically" text. It
also hardcoded "exhausted quota" as the cause for every failure, including failures that
were not about quota at all. Each reason now has its own wording, and the provider's raw
message is one clamped line with the full text on hover — inlined in full it was up to 400
characters, which made the banner taller than the conversation around it.

The banner carries the way forward, not just the news. When the plugin could not pick the
work back up itself — automatic recovery is off, the budget is spent, or a message was
already waiting — **Continue** appears instead: it fills an editable prompt ("continue from
where the previous answer stopped") into the draft and persists it, so the decision to
resend stays yours. It never sends on your behalf. **Switch back** is offered under the same
condition, since it moves the session's model back. **Stop switching** suppresses automatic
switching for that session until the harness restarts. **Dismiss** hides the report for
that switch only.

Some gateways report a *model's* quota exhaustion as HTTP 429, which the harness's own
classifier maps to a retryable `RATE_LIMIT` — indistinguishable from an account-wide rate
limit. The two need opposite handling, so this plugin reads the gateway's numeric business
code out of the error body instead of trusting the mapped code. The code table is at the
top of `index.js`; adjust it there if your gateway numbers things differently.

## Why probing is manual

`GET /v1/models` is free but is only a directory, not a callability list: a model can be
advertised and still fail on first use (wrong protocol, no capacity, image-only). Probing
each model deeply is therefore the only way to learn whether it works — and deep probes
spend the gateway's **per-key** rate budget, so a sweep large enough to be useful is also
large enough to rate-limit the user out of their own gateway.

Health is learned cheapest-first instead:

1. the free directory set,
2. real request failures as they happen (passive, zero extra traffic),
3. explicit probes the user starts, throttled at `probe.intervalMs` and capped at `probe.batch`.

Each row's status is the strongest evidence available, in this order:

| Status | Means | Shown when |
|---|---|---|
| `retired` | the gateway no longer lists the model | the directory read succeeded and the model is absent from it |
| the recorded health | a probe or a real request produced a verdict | any health record exists for that route+model |
| `ok` | the gateway lists it, and no failure is known | the directory read succeeded and there is no health record |
| `unknown` | nothing is known | the route exposes no `baseURL`, so there is no directory to compare against |

`ok` therefore means "listed and not known to be broken", which is weaker than "verified
working" — a model can be advertised and still fail on first use. The panel keeps the
distinction visible by showing the source alongside the status, so a row reads
**usable · deep probe** once it has actually answered and **usable · never checked** while it
has not. Neither is hidden: the second is the honest label for the majority of a large
catalogue, because verifying all of it at once is what would rate-limit you out.

## Verifying it

Five suites, all runnable without any particular deployment:

```
node verify.mjs          # Host half: registry, gateway, classification, fallback
node verify-client.mjs   # Browser half: renders the panel in jsdom and clicks it
node verify-browser.mjs  # Control geometry in a real engine (headless Chrome)
node verify-parity.mjs   # Did the shipped seats we take keep their capabilities?
node verify-live.mjs     # The whole thing against a RUNNING harness (opt-in)
```

`verify-parity.mjs` needs the harness **source** (`DSH_CHECKOUT`) and fails without
it, because its whole job is comparing this plugin against the shipped one. See
[docs/upstream-parity.md](docs/upstream-parity.md).

Each suite picks a mode automatically:

- **`real`** — this machine has a profile whose first provider route resolves, plus that
  route's credential. The settings under test are then the deployed ones, and the gateway
  directory is read live. This is the mode that catches a fixture agreeing with a wrong
  assumption.
- **`synthetic`** — otherwise. A local stub serves a synthetic catalogue, so every code
  path still runs: offline, deterministically, with no credential and no internal endpoint.

```
LLMM_VERIFY_MODE=synthetic node verify.mjs    # force a mode
DSH_CHECKOUT=/path/to/deepseek-harness node verify.mjs
```

`DSH_CHECKOUT` points at the harness checkout, which supplies the real Tool registry,
React and jsdom. It is not vendored here; the suites try a few conventional locations and
then tell you what to set.

`verify.mjs` also gates the **publish surface**: where the maintainer's
company-information scanner is present it fails if the runtime files (`index.js`,
`client.js`, `package.json`, `cordis.patch.yml`, `icon.svg`) contain anything identifying
a particular employer or internal service; in this published package the scanner is
absent, and the gate says so rather than reporting a pass it did not perform. The scanner
is not shipped because its own rule patterns have to quote the identifiers they look for.

Some checks exist because the live harness caught bugs a shallower suite passed:

- **The suites execute the registered tool**, not just register it. A definition can
  register cleanly and throw on its first call.
- **The fixture context enforces Cordis's inject guard**, so reading `ctx.llm` from
  `apply`'s own context fails exactly as it does live.
- **Never test one half alone.** The two halves can agree on every type and still disagree
  on a field name: the panel once folded `data.snapshot` while the Host returned the same
  state under `value`, so pin/favorite/hide updated nothing until the user reloaded by
  hand. A Host-only suite passed it, and so did a client suite whose other half was a mock
  returning whatever field the client asked for.
- **`verify-browser.mjs`** exists because jsdom has no layout: every
  `getBoundingClientRect()` returns zeros, so a tooltip's position and a button's width
  cannot be measured in-process. It loads the real panel into headless Chrome and asserts
  the geometry the design depends on, then skips with exit 0 when no Chrome-family binary
  is present (`CHROME_PATH` overrides).
- **`verify-live.mjs`** exists because every other suite builds its own page and hands the
  plugin a context it controls — so none of them can catch a contract they do not enforce.
  The plugin declared `slots`, `modelDirectories` and `sessions` at the top level, then
  called `modelDirectories.directoryFor()`, which internally reaches
  `this.ctx.remote.session`. Cordis checks the **consumer's** inject list, so in the live app
  that read threw `cannot get property "remote.session" without inject`, the picker's slot
  entry crashed, and because `Style` renders inside that same subtree the composer's model
  control lost **every rule in its stylesheet**. All three suites were green: the hand-built
  contexts were plain objects that enforced nothing.

  It opens the URL `dsh web` prints — in a real engine, against the real profile, real
  catalogue and real composer — and skips with exit 0 when no live harness answers:

  ```
  DSH_LIVE_URL='http://127.0.0.1:3080/?token=...' node verify-live.mjs
  DSH_LIVE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:3080/ DSH_LIVE_COOKIE='dsh-auth-...=...' node verify-live.mjs
  ```

### Two more contract mistakes the suites had to learn

Both of these shipped, both were green in every suite, and both were found by looking at
the running app. They are worth stating because each one changed what the suites assert.

**The theme cannot be supplied by the thing being tested.** The card was painted with
`--dsw-alias-bg-overlay`, which the plugin token contract labels *"Overlay and popover
background"* — a reasonable reading of the docs. Measured in the app it is `#e9ecf2`, a mid
grey, darker than the white composer it drops out of; DSH's own popovers paint the
translucent `--dsw-specific-menu` on a child layer with a backdrop blur instead. The suites
could not catch it because they defined that token themselves: `verify-browser.mjs` had
`--dsw-alias-bg-overlay:#fff`, and the deleted `preview.mjs` invented the same white. The
suites now carry the values the app actually resolves, and `verify-browser.mjs` fails if the
stylesheet reads any token its theme block does not define — 27 are read. `verify-live.mjs`
asserts the painted surface against the token's real value.

**A stylesheet in a template literal can truncate without a syntax error.** A backtick or
`${` inside a CSS comment ends the literal early. The pieces often still re-parse as
JavaScript, so `node --check` passes, and the failure that reaches you is a browser refusing
the import — the whole client half silently absent. `verify-client.mjs` extracts the literal
and asserts it is intact, which catches the case that parses but is wrong.

  The lesson generalizes past this bug: **a suite that supplies the context cannot verify
  the context.** An inject declaration is a contract with the runtime, and only the runtime
  can check it.

### Looking at the panel without restarting

```
DSH_LIVE_URL='http://127.0.0.1:3080/?token=…' node screenshot.mjs
```

Captures the panel and the model picker out of the running harness, light and dark, into
`docs/` — which is gitignored, so the images stay on your machine. It is the preview of record
because it supplies nothing: it opens the URL `dsh web` printed and photographs what is there.

The images are not committed because a capture of a real harness is a picture of the routes
and model inventory that harness is configured with. That is the maintainer's deployment, and
it is also the one kind of content a text scan cannot inspect: a route name rendered into a
PNG reads as PNG bytes, matches no rule, and passes. Four such screenshots were published
before anyone noticed. `build-public.mjs` now refuses to stage any binary asset, and
`scan-company-info.mjs` reports files it cannot read as unscannable rather than counting them
as clean — the whitelist that decided which extensions to open was the whole defect.

This replaced a `preview.mjs` that rendered the plugin into a hand-written page with a
hand-written theme. That page defined `--dsw-alias-bg-overlay:#fff` — a value the token never
has in the app, where it is `#e9ecf2` — and defined only the 14 tokens the plugin contract
documents while the stylesheet reads 27. The mock showed a white card; the app painted a grey
one. A preview that supplies its own theme cannot show you the theme, and an approved mock is
worse than no mock: it is the reason the grey card shipped.

The replacement supplies nothing of its own and skips with exit 0 when no harness answers, so
it never reports a picture it did not take. To reach the panel it sends the `settings.open`
chord — `primary+alt+Comma` on web, not the plain `primary+Comma` the desktop runtime uses —
then clicks through the settings nav until the panel appears, matching no label because the
labels are localised. A development aid, not a test.

## Where it appears

- **Settings → Models → the provider card**: the management panel.
- **The composer model picker**: this plugin's picker in the shipped picker's seat — one
  entry, one panel, with the shipped capabilities (search, provider grouping, keyboard
  roaming, a trigger that names the current model and level) plus levels, probes, the
  manager and the usage figures. `selector.mode: native` hands the seat back to the shipped
  picker and leaves only the health dot, level chip and listing badge on its rows.
- **Above the composer**: a banner when this session's model was switched.

### Decorating the shipped picker

As of DSH 0.2.2 the shipped picker carries its own reasoning levels, its own badges and the
provider-default effort, so this plugin stopped shadowing it: the seat belongs to the owner
and we contribute the marks the owner cannot know — the health verdict, the proficiency
level use has earned, and the listing badge.

That is a slot contribution (`conversation.input.model.label`), and two of its rules decided
the implementation:

- A contribution **replaces** the owner's fallback, so the model name is ours to draw. A

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-mermaid-plus

[![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/dsh-mermaid-plus.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-mermaid-plus)
[![license](https://img.shields.io/npm/l/dsh-mermaid-plus.svg)](LICENSE)
[![DSH](https://img.shields.io/badge/DSH-0.2.0--rc.2-4b5563)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-Harness)
[![install](https://img.shields.io/badge/dsh%20plugin%20add-dsh--mermaid--plus-5b8def)](#install)

Mermaid diagrams for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-Harness) — rendered **when a diagram scrolls into view** by default, with an on-demand mode for when a layout pass per diagram is not worth it.

**Configure it in Settings → General.** Two rows belong to this plugin: *Mermaid diagrams* picks when a diagram renders (on demand · when visible · always) and *Diagram layout* picks the engine (compact ELK · standard dagre). Defaults: when visible, compact.

![The plugin's two rows in Settings → General: Mermaid diagrams and Diagram layout](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pidongqianqian/dsh-mermaid-plus/main/docs/settings.png)

[中文说明](#中文说明)

---

## Screenshots

A rendered diagram in its card. The header switches to the source, copies it, or opens the diagram fullscreen:

![A mermaid card with a rendered diagram, and Code, Copy and Expand controls](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pidongqianqian/dsh-mermaid-plus/main/docs/card.png)

Fullscreen viewer, light and dark. The sheet is painted with the palette the diagram was rendered for, so labels stay readable in both themes — the bug that started this viewer was black text on a dark backdrop:

![Fullscreen mermaid viewer on a light sheet](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pidongqianqian/dsh-mermaid-plus/main/docs/viewer-light.png)

![Fullscreen mermaid viewer on a dark sheet](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pidongqianqian/dsh-mermaid-plus/main/docs/viewer-dark.png)

### The same diagram, two layout engines

In a conversation column, width is what breaks a diagram: a wide graph has to be panned,
a narrow one just scrolls with the page. ELK is the default; *Settings → General →
Diagram layout* switches to dagre.

| dagre (standard) | ELK (compact, default) |
|---|---|
| ![The architecture diagram laid out by dagre, 1956 px wide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pidongqianqian/dsh-mermaid-plus/main/docs/layout-dagre.png) | ![The same architecture diagram laid out by ELK, 1249 px wide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pidongqianqian/dsh-mermaid-plus/main/docs/layout-elk.png) |
| 1956 × 1624 px | **1249 × 1833 px** (−36% width) |

Measured on the corpus in [`test/bench/`](test/bench/): ELK costs 5–20 ms per diagram
(and is faster on the 150-node case) while cutting the width of wide diagrams by
31–79%. See [`test/bench/results.md`](test/bench/results.md).

## What it does

A fenced ` ```mermaid ` block in the conversation (or in a Markdown file preview) becomes a card:

- **Compact layout by default** — diagrams are layered with ELK, Mermaid's compact
  engine. On the benchmark corpus it cuts the width of wide diagrams by 31–79% at a
  cost of a few milliseconds per diagram; *Settings → General → Diagram layout*
  switches to the standard dagre layout, and switching re-draws the diagrams already
  on screen.
- **When visible (default)** — a diagram renders the first time its card scrolls into view. The 5.4 MB Mermaid runtime loads then, not at page load, so a transcript nobody scrolls costs nothing.
- **On demand** — the source stays visible and a `Diagram` button waits in the card header; nothing is downloaded or laid out until you press it.
- **Always** — renders as soon as the block appears (the classic behaviour).

Every rendered diagram can be opened **fullscreen** with zoom and pan, which is the point: a wide flowchart squeezed into the message column is unreadable, while the same diagram at natural size is fine.

## Features

- Renders `mermaid`, `mermaidjs`, `mmd` and unlabelled blocks that start with a diagram keyword.
- Supports the diagram types the bundled Mermaid build ships: `flowchart`/`graph`, `sequenceDiagram`, `classDiagram`, `stateDiagram`, `erDiagram`, `gantt`, `pie`, `mindmap`, `journey`, `timeline`, `quadrantChart`, `xychart`, `gitGraph`, `requirementDiagram`, `C4`, `block-beta`, `packet-beta`, `sankey-beta`, `kanban`, `architecture-beta`, and more.
- **Theme-aware**: diagram colours are derived from the app's live design tokens, and a palette change re-renders only the diagrams you are looking at.
- **Streaming-safe**: a block is handed to Mermaid only after its source settles, so a half-written fence never flashes a parse error.
- **Cached**: a rendered diagram is kept by source + palette + layout engine, so switching between Code and Diagram, or reopening the viewer, costs nothing.
- **Copy**: the card header copies the fence source, replacing the code block's own toolbar when the card replaces it.
- **Coexists with other renderers**: a block another Mermaid renderer already claimed, and its error echo, are left alone.
- **Takes over the code-block frame, not the transcript**: the card replaces the application's frame, keeps its syntax-highlighted body, and puts the frame back on unmount.
- **Fullscreen viewer**: wheel zoom, drag to pan, double-click to fit, `Esc` to close, focus-trapped dialog, restores focus and page scrolling.
- Falls back to the visible source with a short error line when a diagram does not parse.
- Unmounting restores every code block to its original place in the transcript.

## Settings

*Settings → General* has two rows owned by this plugin — the same rows shown at the
top of this page:

| Row | Values | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Mermaid diagrams** | On demand · When visible · Always | When visible |
| **Diagram layout** | Compact (ELK) · Standard (dagre) | Compact |

## Benchmarks

[`test/bench/`](test/bench/) is a reproducible benchmark (nine diagrams, real Chrome
over CDP with the real clock) used to choose the layout default and to re-check an
upgrade. Results: [`test/bench/results.md`](test/bench/results.md).

## Install

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add dsh-mermaid-plus
```

Or install it from a catalog in **Settings → Plugins → Marketplace** (see the [DSH 1024Store](https://github.com/imsai-sh/awesome-deepseek-harness-plugins) listing). Restart the app or reload the page afterwards.

The Mermaid runtime is **bundled** with the package (`vendor/mermaid.esm.min.mjs`, Mermaid 12.2.0) and served from the plugin's own Host route, so rendering works offline and no CDN is contacted. The fullscreen viewer and card never send diagram source anywhere.

## Settings

**Settings → General → Mermaid diagrams** offers the three modes. The choice is stored per page origin and is namespaced by package name, so it never collides with another diagram plugin.

## Compatibility

- Built and verified against DSH `0.2.0-rc.2`; last checked on Desktop `2.0.21-next` (code-block DOM `div.md-code-block > [data-code-block-content] > pre`).
- DSH is a developer preview: client plugin contracts, slot keys, and rendered Markdown can change between releases. This plugin decorates the rendered `<pre><code>` output, which is the part most likely to shift; if a release breaks it, the cards simply stop appearing and the code blocks stay intact.
- Requires a browser or Electron renderer with `IntersectionObserver` (used only in "when visible" mode) and `DOMParser`.

## How it works

- **Host half** (`index.js`) mounts one prefix route that serves the vendored Mermaid ES module. The route is derived from the package name (`/x-dsh-mermaid-plus`), so two diagram plugins can coexist.
- **Browser half** (`client.js`) is a normal DSH client bundle: it registers a root-scoped occupant on `shell.overlay` (which exists before any session), plus a status row and the settings row. It never imports Harness client packages and never touches the model's context.
- Because the shipped Markdown renderer exposes no code-block extension point, the browser half decorates the rendered output: it moves a mermaid `<pre>` into a card it owns, and puts it back on unmount. The original DOM node is preserved, so the transcript, copy, and select all keep working.

## Troubleshooting

The browser half reports lifecycle events to its Host half, which appends them to a bounded log:

```
<os tmp>/dsh-mermaid-plus/report.json
```

It records lifecycle events only — `start`, `apply-ok`, `apply-throw`, `adopted`, `render-ok`, `render-error`, `blocks-unmatched` — with counts, not document text: no diagram source, no file contents, no paths beyond the plugin's own. If diagrams stop appearing, that file plus the browser console (a failed import) usually identifies the cause.

## Development

The plugin has no build step for its own code: `index.js` and `client.js` run as they are. Only `vendor/mermaid.esm.min.mjs` is generated, and only when the bundled Mermaid version changes.

```sh
npm install                 # mermaid 12.2.0, esbuild, jsdom
node build.mjs              # rebuild vendor/mermaid.esm.min.mjs
node test/run.mjs           # host route, real cordis mount, jsdom browser-half behaviour
node test/serve-e2e.mjs     # then open http://127.0.0.1:8732/ for 35 real-browser cases
node tools/doctor.mjs       # activation, install mode, last browser events
node tools/dev-sync.mjs     # copy this checkout over an npm-installed copy
```

[`docs/development.md`](docs/development.md) covers the debug loop, what each symptom means, and the release flow.

## License

## Contributing

The plugin is intentionally small: two JavaScript files, no runtime dependencies,
no build step for its own code. Bug reports with a minimal diagram source and
contributions of any size are welcome.

- [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](CONTRIBUTING.md) — setup, the test loop, where each change goes, PR expectations.
- [`docs/development.md`](docs/development.md) — the debug loop, what each symptom means, release flow.
- [`CHANGELOG.md`](CHANGELOG.md) — what changed and why.
- [`SECURITY.md`](SECURITY.md) — private vulnerability reporting.

Credits: **Dunianggg** (pull request #1 — coexistence, the code-block frame,
`suppressErrorRendering`) and **Songyanglin-curious** (the Mermaid 12 / ELK fork —
the ELK direction, render-validity guards, cache versioning, the Windows build fix)
are recorded in [`CREDITS.md`](https://github.com/pidongqianqian/dsh-mermaid-plus/blob/main/CREDITS.md).

Wanted, with a working prototype in a community fork:

- **Compact layout (ELK)** — Mermaid 12's ELK layout makes wide diagrams like the architecture sample dramatically more readable; it costs runtime size and a license notice, so it needs a design (a setting, or automatic by diagram size) before it lands.
- **Diagram export** — SVG and PNG from the viewer, with the theme background baked in.
- **More browser fixtures** — one case per diagram type keeps the decoration layer honest across DSH upgrades.

See [issue #2](https://github.com/pidongqianqian/dsh-mermaid-plus/issues/2) for the invitation and the review notes.

## License

MIT. The bundle also carries Mermaid (MIT) and its layout engine ELK (EPL-2.0);
see [`THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md`](THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md) and `vendor/*.LICENSE`.

## 中文说明

把对话（以及 Markdown 预览）里的 ` ```mermaid ` 代码块渲染成图表卡片。

**配置在 设置 → 通用**。有本插件自己的两行：「Mermaid 图表」决定什么时候渲染（手动 · 滚动可见 · 立即），「图表布局」决定布局引擎（紧凑 ELK · 标准 dagre）。默认是「滚动可见 + 紧凑」。

**默认「滚动可见」**：卡片第一次滚入视口时才加载 Mermaid（约 5.4 MB）并渲染，页面打开时不加载。另外两种模式是「按需」（代码块保持源码可见，点卡片上的「图形」才渲染）和「立即」（出现即渲染）。

**默认使用 ELK 紧凑布局**。同一张架构图，标准布局（dagre）宽 1956 px，ELK 宽 1249 px（−36%）；在基准里宽图普遍收窄 31–79%，代价是每张图多 5–20 ms。设置里可以切回标准布局，切换会立刻重绘已经显示的图——数据见 `test/bench/results.md`。

渲染后的图表可以**全屏放大**：滚轮缩放、拖动平移、双击适应窗口、`Esc` 关闭；全屏只克隆已有 SVG，不会重新渲染。

其他特性：

- 配色取自应用当前的 `--dsw-*` 设计令牌，明暗主题各自适配；主题切换只重绘你正在看的图。
- 流式输出期间不会渲染半截源码。
- 渲染结果按「配色 + 源码 + 布局引擎」缓存，切换「代码/图形」或重开全屏都是零成本。
- 卡片头部可以**复制源码**；当卡片取代应用自己的代码块框时，语言栏与复制按钮的职责由卡片承担。
- 与其它 Mermaid 渲染器共存：被别的渲染器标记过的块、以及它失败时回显的源码，都不会被重复接管。
- 解析失败时保留源码并给一行错误提示；ELK 排不出来的图会自动用 dagre 重试一次。
- 卸载时把每个代码块（连同应用原来的代码框）放回原位，不破坏对话内容。

两个设置在 **设置 → 通用**：

| 行 | 选项 | 默认 |
|---|---|---|
| **Mermaid 图表** | 手动 · 滚动可见 · 立即 | 滚动可见 |
| **图表布局** | 紧凑（ELK） · 标准（dagre） | 紧凑 |

Mermaid 运行时随包内置（12.2.0），由插件自己的 Host 路由提供，**不访问 CDN、离线可用**，图表源码不会发往任何地方。

其中 ELK 布局引擎以 EPL-2.0 随包分发（插件自身仍是 MIT），许可证与来源见 [`THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md`](THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md)。

兼容 DSH `0.2.0-rc.2`（桌面版已在 2.0.21-next 上验证）。DSH 处于开发者预览阶段，客户端插件契约可能变化；本插件装饰渲染后的 `<pre><code>`，是最容易受影响的一层——若某次升级后卡片不再出现，代码块本身仍然完好。

排障：浏览器半侧会把生命周期事件报告给 Host，写入 `<系统临时目录>/dsh-mermaid-plus/report.json`（`start` / `adopted` / `render-ok` / `render-error` / `apply-ok` / `apply-throw`）。

# dsh-pi-line

Bundle [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH) yang memasang agent preset
**`software-build`**: loadout coding ramping gaya [pi](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi) — persona pendek
yang *menggantikan* system prompt besar, tool seperlunya (read / write / edit batch / bash), plus timeout
context via grup compaction.

Satu repo, satu paket, dua artefak:

| Artefak | Lokasi | Fungsi |
|---|---|---|
| Preset `software-build` | `cordis.patch.yml` (row `@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset`) | komposisi persona + tool |
| Tool `edit` batch | `lib/tool-edit-batch.js` | banyak targeted replacement dalam satu call, dicocokkan ke isi file **ORIGINAL** |

## Mekanisme pengemasan (dan kenapa bukan monorepo dua paket)

Dua opsi diuji langsung dengan pnpm 12.18 di mesin pengembangan:

**1. Monorepo dua paket + dependency silang lewat git — GAGAL.**

```
$ pnpm add "git+file:///tmp/mono-probe#path:/packages/a"
✗ ERR_PNPM_EXOTIC_SUBDEP
  Exotic dependency "probe-b" (resolved via git-repository) is not allowed in
  subdependencies when blockExoticSubdeps is enabled
```

pnpm 12 memblokir *exotic subdependency* (git/tarball) secara default, jadi paket preset tidak boleh
bergantung pada paket tool lewat spec git/`#path:`. Bisa juga lewat npm, tapi itu menambah langkah rilis
(publish 2 paket) dan kredensial registry.

**2. Nama relatif di dalam patch preset — TIDAK DIDUKUNG.**

`anchorInsertedPluginNames()` di `@deepseek-ai/dsh-app-boot` memang mengubah nama relatif/absolut menjadi
`file://` URL, **tetapi hanya** untuk row hasil `insert` dan hanya me-rekursi ke row `cordis:group`
(`entry.group && Array.isArray(entry.config)`). Row `@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset` menyimpan anaknya di
`config.plugins`, yang **tidak** dikunjungi — sudah diverifikasi: nama tetap `./lib/tool-edit-batch.js`.

**3. Satu paket, row tool memakai nama paket — DIPAKAI.**

`package.json` paket ini menetapkan:

```json
"main": "lib/tool-edit-batch.js",
"exports": { ".": "./lib/tool-edit-batch.js" },
"dsh": { "bundle": { "patch": "./cordis.patch.yml" } }
```

Sehingga di dalam preset, row tool cukup:

```yaml
- id: tool-edit-batch
  name: 'dsh-pi-line'
```

Loader me-resolve nama paket dari `node_modules` profile — pola yang sama dengan plugin lain di profile DSH
(mis. `dsh-plugin-mobile-gateway`), dan sudah terbukti jalan untuk paket tool yang dipasang sebagai dependency
biasa. Package ini juga yang memasang dependency registry-nya (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools`, `dsh-fs`,
`schemastery`), jadi `lib/tool-edit-batch.js` bisa me-resolve import-nya lewat `nodeLinker: hoisted`
(bawaan template profile DSH).

Hasilnya: **satu spec install, satu tag, tanpa publish, tanpa dependency silang.**

## Instalasi (device mana pun)

Prasyarat: DSH `0.2.1-rc.5`, Node ≥ 22, profile `web` sudah ada. Cek: `dsh --version && node -v`.

### 1. Web UI (disarankan — ada inspect & rollback)

1. `http://<host>:3080/` → sidebar **Plugins** → **Add plugin**
2. Spec: `github:RafiMM0609/dsh-pi-line#v1.0.0`
   (atau `dsh-pi-line@1.0.0` bila di-publish ke npm, atau `link:/abs/path/dsh-pi-line` untuk uji lokal)
3. **Inspect**: harus `status: accepted` dan terdeteksi sebagai bundle (kalau `not-a-bundle` → field
   `dsh.bundle.patch` tidak terbaca)
4. **Install**, lalu cek `application`:
   - `applied` → preset langsung ada di roster
   - `restart-required` → restart DSH Web di device itu
5. Bundle otomatis masuk `dsh.profile.bundles` dan aktif.

> Installer akan menarik dependency `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools`, `dsh-fs`, `schemastery` dari registry yang
> dikonfigurasi pnpm di device itu (semuanya tersedia di npm/npmmirror). Tidak ada build script → tidak ada
> `pendingBuilds` yang perlu approval.

### 2. Dari HP (lewat gateway device itu)

Ke koneksi **control** dengan token device yang sudah ter-pair:

```json
{"type":"plugin-inspect","requestId":"i1","spec":"github:RafiMM0609/dsh-pi-line#v1.0.0"}
{"type":"plugin-install","requestId":"p1","spec":"github:RafiMM0609/dsh-pi-line#v1.0.0"}
{"type":"plugin-catalog","requestId":"c1"}
```

Progres: `plugin-install-state` (`installing`/`cancelling`/`applying`) + `plugin-install-log`.
Hasil: `plugin-install-result`. Koneksi putus → `{"type":"plugin-install-status","installId":"p1"}`;
jangan ulangi install dengan `requestId` baru.

### 3. CLI

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add github:RafiMM0609/dsh-pi-line#v1.0.0
```

CLI hanya menjalankan `pnpm add`, jadi nama paket **harus** ditambahkan sendiri ke `dsh.profile.bundles`
di `~/.dsh/profiles/web/package.json` (paling akhir = prioritas terendah), lalu restart DSH di device itu:

```json
"dsh": {
  "profile": {
    "bundles": [
      "@deepseek-ai/dsh-base",
      "@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app",
      "dsh-pi-line"
    ]
  }
}
```

## Verifikasi

```bash
# 1) baris preset masuk komposisi, dan nama tool sudah jadi file:// URL
dsh --profile web --dump-config | grep -n -A10 preset-software-build

# 2) roster dari sisi app/gateway: entri software-build ada dan TANPA field "broken"
#    (selector preset di Web UI, atau /mgw/pair + probe WS)

# 3) fungsional: sesi baru dengan preset "software-build"
#    - persona pendek (bukan system prompt besar)
#    - tool edit batch menerima {"path": "...", "edits": [...]}
```

## Uninstall / rollback

1. Plugins page → **toggle off** bundle (preset hilang dari roster; sesi lama tetap memakai komposisinya),
   lalu **Remove**.
2. Alternatif manual: hapus blok `- insert:` dengan `id: preset-software-build` dari
   `~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml`, lalu restart.

## Jebakan

1. **Jangan** memasang bundle ini di device yang masih punya blok manual `preset-software-build` di
   `cordis.patch.yml` → id row duplikat. Cek dulu:
   `grep -n preset-software-build ~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml`
   Hapus blok manualnya **setelah** bundle terpasang dan roster bersih.
2. **Versi harness harus sama** (`0.2.1-rc.5`): `engines.dsh` + dependency inti di-pin exact. Beda versi
   ditolak gate kompatibilitas → pakai `dsh plugin allow-version` / version-exemption, jangan dipaksa.
3. Urutan layer: **bundle dulu**, baru `cordis.patch.yml` profil. Override per-device (mis. ganti `prefix`
   persona) tulis di `cordis.patch.yml` — itu menang.
4. Tool ini memakai `ctx.fs` dan gate `fs/edit-intent` yang sama dengan `edit` bawaan; jangan mount dua tool
   `edit` sekaligus (`tool-fs` di preset ini disetel `edit: false`).

## Struktur repo

```
dsh-pi-line/
├── cordis.patch.yml        # row preset software-build (+ rujukan ./lib/tool-edit-batch.js)
├── lib/tool-edit-batch.js  # tool edit batch (salinan apa adanya dari profil yang terbukti jalan)
├── package.json            # name, dsh.bundle.patch, repository, dependency registry
├── README.md
├── LICENSE
└── .gitignore
```

## Status verifikasi (saat paket dibuat)

Diuji pada mesin pengembangan dengan DSH `0.2.1-rc.5`, **tanpa menyentuh instalasi yang sedang aktif**
(DSH_HOME terpisah di `/tmp`, port 3099):

| Uji | Hasil |
|---|---|
| `pnpm add file:<paket>` di profile bersih (`nodeLinker: hoisted`) | ✅ paket + dependency registry terpasang, `files` lengkap (`cordis.patch.yml`, `lib/tool-edit-batch.js`) |
| `dsh --profile web --dump-config` | ✅ row `preset-software-build` muncul; row `tool-edit-batch` = `dsh-pi-line` |
| boot instance + query `agent-presets` lewat gateway | ✅ `software-build` ada, **`broken` count 0** → semua row preset (termasuk tool) berhasil start |
| `engines.dsh` / gate kompatibilitas | ✅ lolos (runtime 0.2.1-rc.5) |

Catatan: import modul plugin dari Node polos di profile gagal (`@deepseek-ai/cordis` tidak ada di profile,
karena `autoInstallPeers: false`), tetapi loader DSH me-resolve modul inti harness sendiri — terbukti dari
`broken: 0` di atas. Jadi jangan mount tool ini di luar loader DSH.

## Lisensi

MIT — lihat `LICENSE`.

decision.reason: Static evidence chain reviewed. MIT, documented Git-source installation and engines.dsh 0.2.1-rc.5 are explicit; no lifecycle hooks. The same-commit patch mounts its own tool-edit-batch implementation alongside official plugins. Edits use ctx.fs.resolve, the fs/edit-intent waterfall, host read/write and replaceIfVersion with the execution signal; no raw child-process edit path was observed. No candidate code or lifecycle hooks were executed; runtime safety and compatibility are unproven.

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# retire-this-session

Retire a DSH session together with its forked and subagent descendants: archive
the tree now, move the log directories into the Session-Time-Vault at the next
start.

Nothing is deleted. Work still running in the tree is cancelled, not killed, and
no `systemd` unit hook is involved, so the plugin behaves identically on Linux,
macOS, and Windows.

## Usage

1. Tell the session to retire itself.

   ![Typing "retire this session" into the composer](assets/retire1.png)

2. Choose **Retire** in the confirmation.

   ![The confirmation dialog offering Retire or Cancel](assets/retire2.png)

3. The session moves to the retired list and is hidden, and a new session starts
   immediately.

   ![A fresh session right after the retirement](assets/retire3.png)

## What it does

`retire_session` (model-facing tool):

`retire_session dry run` — call it with `dry_run: true` to see the plan without
changing anything: it reads the headers, builds the tree, resolves each member's
directory, and reports them. It asks no question, archives nothing, queues
nothing, and never reaches the confirmation in step 3 or the archiving after it.
Use it to inspect the tree before the real call.

1. reads every stored header, including archived forks that the UI does not show;
2. builds the tree as the transitive closure of `parentSession` from the calling
   session;
3. asks the human in the UI to confirm (options `Retire` / `Cancel`) and does
   nothing unless `Retire` is chosen — the tool has no self-approval path, and
   without the `userQuestions` service it refuses rather than proceeding;
4. refuses when the root has no log or when a member's `cwd` differs from the
   root's, or when a member is pinned; an already-archived member is skipped
   instead of refused, so a partly retired tree can still be finished and a
   second call is a no-op;
5. writes each member's artifact directory to
   `<dshHome>/session-retirement-queue.json` **before** archiving anything;
6. archives every member through
   `ctx.workspaceRegistry.archiveSession(id, { stopActivity: true })`, children
   first and the root last, which is reversible, hides the session from every
   grouping surface, blocks its next step, drops any pin, cancels any turn, job,
   subagent, or schedule still running in the tree, and emits the change event
   the Web UI already reacts to.

Because the root's archive cancels the calling turn, `retire_session` returns as
`aborted` even when the retirement succeeded. The archive event in the UI is the
authoritative outcome, and the session does not accept another step.

At the next start the plugin drains that queue, after `ctx.inject` hands it the
workspace registry and the session store: `rename` into
`<dshHome>/Session-Time-Vault/<id>`, falling back to copy-then-remove when the
vault is on another filesystem. A live session, an existing vault entry, a
vanished directory, and an entry whose session is no longer archived are all
handled without failing the rest; survivors stay queued. The archive gate is
what keeps a crash between the queue write and the archive from moving the log
of a session that is still listed, and waiting for the registry is what keeps a
startup earlier than the registry from postponing the drain indefinitely.

## Why not move immediately

The JSONL backend appends with `open(path, 'a')` → write → fsync → close, and the
lease verifies the locked inode against the lock path. Renaming a live session's
directory makes the next append recreate the old path: the vault gets a truncated
log and the split continues silently. At startup nothing holds those files, so
the move is safe — and portable, which is what a `systemd` `ExecStopPost` hook is
not.

## Where retired logs go, and the Web UI log

The retired directories are the backup: they move to
`<dshHome>/Session-Time-Vault/<session-id>` and stay there. Unarchiving restores
the list row, not the directory.

The Web UI's own diagnostics go to `<dshHome>/gui-log.log` (boot manifest, failed
`/api` calls, script errors). Some setups append there through a separate logging
plugin; retirement never touches it either way. When a page misbehaves after a
restart, read that file before blaming the retirement:

```sh
tail -n 50 ~/.dsh/gui-log.log
```

The confirmation dialog prints both paths.

## Install

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add retire-this-session
```

Restart the service once (`systemctl --user restart dsh`, or stop and start it
however you run DSH) so the new bundle composes. The `retire_session` tool then
appears in the next session.

To work on a local checkout instead:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add "retire-this-session@link:$PWD"
```

Verify composition (also writes `cordis.yml` into the profile, so run it outside
the service's read-only sandbox):

```sh
dsh --profile web --dump-config | grep session-retirement
```

## Config

The patch row needs no config; every path defaults from `$DSH_HOME` (or `~/.dsh`
when it is unset). Override a path from the profile's `cordis.patch.yml` when
needed; relative values resolve against `$DSH_HOME`:

```yaml
- id: session-retirement
  config:
    vaultDir: Session-Time-Vault
    queueFile: session-retirement-queue.json
    guiLogFile: gui-log.log
```

## Uninstall

Archive and unarchive stay DSH's own state and can be changed from the UI at any
time. Removing the plugin stops the drain; already-archived sessions keep their
flags and their logs stay in `sessions/`. A non-empty
`session-retirement-queue.json` then needs a manual move.

## Tests

```sh
node --test test/*.test.js
```

Twenty-two tests cover the tree closure, every refusal, directory discovery,
queue atomicity, the drain's move/live/archived/existing/missing behaviour,
root-last archiving with rollback, and the archive path against a host that
refuses an active session unless `stopActivity` is passed.

## License

MIT. See [LICENSE](LICENSE).

decision.reason: Static evidence chain reviewed. MIT, documented local Git-source installation and engines.dsh at least 0.2.0 are explicit; no lifecycle hooks. Fixed index.js/plan.js implement dry-run planning and require a userQuestions Retire selection before queuing/archiveSession with stopActivity. Startup relocation checks live/archived state; cross-device moves copy then remove the old directory. The filesystem/session effects are disclosed, not runtime-certified. No candidate code or lifecycle hooks were executed; runtime safety and compatibility are unproven.

# mont-forge

生产级工程技能包 —— **44 个技能**，覆盖软件开发生命周期从 `spec` 到 `ship`，并补入大跨度规划、领域建模、issue 分诊等能力。
**一个仓库，多端通用**：同一份 `skills/` 内容真源，通过各平台的外壳声明，
可安装到 DSH、Pi、Claude Code、Codex、Gemini、OpenCode 等主流 AI 编码代理。

> **来源声明**：本仓库合并自两个 MIT 项目 ——
> [`addyosmani/agent-skills`](https://github.com/addyosmani/agent-skills)（作者 Addy Osmani，25 个技能，构成骨架）
> 与 [`mattpocock/skills`](https://github.com/mattpocock/skills)（作者 Matt Pocock，19 个独有技能，补入锋利切口）。
> 归因见 [NOTICE.md](NOTICE.md)、[LICENSE](LICENSE)、[LICENSE-mattpocock](LICENSE-mattpocock)。

## 版本

`0.1.1`

## 技能构成

| 来源 | 数量 | 说明 |
|---|---|---|
| addyosmani/agent-skills | 25 | 生命周期骨架（定义/规划/构建/验证/评审/交付） |
| mattpocock/skills | 19 | 独有能力（大规模规划、领域建模、分诊、复盘、教学等） |
| **合计** | **44** | 全部遵循 [Agent Skills 规范](https://agentskills.io/specification) |

## 多端安装

| 平台 | 外壳 | 安装方式 |
|------|------|----------|
| **DSH（npm，推荐）** | `dsh` key + `cordis.patch.yml` | `dsh plugin --profile <profile> add mont-forge` |
| **DSH（市场）** | `market/index.json` | 插件市场添加索引源，点击安装/卸载 |
| **DSH（GitHub 订阅）** | 根 `skills/` | Skills Manager「发现 → GitHub 仓库订阅」本仓库 |
| **Pi** | `pi` key + `pi-package` keyword | `pi install git:github.com/royrao2007/mont-forge` |
| **Claude Code** | `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` | `/plugin marketplace add royrao2007/mont-forge` |
| **Codex** | `.codex-plugin/plugin.json` | Codex 插件市场添加本仓库 |
| **Gemini** | `.gemini/commands/*.toml` + `commands/*.toml` | Gemini 订阅本仓库 |
| **OpenCode** | 根 `skills/`（Agent Skills 规范） | 订阅本仓库，自动发现 `skills/` |

所有平台都消费同一份 `skills/<name>/SKILL.md`（遵循 [Agent Skills 规范](https://agentskills.io/specification)），
外壳只是各平台的"入口声明"，不复制技能内容。

> **网络受限环境建议用 npm 安装**：走 registry（海外 `registry.npmjs.org`，国内
> `registry.npmmirror.com`），不依赖 `github.com` 直连。

### 手动部署到 DSH 原生技能目录（无需网络）

```powershell
# 把全部技能复制到 DSH 技能目录，热加载立即生效
Copy-Item .\skills\* "$env:DSH_HOME\skills\" -Recurse -Force

# 卸载（只删本仓库部署的技能）
.\scripts\uninstall-from-dsh.ps1
```

## 技能清单（44 个）

### 来自 addyosmani/agent-skills（25 个，生命周期骨架）

按软件开发生命周期阶段分组：

| 阶段 | 技能 |
|------|------|
| **定义 Define** | `interview-me`、`idea-refine`、`spec-driven-development` |
| **规划 Plan** | `planning-and-task-breakdown` |
| **构建 Build** | `incremental-implementation`、`test-driven-development`、`source-driven-development`、`doubt-driven-development`、`context-engineering`、`constraint-driven-development`、`frontend-ui-engineering`、`api-and-interface-design` |
| **验证 Verify** | `browser-testing-with-devtools`、`debugging-and-error-recovery` |
| **评审 Review** | `code-review-and-quality`、`code-simplification`、`security-and-hardening`、`performance-optimization` |
| **交付 Ship** | `git-workflow-and-versioning`、`ci-cd-and-automation`、`deprecation-and-migration`、`documentation-and-adrs`、`observability-and-instrumentation`、`shipping-and-launch` |
| **元技能 Meta** | `using-agent-skills` |

### 来自 mattpocock/skills（19 个，独有能力）

| 类别 | 技能 |
|------|------|
| **规划与拆解** | `wayfinder`（跨多个会话的大规模工作地图）、`to-tickets`（拆成带阻塞边的 tracer-bullet 票）、`to-spec`（对话转规格） |
| **设计** | `codebase-design`（深模块设计词汇）、`domain-modeling`（领域建模 / GLOSSARY）、`improve-codebase-architecture`（架构深化扫描） |
| **执行** | `implement`（按 spec/票执行）、`prototype`（一次性原型验证设计） |
| **质量** | `triage`（issue 分诊状态机）、`retro`（会话复盘）、`pr`（写 PR 描述） |
| **协作** | `grilling`（设计树式连环拷问）、`grill-me`（精确触发词别名，转发到 `grilling`）、`to-questionnaire`（把答不了的决策转成问卷） |
| **知识** | `research`（派后台 agent 查一手资料）、`teach`（教学）、`writing-for-agents`（给 agent 写文档） |
| **配置** | `setup-matt-pocock-skills`（初始化 issue tracker / 术语表布局；支持本地 markdown 模式）、`wizard`（生成交互式 bash 向导） |

> 这 19 个技能保存在 `overrides/skills/`，不进入上游同步层，升级时不会被覆盖。
> 其中 `implement` 的两处交叉引用已适配为本包内的技能名
> （`tdd` → `test-driven-development`，`code-review` → `code-review-and-quality`）。

## 安装到 DSH

在 DSH Skills Manager 的「发现 → GitHub 仓库订阅」中输入本仓库地址即可整仓
扫描并安装。技能目录遵循 `skills/<kebab-case-name>/SKILL.md` 规范，frontmatter
含合法的 ASCII `name` 与 `description`，可直接被 DSH 宿主加载调用。

## 目录结构（三层隔离）

```
mont-forge/
├── skills/          # 唯一内容真源（44 个 SKILL.md，所有平台共享）
├── references/      # 7 个共享清单（被部分技能以 ../../references/ 引用）
├── overrides/       # 你的优化层（同步脚本永不写入，物理隔离）
│   ├── skills/      # 19 个 mattpocock 合并技能（已并入 skills/，此处为来源层）
│   └── patches/     # 放 .patch 增量补丁
├── index.js + cordis.patch.yml + dsh key    # DSH 插件外壳
├── pi key + pi-package keyword              # Pi 插件外壳
├── market/index.json                        # DSH 市场索引（格式 1）
├── .claude-plugin/ + .claude/               # Claude Code 外壳
├── .codex-plugin/                           # Codex 外壳
├── .gemini/ + commands/                     # Gemini 外壳
├── scripts/
│   ├── sync-upstream.ps1   # 一条命令：拉上游 → 重放 skills/references
│   └── build-dist.ps1      # 合并 upstream + overrides → 根级 skills/
├── LICENSE          # 上游 MIT 原文（含 Addy Osmani 署名，合规保留）
├── NOTICE.md        # 来源声明
└── README.md
```

**关键设计**：`upstream` 不在仓库里占一个目录（避免 DSH 扫描到重复的
`SKILL.md`），而是作为 **git remote**（`addyosmani/agent-skills`）存在。
同步脚本 fetch 上游后，把 `skills/` 与 `references/` 检出到根目录。

## 同步与升级

```powershell
# 拉取上游最新，重放到根级 skills/ + references/（只更新上游层，永不碰 overrides/）
.\scripts\sync-upstream.ps1

# 合并 upstream + overrides 生成最终 dist（初期 overrides 为空，等同纯镜像）
.\scripts\build-dist.ps1
```

合并优先级：`overrides/` > `patches/` > `upstream`。
当上游某技能更新、而你也在 `overrides/` 有对应优化时，脚本会打印告警清单，
不静默覆盖，由你决定采纳上游新版、保留优化还是重新合并。

## 许可证

上游内容遵循两个 MIT License：

- [LICENSE](LICENSE) — Copyright (c) 2025 Addy Osmani（`addyosmani/agent-skills`，25 个技能）
- [LICENSE-mattpocock](LICENSE-mattpocock) — Copyright (c) 2026 Matt Pocock（`mattpocock/skills`，19 个技能）

本项目（打包、同步工具、多端外壳、市场索引）由 mont 维护。

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-deepseek-chatframe

给 DeepSeek Harness（DSH）用的聊天气泡皮肤插件：解析 `config.json` + `bubbleframe/*.png` 气泡包，在 DSH 设置页新增「DeepSeek聊天框」，把消息气泡替换成可逐帧动画的气泡框，进行一系列的美化ovo

[![version](https://img.shields.io/badge/version-1.0.0-blue.svg)](package.json)
[![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-BSD--3--Clause-green.svg)](LICENSE)
[![platform](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-DSH%20Desktop-lightgrey.svg)](#兼容性与已知限制)

- 版本：`1.0.4`（构建 `1.0.4`）
- 运行时依赖：**零**（Host 半纯 Node，无需构建）
- 素材：插件不内置气泡，导入自己的气泡包即可

## 预览

[![img](image/1.png)](image/1.png)

[![img](image/2.png)](image/2.png)

[![img](image/3.png)](image/3.png)

## 目录

- [这是什么](#这是什么)
- [功能](#功能)
- [安装](#安装)
- [使用](#使用)
- [兼容性与已知限制](#兼容性与已知限制)
- [开发](#开发)
- [项目结构](#项目结构)
- [常见问题](#常见问题)
- [致谢与许可](#致谢与许可)

## 这是什么

DSH 默认的消息气泡是纯色圆角。本插件把它替换成**气泡包里的九宫格/中缝拉伸图案**，并支持多帧动画、输入框气泡、发送时动画、已读/未读状态与待下达指令镜像。

核心思路：

- 不写死像素：内洞、边框、文字内缩、缩放全部由**当前气泡图案实测** + 元素字号推导，换任何素材都自适应；
- 只使用 DSH 公开的语义 DOM 锚点与状态，不修改官方 React 组件；
- Host 半侧只负责状态、素材扫描与帧下发，浏览器半侧负责绘制与动画；
- 关闭插件时还原官方界面，不残留样式与 DOM。

## 功能

### 气泡装扮

- 左右两侧角色可分别选择气泡（我的消息 / DeepSeek 消息）；
- 支持普通目录、文件夹、`.zip` 等气泡包导入；
- Canvas `auto` 合成：在图案最空的一列/行做九宫格拉伸，保留原图图案；
- 多帧气泡自动播放帧动画，可调动画速度与整体缩放；
- 填充色自动取帧图白底平均色，也可手动覆盖；
- 裁切点 / 锚点 / 帧管理可视化编辑。

### 输入框气泡

- 内置「iMessage输入框」预设；
- 也可选择任意导入气泡作为输入框背景，不覆盖文字、光标与按钮。

### 发送时动画（独立模块）

- 内置 `iMessage 经典发送` / `iOS 26 飞入发送` 等预设；
- 只给发送时出现的那一条消息播放一次，播完立即移除标记；
- 插话 / 插入消息同样播放；
- 关闭「启用聊天气泡皮肤」后仍然生效，不依赖气泡装扮。

### 已读 / 未读

- 消息下方显示已读 / 未读，文字可自定义；
- 对方消息只在**正文**显示，思考 / 工具过程行不显示；
- 待下达指令（排队消息）按「未读」显示，并提供插话发送 / 编辑 / 删除；
- 左侧会话栏显示 `状态 · 会话标题`；
- 状态只存内存，不做持久化；空状态默认「已读」。

### 待下达指令（插话）

- 隐藏 DSH 原生队列 dock，把排队消息画成「DSH 原生已发送消息 + 插件气泡装扮」；
- 插话发送 / 编辑 / 删除复用 DSH 原生按钮；
- 编辑就在原气泡文字位置出现输入框：Enter 保存、Shift+Enter 换行、Esc 取消；
- 多条待下达指令显示一个汇总气泡 + 折叠式抽屉；
- 插话完成（durable steering）后仍与普通消息一样保留气泡。

### 性能

- Host：`state.json` 按 mtime 缓存、气泡清单按目录 mtime + 3s TTL 缓存、帧 PNG / 首帧缩略图按文件 mtime 缓存；
- 浏览器：单全局 `MutationObserver`、`bubbleEls` 集合驱动帧定时器、保存按钮增量脏检查、布局属性按需写入；
- 超极致模式只给当前屏幕上下文套气泡；
- 支持预加载气泡帧、折叠/空闲状态保留气泡。

## 安装

### 前置

- DSH `0.2.0-rc.2`（本插件按该版本的 slot 契约编写）
- **无需构建**：`client.js` 就是发布产物，手写、可读，便于静态审计

### 方式一：插件面板（推荐）

1. 下载 / 克隆本目录到本机任意位置（安装后不要移动或删除）；
2. 打开 DSH Desktop → 设置 → 插件 → 添加插件；
3. 填入本目录的完整路径（不是 `.zip`，也不是 `package.json`）；
4. 勾选信任确认 → 安装 → 启用；
5. 完全退出并重开 DSH Desktop（只关窗口不够）。

### 方式二：命令行（非 desktop profile）

```powershell
dsh plugin --profile web add link:"<本目录的绝对路径>"
dsh --profile web --dump-config
```

确认配置里出现 `dsh-deepseek-chatframe`。

### 验证已生效

重开 DSH 后：

1. 设置 → **DeepSeek聊天框** → 顶部应显示 `版本 v1.0.0 · 引擎 1.0.0+clean.1`；
2. 选择「我发的消息 / DeepSeek 消息」各一个气泡并保存，消息应立刻换肤；
3. 没有气泡素材时，先到设置页导入气泡包。

### 升级与卸载

- 升级：重新指向新目录 / 重装，然后完全退出并重开 DSH Desktop；
- 卸载：插件面板卸载；手工安装的用 `dsh plugin --profile <profile> remove dsh-deepseek-chatframe`。

> 不要直接删除 profile 里的 junction，可能顺着链接删掉插件本体。

## 使用

### 设置页结构

```
启用聊天气泡皮肤
  ├─ 性能模式
  ├─ 替换原来的输入框为气泡
  ├─ 无论状态是否空闲 始终应用气泡
  ├─ 预加载气泡
  ├─ 超极致模式
  ├─ 禁用所有气泡动画
  ├─ 气泡选择
  ├─ 动画预览
  ├─ 外观 → 气泡装扮
  ├─ 外观细节
  └─ 素材

独立功能
  ├─ 外观 → 气泡动画
  └─ 显示聊天风格指令（已读 / 未读）
```

### 素材目录

默认：

```
~/.dsh/deepseek-chatframe/bubbles
```

把气泡包目录或 `.zip` 放进去，或在设置页拖拽导入。

## 开发

包本身零依赖：

```powershell
node --check lib/index.js
node --check lib/client.js
```

- 浏览器半侧是手写的 `window.__ModuleLoader__.load({ ... })` bundle，无构建步骤；
- Host 半侧是 Node ESM，路由前缀 `/dsh-deepseek-chatframe`；
- 修改 Host 后必须完全退出 DSH（托盘右键退出）再启动；
- 离线断言套件在开发仓库的其他目录维护，本发布包不含 `test/`。

## 项目结构

```
dsh-deepseek-chatframe/
├─ lib/
│  ├─ index.js          Host 半侧：状态、素材扫描、帧路由
│  └─ client.js         浏览器半侧：设置面板、气泡绘制、动画
├─ cordis.patch.yml     把本包 insert 进 profile 组合层
├─ package.json         声明 dsh.bundle.patch 与 dsh.client
├─ LICENSE              BSD-3-Clause
└─ README.md
```
## 常见问题

**装完没反应？**
先完全退出并重开 DSH Desktop（不是关窗口）。再检查插件详情页有没有报错行。宿主直接 `JSON.parse` 读 `package.json`，清单损坏会导致整包被丢弃。

**面板显示旧版本 / 改代码不生效？**
DSH 的客户端 bundle 地址带启动时缓存的 `rev`，改客户端后需要**完全退出 DSH 再启动**；只刷新页面可能仍加载旧文件。

**消息没有换肤？**
确认已勾选「启用聊天气泡皮肤」、两个气泡都已选择并保存；没有素材时先在「素材」里导入气泡包。

**待下达指令没有气泡 / 没有动画？**
确认 `userBubble` 已选择；插话消息与普通消息共用同一套气泡与发送动画。

**已读/未读不显示？**
确认勾选「显示聊天风格指令」；对方消息只在正文显示，思考/工具过程行不显示。

**气泡包导入失败？**
确认包内有 `config.json` 与 `bubbleframe/` 目录；本插件不内置素材。

**插件报 `package.json: ENOENT`？**
插件元信息读取时 `package.json` 不存在。确认插件目录里有 `package.json`，并且 profile 里的本地依赖 tgz / link 指向的路径有效；修复后完全重启 DSH。

### 如果有其他异常 欢迎提Issues反馈~

## 致谢与许可

- 气泡包格式与九宫格思路来自聊天气泡包生态；
- [deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) 探索未至之境；

许可：[BSD-3-Clause](LICENSE)。
